articles.o: Four Decades of Rock Legacy Meets Fashion: Blucheez × Warfaze Limited Edition Collection Unveiled
articles.s: A celebration of music, youthful energy, and creative expression. articles.x: A celebration of music, youthful energy, and creative expression. Bangladesh’s iconic rock band Warfaze brings its remarkable musical journey and distinctive cultural identity into fashion through an exclusive collaboration with leading Bangladeshi fashion brand Blucheez. Some songs are not simply heard; they are felt. Some bands do more than perform music; they become part of generations of memories, emotions, and cultural identity. Warfaze is one such name in the history of Bangladeshi rock music. With more than four decades of musical excellence, a distinctive sound, creative evolution, and the unwavering love of countless fans, the band’s remarkable journey now finds a new expression through fashion. Leading Bangladeshi fashion brand Blucheez and legendary rock band Warfaze have jointly introduced the ‘Blucheez × Warfaze Limited Edition Collection’ . The exclusive collection was officially unveiled at a special event held at Blucheez’s Banani outlet in Dhaka. A Special Unveiling with the Presence of Warfaze The event was attended by all seven members of Warfaze: Sheikh Monirul Alam Tipu (Co-founder and Band Leader), Shams Mansoor Ghani, Samir Hafiz, Zaber Ahmed, Palash Noor, Ibrahim Ahmed Kamal, and Soumen Das. The band members personally unveiled the ‘Blucheez × Warfaze Limited Edition Collection’ , making the occasion even more special for fans and invited guests. The gathering was filled with engaging conversations, stories and experiences from the band’s long musical journey, and memorable moments of interaction and photography. Fans had the opportunity to meet their favourite musicians up close, creating an atmosphere of excitement, nostalgia, and celebration throughout the event. The welcome address was delivered by Dr. Mohammad Kamruzzaman, Founder of Bluchee

articles.x: A fabric technology originally developed to reproduce the appearance of woven mattress ticking by British Textile Machinery Association (BTMA) member Monarch Knitting Machinery is finding new applications in apparel, with growing interest from textile manufacturers in Turkey. Monarch’s OD5B-M-7ED44 double-knit circular knitting machine enables the production of fine knitted structures that closely resemble woven textiles while retaining the stretch, comfort and flexibility associated with knitted fabrics. The development is attracting particular interest from Turkish manufacturers producing men’s shirting, where the combination of a refined woven appearance and the production flexibility of circular knitting offers new possibilities for fabric development. Monarch is also exploring mercerisation and pattern printing as additional finishing options for fabrics produced using the technology, potentially extending its appeal to a wider range of apparel applications. articles.x: Airbus Helicopters is evaluating automated composite manufacturing technologies developed by Dutch specialist Airborne as it seeks to increase production efficiency and capacity at its rotor blade manufacturing centre in Paris-Le Bourget, France. Under a new agreement, Airborne will assess the potential integration of its Automated Ply Placement (APP) and Kit by Light (KBL) systems into the facility, which serves as the Airbus Helicopters Centre of Excellence for composite rotor blade engineering, manufacturing and repair. The project forms part of a broader assessment of industrial automation technologies intended to improve material utilisation and production flexibility as Airbus responds to growing international demand for helicopters. Rotor blades pose particular challenges for automated composite manufacturing as a result of their complex geometries and the precise positioning of reinforcement materials required to achieve the necessary structural performance. Airborne’s APP technology is designed to automate the cutting, picking and accurate placement of individual composite plies to create laminates and preforms. Flexibility The software-driven system can handle prepreg, dry fibre and thermoplastic materials, enabling manufacturers to work with different composite constructions without relying on conventional robot programming. This flexibility is particularly relevant to aerospace production, where different components and material configurations may need to be accommodated within the same manufacturing environment. Airborne’s complementary Kit by Light technology addresses an earlier stage of the process by digitising material cutting and kit preparation. articles.x: Lululemon is launching a limited capsule in Australia and New Zealand featuring two core styles made with enzymatically recycled polyester. Developed through its long-term work with Australian-based Samsara Eco, the capsule’s Hotty Hot High-Rise Lined Short 2.5” and Pace Breaker Linerless Short 7” build on earlier products featuring enzymatically recycled polyester. Samsara Eco’s technology uses enzymes to break down plastic and textile waste into molecular building blocks that can be used to make new polyester. In both pairs of shorts, enzymatically recycled polyester makes up at least 50% by weight and is used in the body material. “Advancing circular innovation takes long-term collaboration, testing, and learning across the value chain,” said Yogendra Dandapure, chief materials scientist at lululemon. “Bringing enzymatically recycled polyester into two of our core run styles is another opportunity to learn how new recycling pathways that can use textile waste as an input can be integrated into our products while maintaining the performance and quality our customers expect.” www.lululemon.com The post Lululemon adds Samsara Eco polyester to core styles appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

articles.s: NUREMBERG, Germany — November 24, 2026 — Three halogen-free flame retardants of the GERPHOS® brand have been included in the OEKO-TEX® list of accepted Active Chemical Products (ACP). articles.x: Credit: Gulec Chemicals NUREMBERG, Germany — November 24, 2026 — Three halogen-free flame retardants of the GERPHOS® brand have been included in the OEKO-TEX® list of accepted Active Chemical Products (ACP). The listing covers GERPHOS 8815-10, GERPHOS 8815-16 and GERPHOS 8815-199, manufactured by Gulec Chemicals GmbH of Nuremberg, Germany. The inclusion addresses a conflict that textile finishers have lived with for years. Active chemical products, a group that includes flame retardants, are generally excluded from OEKO-TEX® certified textiles. An exception applies to flame retardants included in the ACP list, a listing that requires an independent toxicological assessment. The three GERPHOS types are listed for all four OEKO-TEX® product classes (I to IV). Articles treated with listed ACPs remain eligible for certification to OEKO-TEX® STANDARD 100, subject to the applicable requirements and assessment of the finished article. “Customers have been putting this question to us for years: fire standard or consumer label,” says Alper Gulec, Managing Director of Gulec Chemicals GmbH. “For three of our types it is no longer an either/or decision.” The three listed types are inorganic, halogen- and antimony-free flame retardants. Developed for demanding polymer and textile applications, they cover PVC, polyurethane, acrylic and unsaturated polyester resin systems and are aimed at textile coating and polymer processing, where fire standards and consumer safety requirements have to be met at the same time. “Progress in our industry is not always visible to the end user,” adds Alper Gulec. “It is often built directly into the materials people rely on every day. articles.o: More Consistent Dyeing: Microwave Measurement Makes Liquor Pick-Up Visible
articles.s: EMPFINGEN, Germany — November 24, 2026 — Consistent shades are essential in continuous textile dyeing. Yet variations in fabric absorbency or uneven padder pressure can go unnoticed until the end of the line. By then, hundreds of metres of fabric may already be affected and may become second-choice
articles.x: EMPFINGEN, Germany — November 24, 2026 — Consistent shades are essential in continuous textile dyeing. Yet variations in fabric absorbency or uneven padder pressure can go unnoticed until the end of the line. By then, hundreds of metres of fabric may already be affected and may become second-choice or rejected. PLEVA’s AF 310 microwave measuring system continuously monitors application moisture immediately after the dye padder, without touching the fabric. Three measuring positions – left, centre and right – reveal variations across the fabric width. The measurement is based on microwave absorption by water in the wet fabric, providing a reliable basis for assessing liquor pick-up and detecting deviations early. In Cold Pad Batch, Pad-Steam and Thermosol processes, real-time monitoring supports uniform application across the width and along the length of the fabric. On suitably equipped padders, the readings can also be used to adjust roller pressure automatically. As a complementary step, the RF 120 microwave system monitors intermediate moisture after the IR pre-dryer – an important parameter for limiting dye migration and maintaining reproducible conditions downstream. Customer applications demonstrate the benefits: At Santista in Argentina as well as Arvind in India, AF 310 supports uniform liquor pick-up in CPB dyeing. Pincroft Dyeing & Printing in the UK uses the inline data to identify irregularities early and reduce rework. More stable dyeing processes mean fewer off-shade batches and less redyeing, helping conserve water, chemicals and energy. PLEVA can also combine its measurement technology with visualisation and process control. More information about sustainable solutions and PLEVA can be found on www.pleva.org Posted: November 24, 2026 Source PLEVA GmbH

articles.x: ORLANDO — November 24, 2026 — Days of education, innovation and excitement buzzed both in the classroom and on the show floor at Advanced Textiles Expo® 2026, the premier show of the textile industry put on by Advanced Textiles Association® (ATA). This year’s event took place Nov. 3-5, at the Orange County Convention Center in Orlando, FL, USA. Co-located for the fifth consecutive year with Sun Shading Expo North America, organized by Messe Stuttgart, the combined events attracted 3,550 participants from around the world. This year’s event also included the return of a successful Hosted Fabricator program, offering exclusive networking and show floor opportunities to 55 fabricators, either attending for the first time or returning after several years. This year’s expo saw new and returning highlights. After Emerging Technologies Conference offered classroom education on the latest textile technology Nov. 2, each morning of the expo included classroom education before the show floor opened. These sessions added more in-depth, focused sessions to the education and hands-on offerings already taking place on the show floor. Some classroom subjects included building resilient workshops, utilizing workspace to maximize productivity, plus interactive demos on subjects like AI, marine fabrication and shade sails. On the show floor, a hands-on learning area became popular, where participants could take part in interactive learning as opposed to listening and taking notes only. articles.x: US advanced materials specialist Carbitex has entered the climbing footwear market with the introduction of its MonoFlex carbon fibre composite technology in the new So iLL Lever climbing shoe. The development extends the application of the company’s patented flexible carbon fibre materials into a demanding new category where precise control of foot movement is essential. Unlike conventional rigid carbon fibre plates, MonoFlex is engineered to flex in one direction while remaining stiff in the other. Integrated into the midsole of the Lever, this directional response is designed to provide support when climbers press against small footholds, while allowing the shoe to conform to uneven surfaces and maintain mobility on steep terrain. The combination is particularly relevant to technical climbing, where footwear must provide sufficient rigidity for sustained edging on narrow footholds without excessively restricting the natural movement of the foot. Developed by specialist climbing footwear company So iLL, based in St Louis, Missouri, the Lever incorporates an aggressively downturned profile intended to concentrate power through the forefoot. Its carbon fibre midsole provides additional arch and midfoot support for controlled footwork on vertical and overhanging climbs. The shoe was designed by Swiss climber Fred Nicole, with development work beginning in May 2022. Technical teams in Switzerland and St Louis subsequently worked with Carbitex from June 2024 to integrate the MonoFlex technology. “Bringing carbon fibre technology into climbing shoes has been a goal of ours for five years,” said Dan Chancellor, founder of So iLL. “Carbitex MonoFlex technology takes Lever’s performance to another level, delivering elite levels of precision and power.” Based in Kennewick, Wash

Monarch’s OD5B-M-7ED44 double-knit machine enables the production of fine knitted stru
articles.x: MANCHESTER, UK — November 23, 2026 — A fabric technology originally developed to reproduce the appearance of woven mattress ticking by BTMA member Monarch Knitting Machinery is finding new applications in apparel. Monarch’s OD5B-M-7ED44 double-knit machine enables the production of fine knitted structures that closely resemble woven textiles while retaining the stretch and comfort associated with knitting. The technology offers a potential alternative to conventional woven fabrics, particularly in applications where appearance and handle must be combined with stretch and ease of movement. The development is now attracting interest from Turkish textile manufacturers, particularly for men’s shirting, where the combination of a refined woven appearance and the production flexibility of circular knitting offers new possibilities. Monarch has also been exploring mercerisation and pattern printing as additional finishing options for fabrics produced on the machine. “This technology has its origins in an unusual coincidence, when two Monarch customers independently approached the company on the same day with an identical request,” explains Kimberley Gent of Monarch’s design department. “They were both looking for a circular knitting machine that could produce a fabric that looked like a woven textile for mattress ticking. “Initially, our engineers doubted whether this would be possible but after studying woven constructions and undertaking extensive trials over several years, they succeeded in developing a knitted structure that reproduced the visual characteristics of woven fabric while maintaining a degree of stretch and comfort.” The resulting Woven Look technology has since been patented in several major markets and is now being used commercially by five European customers

articles.o: Beyond Compliance: What ZDHC MRSL V4.0 means for Bangladesh’s textile, apparel and leather industries
articles.s: Bangladesh's textile, apparel and leather industries are major contributors to the country's economy and global manufacturing supply chains. However, their reliance on chemical-intensive processes, pa...
articles.x: Bangladesh's textile, apparel and leather industries are major contributors to the country's economy and global manufacturing supply chains. However, their reliance on chemical-intensive processes, particularly in dyeing, printing, finishing and leather processing, makes responsible chemical management essential. As international brands increasingly emphasize supply chain transparency, product safety and environmental responsibility, manufacturers must go beyond conventional compliance to strengthen how chemicals are selected, purchased, used and managed. In this context, the release of ZDHC Manufacturing Restricted Substances List (MRSL) Version 4.0 in October 2026 marks an important development for the industry. Building on Version 3.1, the updated standard introduces revised chemical restrictions, formulation limits, testing requirements and supplier guidance. These changes have implications not only for chemical manufacturers and suppliers but also for factories seeking to maintain alignment with evolving brand expectations and sustainability requirements. Figure 1: ZDHC launches MRSL V4.0 For Bangladesh's textile, apparel and leather sectors, understanding MRSL V4.0 is therefore essential for preparing for the transition, managing operational risks and strengthening long-term chemical stewardship. What changes under MRSL V4.0 ZDHC MRSL V4.0 introduces several important changes compared with Version 3.1, including 16 newly added substances, revised formulation limits, updated analytical testing methods and changes to the Candidate and Archive Lists. The Main List now includes dedicated categories for Bisphenols, Aldehydes and Ketones, Polychlorinated Biphenyls (PCBs), and Oxidising and Reducing Agents. articles.x: BALLY, Pa. — November 23, 2026 — Bally Ribbon Mills (BRM), an industry leader in the design, development, and manufacture of highly specialized engineered woven fabrics, highlights its harness webbing for safety applications. BRM’s safety harness webbing and tapes provide fall protection and are appropriate for firefighting and law-enforcement use, as well as fire, industrial, military, and commercial applications. Harness webbing is an essential component in safety equipment designed to help secure and support the wearer in demanding environments. BRM develops woven safety-webbing solutions using nylon, Nomex®, Kevlar®, Vectran®, and other specialty fibers. The selected fiber and fabric construction can be engineered to address the specific performance requirements of a finished harness or related safety component. BRM’s harness webbing can be designed to provide high tenacity, abrasion resistance, flame and heat resistance, controlled elongation, chemical resistance in specific environments, conductivity, dimensional stability, strength, reduced weight and size, and flexibility. These properties are important in safety harness systems intended for fall protection, firefighting equipment, law-enforcement gear, military products, industrial safety equipment, and other commercial safety applications. BRM applies engineered narrow-fabric expertise to maximize end-use performance through fiber orientation and woven construction. BRM’s engineered textiles provide an alternative to conventional materials such as plastic, steel, aluminum, and alloys in specialized product designs. articles.x: The Jamuna Group is one of Bangladesh’s largest industrial conglomerates, with operations spanning diverse sectors including textiles and apparel, media, education, electronics, automotive, chemicals, and real estate. Established in 2005, Jamuna Denims Weaving Ltd is a comprehensive denim manufacturing factory. The company has a daily production capacity exceeding 30,000 units of various denim garment, ranging from basic styles to high-end fashion-forward designs. The facility is equipped with fully automated, ultra-high-speed air-jet looms, producing a wide array of fabrics—including standard denim, canvas, chambray, cross-hatch denim, Oxford-style denim, and Bradford-style denim. By utilizing advanced, modern machinery sourced from the United States, Switzerland, Germany, and Italy, the company ensures high precision throughout its production processes. The facility also incorporates an on-site wastewater treatment plant. Through precise control of yarn tension and accurate stretching techniques, Jamuna produces denim of exceptional quality, suitable for a wide range of applications. In a new collaboration, Jamuna Denims has partnered with Goller to design a versatile denim processing line, scheduled for installation in 2027. This equipment will significantly enhance both the flexibility and the quality of Jamuna’s denim fabrics during the wet-processing and finishing stages. articles.x: Spanish textile recycling specialist Recover has entered into a global partnership with Supima, the organisation representing American-grown Pima cotton, to develop a new range of premium recycled cotton fibres and yarns. The collaboration aims to establish a higher-value market for recycled cotton by recovering waste from Supima cotton products and returning it to the textile supply chain in new yarns and garments. Grown in the western and southwestern United States, Supima cotton is prized for its extra-long staple fibres, which provide exceptional softness, strength and durability. Established in 1954, the Supima organisation now works with more than 1,000 licensees worldwide to protect the identity and authenticity of American Pima cotton. The partnership will combine this established premium positioning with Recover’s mechanical textile recycling technology and international production capabilities. An important aspect of the development is the ability to maintain the identity of the original cotton throughout the recycling process, allowing brands to distinguish the resulting materials from conventional recycled cotton. Both the virgin and recycled fibres will originate from American-grown Supima cotton, with the recycled material digitally traced through the TextileGenesis platform. articles.x: Coats Digital has been named Best Company in AI-Powered Fashion Technology in the 2026 Best in SaaS Awards. The award recognises the company’s application of artificial intelligence to address some of the most pressing challenges facing fashion and apparel manufacturers. Its growing portfolio of AI-powered solutions is helping businesses improve costing accuracy, access specialist manufacturing expertise and turn complex operational data into actionable insights. These innovations include GSDQuest, which brings AI-powered expertise into garment costing, AI Analytics, which enables users to interrogate business data and identify meaningful insights, and GSD RealMotion, which uses AI and computer vision to explore new possibilities in factory-floor method analysis. “Coats Digital is showing what AI can do for the fashion and apparel industry, turning complex production data into faster, smarter decisions for brands and manufacturers,” said Steve Donovan, co-founder of the Best in SaaS Awards.” “Congratulations to our global team on this fantastic achievement,” added Coats Digital MD Himanshu Mehrotra. “AI is opening up significant opportunities for the fashion and apparel industry and we are investing heavily in developing next-generation solutions that turn this potential into practical benefits for manufacturers. We are committed to putting powerful technology and specialist expertise into the hands of the people who can use it to shape a more productive and competitive future for our industry.” Established in 2018, the Best in SaaS Awards celebrates innovation across more than 200 award categories, with winners selected by an independent panel of judges with relevant professional experience. www.bestinsaasawards.com The post Honour for Coats Digital appeared first on I

articles.s: PARIS — November 24, 2026 — EverDye, the French deeptech company specialising in sustainable textile dyeing, has joined the Denim Deal, a global community of companies and innovators committed to accelerating circular denim production. Their initiative brings together brands, manufacturers, mills, r
articles.x: PARIS — November 24, 2026 — EverDye, the French deeptech company specialising in sustainable textile dyeing, has joined the Denim Deal, a global community of companies and innovators committed to accelerating circular denim production. Their initiative brings together brands, manufacturers, mills, recyclers, and technology innovators across the denim supply chain. As the denim sector works to reduce its environmental footprint and increase the use of recycled materials, innovation across the entire production chain is becoming increasingly important. While circularity often starts with the materials used to make a garment, the processes involved in transforming those materials into finished products also play a significant role. Through its membership, EverDye brings a new dimension to the Denim Deal’s mission: tackling the environmental impact of textile dyeing. While the initiative focuses on accelerating circularity through recycled materials, EverDye contributes expertise in transforming one of the most resource-intensive stages of textile manufacturing. Its participation highlights the importance of combining material innovation with cleaner production processes to drive meaningful change across the denim value chain. Bringing a new approach to the denim industry Denim is one of the most resource-intensive segments of the fashion industry. According to the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), producing a single pair of jeans can require between 3,000 and 4,000 litres of water, depending on the manufacturing processes involved. The environmental footprint extends beyond water consumption: cotton cultivation, fabric manufacturing, dyeing, and finishing all contribute to the industry’s greenhouse gas emissions, chemical use, and water pollution. articles.s: At the ITMA NEXT | Industry Networking event on 22 November in Shanghai, CEMATEX unveiled its plan for ITMA ASIA Singapore 2029, marking a new chapter under its sole organisation and management. CEMATEX also highlighted exciting initiatives for ITMA 2027, inviting the global textile and garment tech
articles.x: At the ITMA NEXT | Industry Networking event on 22 November in Shanghai, CEMATEX unveiled its plan for ITMA ASIA Singapore 2029, marking a new chapter under its sole organisation and management. CEMATEX also highlighted exciting initiatives for ITMA 2027, inviting the global textile and garment technology community to convene in Hanover to discover breakthrough innovations, exchange insights and forge partnerships that will shape the future of textiles. Hosted by CEMATEX, the owner of ITMA, the reception welcomed Ms Laura Engel, Deputy Consul General and Head of the Economic Affairs Division, Consulate General of the Federal Republic of Germany in Shanghai, as guest of honour. She was joined by Dr Jorg Weberndorfer, Minister Counsellor, Industrial and SME Policies, Trade & Investment Section, Delegation of the European Union to the People’s Republic of China; Mr Charles Beauduin, Chairman of ITMA Services; Mr Daisuke Murata, President of the Japan Textile Machinery Association; and Ms Jo Yee, Deputy Director, Exhibitions and Conferences, Singapore Tourism Board, together with CEMATEX member associations, industry and media partners, and members of the international textile and machinery community. Opening the event, CEMATEX President, Mr Alex Zucchi reaffirmed ITMA’s pivotal role in advancing the global textile and garment technology industry. For 75 years, ITMA has been recognised as the industry’s Olympics, bringing together the world’s leading innovators and shaping technological progress. He emphasised CEMATEX’s continued commitment to leveraging the ITMA platform to foster industry development by supporting start-ups, research and innovation institutions, as well as meaningful new initiatives led by industry associations and organisations. articles.o: Groz-Beckert brings innovations to INDIA ITME
articles.s: Groz-Beckert will present a wide range of innovations and technological developments at INDIA ITME 2026, taking place from 4-9 December in Greater Noida, India. The company will showcase its latest solutions for knitting, weaving, nonwovens, sewing, tufting and spinning in Hall 14, Booth B6. With a
articles.x: Groz-Beckert will present a wide range of innovations and technological developments at INDIA ITME 2026, taking place from 4-9 December in Greater Noida, India. The company will showcase its latest solutions for knitting, weaving, nonwovens, sewing, tufting and spinning in Hall 14, Booth B6. With a focus on energy efficiency, process reliability, productivity and fabric quality, Groz-Beckert will demonstrate how its precision components and systems can help textile manufacturers address current production challenges. In the knitting sector, the company will highlight developments across circular knitting, flat knitting, legwear and warp knitting, with particular emphasis on reducing energy consumption, improving machine performance and supporting increasingly demanding textile applications. For circular knitting, one of the main attractions will be the next generation of LCmax energy-saving needles. Featuring an innovative wave-shaped shank geometry, the needles are designed to reduce friction and optimise energy efficiency during high-performance knitting operations. When combined with Groz-Beckert’s SNK SF sinker, the technology also helps reduce contamination and extend cleaning intervals, contributing to improved machine availability and production efficiency. The company will additionally present its compound needle technology, developed to support stable knitting processes, high productivity and consistently high fabric quality. In flat knitting, Groz-Beckert will demonstrate specialised needle solutions for technically demanding applications. The SAN TT needle is designed to produce particularly tight loops, making it suitable for technical and medical textiles where precise stitch formation is essential. articles.o: Karl Mayer sets spacer fabric speed record
articles.s: Karl Mayer has introduced what it describes as the fastest seven-bar double needle bar raschel machine on the market, setting a new benchmark for high-speed spacer fabric production. The new RD 7/2-6 MAX is being showcased at a special Product Show hosted by Karl Mayer (China) in Changzhou during th
articles.x: Karl Mayer has introduced what it describes as the fastest seven-bar double needle bar raschel machine on the market, setting a new benchmark for high-speed spacer fabric production. The new RD 7/2-6 MAX is being showcased at a special Product Show hosted by Karl Mayer (China) in Changzhou during this week’s ITMA Asia + CITME 2026. Designed for high-volume manufacturing, the new warp knitting machine achieves a working speed of 1,400 rpm making it more than 30% faster than comparable machines currently available on the market. According to Karl Mayer, the performance improvement offers significant advantages for manufacturers operating in increasingly competitive, price-sensitive markets. The machine has attracted considerable interest from industry professionals attending the Changzhou event, particularly those seeking greater productivity without compromising fabric quality or process reliability. “Visitors in Changzhou are thrilled by the RD 7/2-6 MAX’s tremendous speed and the outstanding engineering behind it. The potential applications for spacer fabrics – especially in high-volume markets – are so diverse that the issue of production efficiency is becoming increasingly important,” said Kay Hilbert, Head of Design Fabrics & Specials at Karl Mayer, on the second day of the event. The RD 7/2-6 MAX has been developed to produce high-performance spacer fabrics for a broad range of end uses, including footwear, sportswear, mattresses and semi-technical textile applications. These three-dimensional knitted structures are particularly valued for their breathability, durability, cushioning properties and structural stability. articles.o: 4 in 10 garments contain elastane, study finds
articles.s: LONDON – Four in ten garments listed on a major US online marketplace contained elastane, according to a study of 1.27 million products. Researchers estimate that removing the stretch fibre where it serves no functional purpose could raise the share of garments meeting recyclers’ fibre requirements
articles.x: LONDON – Four in ten garments listed on a major US online marketplace contained elastane, according to a study of 1.27 million products. Researchers estimate that removing the stretch fibre where it serves no functional purpose could raise the share of garments meeting recyclers’ fibre requirements from 45 to 75 per cent. Writing in Sustainable Production and Consumption, the authors examined the fibre content declared in product listings and compared it with the materials different recycling processes can accept. Only 45 per cent of the garments listed were made from a single fibre. When the researchers applied the specifications of processes able to handle a wider range of blends, 80 per cent of the same sample qualified – a gap of 35 per cent between the two types of process. articles.o: Hyosung and Santoni advance bio-based seamless knitting
articles.s: Hyosung TNC has collaborated with Italian circular knitting machinery specialist Santoni to develop a collection of seamless garments using its new regen BIO Elastane, demonstrating the material’s compatibility with established seamless manufacturing processes. The collection was showcased at the Ve
articles.x: Hyosung TNC has collaborated with Italian circular knitting machinery specialist Santoni to develop a collection of seamless garments using its new regen BIO Elastane, demonstrating the material’s compatibility with established seamless manufacturing processes. The collection was showcased at the Venice Sustainable Fashion Forum (VSFF), held in Venice, Italy, from 5-6 November 2026, where Hyosung participated as a main partner. The collaboration follows the start of commercial production of regen BIO Elastane in Vietnam and represents another step towards wider adoption of bio-based stretch fibres in apparel manufacturing. Developed using Santoni’s advanced seamless knitting technology, the collection demonstrates how bio-based elastane can be incorporated into garments requiring stretch, freedom of movement and targeted support. The partners focused particularly on applications in sportswear and activewear, where seamless construction is increasingly used to combine comfort, functionality and performance. Santoni produced the garments on its SM8-TOP2ST circular knitting machine, which incorporates patented selective terry technology. This enables raised loops to be knitted directly into designated areas of the garment, creating targeted cushioning and three-dimensional textures without the need for additional manufacturing processes. Hyosung’s regen BIO Elastane contains approximately 70% sugarcane-derived renewable feedstock, providing an alternative to conventional fossil-based elastane. According to the company, the material delivers equivalent performance to conventional elastane in terms of elongation, recovery and durability over time. articles.x: Decarbonizing a high-intensity 50 TPD dyeing & knit composite operation alongside 120 garment lines isn’t just an environmental goal it’s a thermodynamic, electrical, and financial engineering challenge. Engr. Mahtab Uddin Ahmed, Deputy General Manager (Maintenance & Utility), HAMS Garments Ltd . In my technical & financial feasibility study, I engineered an integrated, fossil-fuel-free utility architecture built for real-world industrial loads (4.5–5.0 MW daytime garment & composite demand; 3.0–3.5 MW nighttime/base load):Steam & Cogeneration: I sized and modeled 3 × 10 TPH (50 bar) chain-grate biomass boilers feeding a 410V backpressure steam turbine synchronized with an 8.0 MW 33 kV/410V net-metered grid incomer, 4.0 MWp solar PV, and a 3.0 MW / 2-hour BESS (6.0 MWh usable capacity). High-Temperature Thermal Heating: I designed the heating balance for 2 × 6M kcal/hr chain-grate biomass thermo-oil heaters serving stenters, dryer, heat-setting, and tumbler backed by a 4-stage flue gas filtration system (multi-dust collector, cyclone separator, bag filter, and vertical multistage water scrubber) with full auxiliary power accounting. articles.o: Fastsewn opens StitchNCut plant in the USA
articles.s: Danish textile technology specialist Mikkelsen Innovation is expanding into the US with the establishment of a manufacturing and technical support operation in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, as it seeks to accelerate the adoption of its Fastsewn automated sewing and laser cutting technology. The company has
articles.x: Danish textile technology specialist Mikkelsen Innovation is expanding into the US with the establishment of a manufacturing and technical support operation in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, as it seeks to accelerate the adoption of its Fastsewn automated sewing and laser cutting technology. The company has developed its StitchNCut system to address one of the remaining labour-intensive stages of digital textile printing – the conversion of printed fabrics into finished products. While digital printing has transformed the production of textile graphics, the subsequent cutting and sewing operations can still involve considerable manual handling, creating bottlenecks in otherwise increasingly automated production environments. Fastsewn is targeting this gap with technology designed for high-volume finishing applications, including silicone edge graphics (SEG), fabric displays and printed cushion and pillow products. The objective is to enable digital print providers to increase production efficiency and achieve more consistent finishing quality while reducing their dependence on conventional manual operations. Production environment The new US subsidiary, Fastsewn Inc, will be based at the Milwaukee facility of Olympus Group, a specialist in printed graphics and displays and one of the technology’s initial customers. This arrangement will give Fastsewn direct access to a commercial production environment as it develops and introduces its systems to the North American market. Once installed, the StitchNCut equipment at Olympus will also be available for demonstrations, allowing prospective customers to assess the technology under actual manufacturing conditions rather than in a dedicated showroom. articles.o: Uster links contamination control stages
articles.s: Uster Technologies will introduce a new integrated approach to contamination control at India ITME 2026, combining data from raw material selection, fibre cleaning and yarn clearing to help spinning mills improve quality while minimising waste. The Swiss company will also present its latest Vision S
articles.x: Uster Technologies will introduce a new integrated approach to contamination control at India ITME 2026, combining data from raw material selection, fibre cleaning and yarn clearing to help spinning mills improve quality while minimising waste. The Swiss company will also present its latest Vision Shield 3i fibre cleaning system and Uster Trade, a new digital service designed to help spinners demonstrate consistent yarn quality to customers. The new Uster Contamination Control (UCC) solution builds on the company’s established Total Contamination Control concept, extending monitoring and analysis across the spinning process. It connects three existing technologies – Uster FiberQ for raw material management, Vision Shield for fibre cleaning and Uster Quantum yarn clearers – to provide an integrated assessment of contamination from incoming cotton through to finished yarn. By correlating data from these stages, the system can recommend adjustments to cleaning settings and raw material mixes, helping mills achieve the required yarn quality without unnecessarily removing good fibre. UCC extends monitoring and analysis across the spinning process. © Uster The approach also enables spinners to identify contamination problems associated with particular raw material suppliers or bale laydowns, potentially allowing them to address quality issues before processing begins. A central feature of UCC is the new Contamination Body, which classifies contaminants detected during fibre cleaning and helps mills establish appropriate removal limits. Based on a concept already used in Uster’s Yarn Body technology for yarn clearing, it allows operators to assess how changes in cleaning settings will affect both contamination levels and fibre waste. The SAV BESS solution is designed to address these challenges by storing electricity from both rooftop solar generation and the national grid during available supply periods. During grid interruptions, the BESS can automatically and almost instantly supply power to connected factory loads, eliminating the need to start diesel generators for the loads covered by the BESS system. articles.o: Securing Europe’s advanced technical textile capabilities
articles.s: Europe must take urgent collective action to protect its advanced technical textile capabilities in defence, personal protection and aerospace, according to a new strategy published by the SmartX Innovation Hub of the European Technology Platform for the Future of Textiles and Clothing (Textile ETP)
articles.x: Europe must take urgent collective action to protect its advanced technical textile capabilities in defence, personal protection and aerospace, according to a new strategy published by the SmartX Innovation Hub of the European Technology Platform for the Future of Textiles and Clothing (Textile ETP). Presented at an event in Brussels on November 19th, organised jointly with Euratex, SmartX Innovation Strategy for Advanced Technical Textiles was developed between February and October 2026 with input from around 200 experts. It sets out a roadmap to 2035 for securing the materials, manufacturing processes, testing capacity and skills needed to support critical European industries, while accelerating the development of next-generation high-performance textile solutions. The strategy identifies four pressures making action increasingly urgent. These include growing defence and security requirements, following EU defence spending of €418 billion in 2025, despite procurement policies rarely addressing textile inputs further upstream in supply chains. Import dependences The Covid-19 pandemic also exposed Europe’s dependence on imported personal protective equipment (PPE), including masks, gowns and filter media, while the continuing erosion of its industrial base presents a further challenge. EU production of technical and industrial textiles has fallen by 37% since 2000 and the region has been a net importer of technical textiles by volume since 2014. At the same time, major policy and regulatory decisions are approaching, including the proposed Advanced Materials Act, changes to public procurement rules and restrictions on PFAS chemicals. articles.o: RMG sector suffers US$428m production loss in 18 days, US$254m orders shifted abroad: BGMEA
articles.s: Bangladesh’s readymade garment (RMG) sector has suffered production losses worth US$428 million in just 18 days due to ongoing instability and disruptions, while buyers have shifted confirmed orders worth another US$254 million to competing countries, according to a survey by the Bangladesh Garment
articles.x: Bangladesh’s readymade garment (RMG) sector has suffered production losses worth US$428 million in just 18 days due to ongoing instability and disruptions, while buyers have shifted confirmed orders worth another US$254 million to competing countries, according to a survey by the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA). The preliminary survey, conducted among its member factories, found that 317 garment factories had to suspend production from November 1 to 18 due to the unstable situation. The affected factories reported production losses amounting to US$428 million in FOB (Free on Board) value, the BGMEA, said in a press release today. Apart from the direct production losses, garment manufacturers are also facing mounting pressure to meet shipment deadlines, with many export orders now at risk. To retain orders, factories have been forced to resort to costly air shipments, offer substantial price discounts and, in some cases, face outright order cancellations. The survey also revealed that buyers had already shifted 59 million pieces of confirmed garment orders, worth approximately US$254 million, to other countries amid concerns over the prevailing instability. The BGMEA said the survey figures represented only a partial picture of the actual damage, as more than 600 factories had been affected, while only 317 factories could participate in the short-notice survey. It also noted that although the survey covered the period up to November 18, instability in industrial areas was still continuing, suggesting that the overall losses could be significantly higher. articles.o: Moving colour creation from dyeing to weaving
articles.s: A new approach to textile colouration developed by London-based Amphico is moving into commercial production, using computational technology to create thousands of fabric shades from just a handful of pre-coloured yarns, without the need for conventional fabric dyeing. The company’s Amphicolor techn
articles.x: A new approach to textile colouration developed by London-based Amphico is moving into commercial production, using computational technology to create thousands of fabric shades from just a handful of pre-coloured yarns, without the need for conventional fabric dyeing. The company’s Amphicolor technology combines solution-dyed yarns with predictive software to determine how different colours will appear when woven together, allowing manufacturers to achieve specific shades through fabric construction rather than subsequent wet processing. In one recent demonstration, Amphico produced a brown gilet from a lightweight recycled nylon fabric containing no brown yarns whatsoever. Instead, the 40-denier material was woven from black, green and red solution-dyed yarns, with the resulting colour determined by their combination in the finished structure. The principle of optical colour mixing through weaving is well established, but Amphico is seeking to take it into a new era of industrial precision and flexibility. Its software predicts the visual effect of different yarn combinations and generates weaving specifications designed to reproduce target shades. The company says the technology can produce more than 5,000 validated colours from just six base yarn colours, potentially eliminating the need to develop and stock individually dyed yarns for every shade required by customers. This could have significant implications for textile manufacturers faced with increasingly fragmented orders, shorter product development cycles and the need to manage extensive colour inventories. articles.x: Australian sailing apparel specialist Zhik has partnered with US-based eVent Fabrics to incorporate its Direct Diffusion waterproof and breathable membrane technology into the new OFS800 Offshore X range. The partnership marks the first application of eVent fabrics by a sailing apparel brand, extending the technology’s established use in outdoor performance clothing into the demanding marine environment. At the heart of the OFS800 range is a three-layer laminate based on eVent’s alpineST technology, marketed as Direct Diffusion for marine and offshore applications. The fabric offers a hydrostatic head exceeding 20,000mm and a moisture vapour transmission rate of more than 20,000gsm over 24 hours, combining protection against water penetration with the ability to release moisture generated during physical activity. Unlike conventional waterproof membranes that rely on additional coatings or layers to facilitate moisture transfer, eVent’s Direct Diffusion technology allows water vapour to pass directly through the membrane. This is intended to reduce moisture accumulation inside garments during prolonged periods of strenuous activity. “Performance matters most when the conditions are at their worst, and that’s where eVent has always focused,” said Chad Kelly, vice president of eVent Fabrics. “Our Direct Diffusion technology was developed to keep people protected while allowing the body to manage heat and moisture, and offshore sailing puts those same demands on a garment.” The OFS800 Offshore X range has been developed as an integrated clothing system comprising a jacket, smock and salopette, which can be combined according to prevailing conditions. © Zhik In addition to the three-layer laminate, the garments incorporate reinforced Cordura panels in areas subject to abras

articles.s: India's Ministry of Textiles has proposed an investment of ₹16,000 crore ($1.72 billion) over five years under a new National Fibre Scheme (NFS) to strengthen domestic fiber production. This plan is t...
articles.x: India's Ministry of Textiles has proposed an investment of ₹16,000 crore ($1.72 billion) over five years under a new National Fibre Scheme (NFS) to strengthen domestic fiber production. This plan is to reduce import dependence and improve the country's position in the global textile supply chain. Figure: The proposed investment comes as India faces a significant gap between domestic fiber availability and industry requirements. Courtesy: Collected Announced in India's Union Budget for FY2027, the proposed scheme will support the production of natural and emerging industrial fibers. It will cover silk, wool, jute and man-made fibers (MMF), bringing different fiber segments under a broader support framework. The proposal is currently awaiting government approval. According to officials cited by The Economic Times on November 20, financial assistance could range from 25% to 75% of project costs, depending on the type of intervention. Support for farmers, artisans and entrepreneurs is expected to cover around 40% to 50% of unit costs in most cases. These rates remain indicative until final approval. The proposed investment comes as India faces a significant gap between domestic fiber availability and industry requirements. According to Wazir Advisors' 2026 industry report, India imported approximately $2.42 billion worth of staple fibers in FY2024-25. Natural fibers accounted for around 80% of the import value, while man-made staple fibers represented approximately 20%. Cotton was the largest imported fiber category, accounting for 50% of total staple fiber import value. Imports of jute and mesta increased significantly, reaching $366 million in FY2024-25, compared with $149 million in FY2019-20. Viscose staple fiber imports also increased from $112 million to $213 million

MEMPHIS, TENN (October 15, 2026) – The U.S. Cotton Trust Protocol announced th
articles.x: Field-level data show lower greenhouse gas emissions and soil loss, greater soil carbon sequestration, and improved water-use efficiency, as U.S. Regen™ brings measurable, traceable regenerative cotton to brands at scale. MEMPHIS, TENN (October 15, 2026) – The U.S. Cotton Trust Protocol announced the first measured outcomes of U.S. Regen™ Cotton at the Textile Exchange Conference in Vancouver. U.S. Regen™ , introduced in 2025, is grown under the U.S. Cotton Trust Protocol, builds on the program’s established Principles and Criteria, and adds regenerative requirements. Field-level data was collected from 59,094 harvested acres on 469 fields across seven major U.S. cotton-growing states through the Field Partner Program pilot. The findings show that U.S. Regen™ cotton was produced with 20% lower greenhouse gas emissions, 30% greater soil carbon sequestration, 75% lower soil loss, and a 49% improvement in water-use efficiency compared to the established baseline.* “Growers are making long-term investments in the health and productivity of their farms, while also adapting regenerative practices to their unique growing region,” said Marjory Walker, Co-Director of the U.S. Cotton Trust Protocol. “U.S. Regen™ supports those efforts through a consistent framework that measures outcomes, verifies practices, and provides traceability to the bale. We’re pleased to see this program expand from pilot to scaled availability for the 2026 cotton crop.” For brands, U.S. Regen™ provides access to verified, field-level data tied to the cotton they source, rather than relying only on industry averages. The resulting data provides brands with a comprehensive suite of outcome metrics including carbon removals, emissions, soil health, water quality/quantity, and biodiversity. Enrolled fields

articles.x: MBM Group has published its ESG Report 2025, becoming the first company in the woven ready-made garment (RMG) industry to obtain external reasonable assurance on its sustainability reporting. The assurance engagement was conducted by TÜV Rheinland , and reasonable assurance is the highest level of independent assurance available for sustainability disclosures. The ESG Report 2025 is the Group’s second annual sustainability report, covering calendar year 2025 for environmental and social data and fiscal year 2024-25 for financial data. It builds on the inaugural report launched earlier this year, which established the Group’s performance baseline, and takes that baseline to an independently verified standard. The achievement continues a record of leadership that spans more than four decades. Since its founding in 1983, MBM Group has been a pioneer of responsible manufacturing in Bangladesh’s apparel sector. It introduced free meals for its associates in 1988 and commissioned its first effluent treatment plant in 2005. In 2015 it established an on-site washing facility engineered for efficient use of water and energy. This 200+ page report makes 145 disclosures under the GRI Standards and the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) across the Group’s four production entities: Cutting Edge Industries Ltd., Cutting Edge Industries Ltd. Washing Plant, MBM Garments Ltd. and Absolute Quality Wear Ltd. It identifies 13 material topics, each assessed for its impact on people and the environment as well as its financial relevance to the business. The initiative aims to strengthen transparency and ensure that sustainability claims accurately reflect the cotton used in products. For years, the term “sustainable” has been widely used in fashion marketing as a general description covering product origin, environmental performance, and farming practices. Courtesy: Collected However, this broad approach is changing as consumers increasingly demand specific information about where their clothing comes from and how raw materials are produced. At the same time, regulators in major global markets are placing greater emphasis on evidence-based environmental claims. Brands are increasingly expected to support sustainability statements with documented information rather than relying on general marketing language. The U.S. Cotton Trust Protocol offers a structured approach to addressing these challenges through three distinct, traceable fiber categories: Tracked U.S. Cotton, Protocol Cotton and U.S. Regen™ Cotton. Each category provides different sourcing and verification options while maintaining a common foundation of verified U.S. origin, quality and supply chain confidence. articles.x: Norwegian outdoor clothing brand Norrøna has partnered with Australian materials company Uluu to develop a seaweed-based fiber for performance apparel. The project aims to create an alternative to conventional plastic-based synthetic fibers, with the eventual goal of using the material in Norrøna products. Figure: Uluu uses seaweed to produce polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA), a natural polymer that can serve as an alternative to conventional plastics. The partnership focuses on developing a bio-based material that can meet the durability and performance requirements of outdoor clothing while reducing dependence on fossil-based materials. Uluu uses seaweed to produce polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA), a natural polymer that can serve as an alternative to conventional plastics. The production process involves fermenting sugars extracted from seaweed in saltwater to create the material, which can then be processed into fibers. Seaweed offers several potential advantages as a raw material. It can be harvested without agricultural land and requires minimal freshwater and fertilizer. This could reduce pressure on land and freshwater resources compared with some conventional raw materials. The resulting material is designed to biodegrade without releasing persistent plastic fibers into the environment. However, its environmental performance will need to be verified through appropriate testing. Norrøna and Uluu have already spun fibers using seaweed-derived Uluu PHA as a core ingredient. Norrøna will now test the material for durability and other performance requirements before considering its use in commercial products. articles.o: Historic Milestone: Bangladesh crosses 300 LEED-certified green factories
articles.s: Twelve more Bangladeshi apparel, textile, and accessories factories have earned LEED certification from the US Green Building Council (USGBC). Bangladesh now has 302 LEED-certified green factories, more than any other country. Platinum: 134 Gold: 148 Silver: 16 Certified: 4 Bangladesh is also home t
articles.x: Twelve more Bangladeshi apparel, textile, and accessories factories have earned LEED certification from the US Green Building Council (USGBC). Bangladesh now has 302 LEED-certified green factories, more than any other country. Platinum: 134 Gold: 148 Silver: 16 Certified: 4 Bangladesh is also home to 53 of the world’s 100 highest-rated LEED-certified green factories. Newly certified factories: Adzi Trims Ltd., Dhamrai, Dhaka: Platinum, 97 points (LEED BD+C: New Construction v4) D & S Pretty Fashions Ltd., Toke Nagar, Gazipur: Platinum, 91 points (LEED O+M: Existing Buildings v4.1) Probridhi Apparels Ltd., Gazipur: Platinum, 88 points (LEED O+M: Existing Buildings v4.1) FKL Printing Building, Kayempur, Narayanganj: Platinum, 86 points (LEED BD+C: New Construction v4) L Usine Fashion Ltd., Gazipur: Platinum, 85 points (LEED O+M: Existing Buildings v4.1) Visual Eco Stylewear Ltd., Chattogram: Platinum, 84 points (LEED O+M: Existing Buildings v4.1) KDS Apparels Ltd., Textile & Washing, Chattogram: Platinum, 82 points (LEED O+M: Existing Buildings v4.1) Paxar Bangladesh Ltd., DEPZ Old Area, Savar: Platinum, 82 points (LEED BD+C: New Construction v4) Expo Accessories Ltd., Biprabartha, Gazipur: Platinum, 82 points (LEED BD+C: New Construction v4) Barnali Collections Ltd., Knitting Unit, Narayanganj: Gold, 68 points (LEED BD+C: New Construction v4) Bestec BD Ltd., Chattogram: Gold, 66 points (LEED BD+C: New Construction v4) Export Building-2, Mirzapur, Tangail: Gold, 64 points (LEED BD+C: New Construction v4) Of the 12, nine are rated Platinum. Adzi Trims scored the highest, with 97 points. Congratulations to the owners, engineers, and workers of these factories. articles.o: Vice City Blues, Or Why Fashion Still Equivocates When It Comes To Cross-Media Cultural Moments
articles.s: Yesterday saw potentially the biggest launch in the history of entertainment’s biggest medium: Grand Theft Auto 6. But outside of limited licensed collections with Selfridges and Nike, and a few unofficial riffs, the tools brands have to capitalise on moments like these involve advance commitments o
articles.x: Key Takeaways Yesterday’s release of Grand Theft Auto 6, which early data suggests will be the biggest entertainment launch of all time, is a reminder of fashion’s on-again-off-again flirtation with videogame collaborations. Fashion and lifestyle brands have increasingly turned to sports as an avenue for cross-channel visibility (including a just-inked partnership between Nike and F1) and as a way to tap into growing cultural cachet, but the industry has placed comparatively little emphasis on gaming as a route to the same. Concerns remain about the brand-safety of both mature videogame franchises and the less savoury aspects of gaming culture, but a larger challenge is aligning fashion’s forecasts and product development calendars with the unpredictability of gaming release dates, or making calculated bets on stock and replenishment when gaming, at a whole-category level, is a much less sure-fire bet than GTA would suggest. It seems redundant to say it, but videogames are big business. And we mean staggeringly big business. Grand Theft Auto 6 (“GTA6”), which launched yesterday, appears to be comfortably one of the biggest games of all time: Sensor Tower estimates it had shifted close to 25 million copies by the end of launch day, including pre-orders. Videogame launch windows tend to get assessed over an extended-weekend period, so the jury is still out on the official take-off, but for context its predecessor (GTA5) made $1 billion US in its first three days on-sale, securing several Guinness World Records in the process, and with the standard US edition at $79.99 a copy (or licence, more aptly), the newest instalment is already estimated to have generated $2.36 billion in retail sales . articles.o: 섬산련 장학재단, 장학생 25명과 멘토링 학술캠프
articles.s: 한국섬유산업연합회 장학재단(이사장 최병오)이 지난 11월 18일 섬유패션 전공 장학생 25명이 참여한 가운데 ‘2026년도 멘토링 학술캠프’를 진행했다. 장학생들은 글로벌 패션기업 미스토홀딩스와 종합시험인증기관 KOTITI시험연구원을 방문해 패션 비즈니스부터 시험·연구까지 섬유패션 산업의 실무를 살폈다.장학생들은 미스토홀딩스의 사업 소개를 듣고 업무 공간을 둘러봤다. 취업 관련 질의응답을 통해 글로벌 패션기업의 실무와 진로에 대해 알아봤다. KOTITI시험연구원에서는 주요 실험실을 견학하며 시험·인증 업무가 이뤄지는 현장을 살폈다.

articles.t: 알레르망, 첫 전기매트 ‘엘룸’ 출시
articles.o: 알레르망, 첫 전기매트 ‘엘룸’ 출시
articles.s: 침구 전문 브랜드 알레르망이 브랜드 최초의 전기매트 ‘엘룸 알러지케어 워셔블 탄소매트’를 출시했다고 23일 밝혔다.이번 신제품은 알레르망의 침구 소재 기술에 탄소 발열 기능을 접목한 제품이다. 기존 침구 사업을 통해 축적한 알러지케어 원단 기술을 온열 제품으로 확장했다는 점이 특징이다.엘룸은 알레르망의 기능성 소재인 ‘알러지 X-Cover’를 매트 상단뿐 아니라 가장자리 파이핑과 바닥 원단에도 적용했다. 집먼지진드기와 알레르겐의 침투를 차단하고 반려동물의 털이 원단에 박히는 것을 줄이는 데 초점을 맞췄다.사용감과 고정력도 고려했다.

articles.o: 야세, 김보라와 두 번째 협업…11종으로 확대
articles.s: 스텝웨어(STEPWEAR) 브랜드 야세(YASE)가 배우 김보라와 두 번째 협업 컬렉션을 선보인다. 지난 7월 첫 협업에서 선보인 ‘데크 보드슈즈’에 대한 호응을 바탕으로 제품군을 11종으로 확대했다. 컬렉션은 2026년 11월 22일 패션 플랫폼 무신사에서 단독 선발매한다.‘우리는 걸음에 입혀지는 것들을 제작합니다’를 슬로건으로 내건 이번 컬렉션은 빈티지 보드화의 자유로운 실루엣을 바탕으로 기획했다. 기존 데크 보드슈즈에는 차콜 색상을 추가하고, 컬렉션 곳곳에 야세의 시그니처인 ‘O링’ 디테일을 적용했다. 네 가지 방식으로 연출할

articles.o: 손앤박, 다이소·GS25 넘어 노브랜드까지 '유통망 전방위 확장'
articles.s: 다이소에서 치크밤으로 흥행에 성공한 손앤박이 GS25에 이어 노브랜드까지 진출하며 저가 뷰티 시장에서 영역을 넓힌다. 기존 다이소 중심의 판매 구조에서 벗어나 편의점과 대형마트로 유통 채널을 다각화하고, 채널별 전용 상품을 통해 소비자 접점을 확대한다는 전략이다.손앤박은 2027년 국내 중저가 색조 시장을 중심으로 유통망 확대에 나선다. 다이소와 GS25, 노브랜드를 주요 판매 채널로 삼고 각 유통사의 소비자 특성에 맞춘 전용 상품을 선보일 계획이다.손앤박은 다이소에서 거둔 판매 성과를 바탕으로 상품 구성을 재정비하고 있다. 202

articles.s: Achieves the World’s Highest LEED Score of 97 out of 110 in the Packaging, Accessories & Garments Trims Sector Bangladesh has achieved another remarkable milestone on the global industrial stage through Adzi Trims Ltd. The company has earned the internationally recognised LEED Platinum Certification
articles.x: Achieves the World’s Highest LEED Score of 97 out of 110 in the Packaging, Accessories & Garments Trims Sector Bangladesh has achieved another remarkable milestone on the global industrial stage through Adzi Trims Ltd. The company has earned the internationally recognised LEED Platinum Certification, scoring an impressive 97 out of 110 points for its environmentally sustainable industrial facility in the Packaging, Accessories & Garments Trims manufacturing sector. The certification, awarded by the US-based U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC), reflects the company’s outstanding commitment to sustainable industrial development, modern technology, environmental responsibility, and sustainable manufacturing practices. According to the company’s sector-specific global comparison, this achievement of 97 points represents the highest LEED score worldwide in the Packaging, Accessories & Garments Trims manufacturing sector. This is not merely a corporate achievement; it represents an important international recognition of Bangladesh’s growing industrial capabilities, technological excellence, and commitment to environmentally responsible manufacturing. 97 Points — A Global Achievement and a Proud Moment for Bangladesh. articles.s: Groz-Beckert, a global leader in textile manufacturing technology and precision components, continues to support the textile industry through innovative solutions, advanced technologies, and a strong focus on productivity, quality, and sustainability. As a regular participant in ITMA Asia + CITME Sh
articles.x: Groz-Beckert , a global leader in textile manufacturing technology and precision components, continues to support the textile industry through innovative solutions, advanced technologies, and a strong focus on productivity, quality, and sustainability. As a regular participant in ITMA Asia + CITME Shanghai , one of Asia’s leading platforms for textile machinery and technology, the company showcases its latest innovations and engages with industry professionals to address the evolving needs of global textile manufacturers. In this interview, Mr. Markus Settegast, Chief Business Officer (CBO) and Member of the Executive Board of Groz-Beckert , shares his insights on the global textile machinery market, the significance of ITMA Asia + CITME Shanghai, the company’s latest technological innovations, and the long-term opportunities and challenges facing Bangladesh’s textile and apparel industry. He also discusses Groz-Beckert’s strategy for strengthening customer partnerships through digitalization, technical expertise, innovation, and sustainable solutions. Textile Focus: Could you please share with us the current status of the global textile machinery business? The global textile machinery market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 5–6% through 2034. However, the short-term business environment remains challenging. Relatively low order backlogs indicate limited market visibility and continued caution among customers regarding capital investment. Manufacturers are increasingly prioritizing efficiency, cost control, and operational flexibility over large-scale capacity expansion. At the same time, demand is growing for high-performance solutions that enhance productivity, ensure consistent quality, and reduce resource consumption. articles.o: R&G 3rd Eye Partners with Chinese LDC Group to Strengthen Cost Efficiency
articles.s: R&G 3rd Eye Consultancy Ltd., one of Bangladesh’s leading RMG consultancy firms, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with LDC Group, a prominent Chinese business group, to implement internal audit and cost control systems at Liz Fashion Industry Limited and Lida Textile & Dyeing Limited.
articles.x: R&G 3rd Eye Consultancy Ltd., one of Bangladesh’s leading RMG consultancy firms, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with LDC Group, a prominent Chinese business group, to implement internal audit and cost control systems at Liz Fashion Industry Limited and Lida Textile & Dyeing Limited. Under this collaboration, R&G 3rd Eye will work intensively to identify operational inefficiencies, minimize wastage, eliminate unnecessary costs, and strengthen financial and operational controls across both manufacturing units. At a time when Bangladesh’s RMG industry faces rising operational costs and growing competitive pressure, this strategic partnership aims to improve cost efficiency, strengthen operational discipline, and support sustainable industrial transformation. articles.t: Smartex.ai, 지능형 직물 검사 생태계 출시
articles.o: Smartex.ai launches intelligent fabric inspection ecosystem
articles.s: Portuguese textile technology company Smartex.ai has appointed Tony Fadell, who led the teams behind Apple’s iPod and iPhone and founded Nest, as Chairman, alongside the launch of a new AI-powered product ecosystem designed to transform fabric quality control and decision-making across fashion’s sup
articles.x: Portuguese textile technology company Smartex.ai has appointed Tony Fadell, who led the teams behind Apple’s iPod and iPhone and founded Nest, as Chairman, alongside the launch of a new AI-powered product ecosystem designed to transform fabric quality control and decision-making across fashion’s supply chain. The new ecosystem, co-designed with Fadell and developed in collaboration with a strategic supplier to H&M Group, combines advanced inspection hardware with intelligent software to give textile mills, garment manufacturers and fashion brands greater visibility of fabric quality before materials reach the cutting table. Tony Fadell, the new Smartex.ai Chairman. © Smartex.ai The technology will make its industry debut at SmartCollab Hong Kong on 27 November, with private previews taking place from 19 November to 2 December. At the heart of the system is Inspect, a hardware solution using proprietary cameras, sensors and artificial intelligence to capture and analyse every metre of fabric on existing inspection machines. Working alongside it is IQ, a software platform that provides mills, factories and brands with a shared source of fabric quality data. Inspect can identify defects larger than 2mm, record their precise position on a fabric roll and measure colour shade with approximately 0.2 ΔE repeatability. The system enables inspectors to concentrate on flagged issues while automating routine inspection processes. articles.o: CHT Group expands dyes portfolio with new blue and yellow solutions
articles.s: BEMACID Brilliant Blue F-WN and BEZAKTIV Solar Yellow ONE With BEMACID Brilliant Blue F-WN, the CHT Group is expanding its BEMACID F portfolio with a highly brilliant blue dye for polyamide and wool...
articles.x: BEMACID Brilliant Blue F-WN and BEZAKTIV Solar Yellow ONE With BEMACID Brilliant Blue F-WN, the CHT Group is expanding its BEMACID F portfolio with a highly brilliant blue dye for polyamide and wool applications. The dye combines high color brilliance with excellent wet fastness properties, supporting high-quality dyeing results for a wide range of end applications. In addition, BEMACID Brilliant Blue F-WN is metal free and AOX-free, providing important formulation properties for modern textile processing. For dyers and textile manufacturers processing polyamide and wool, color intensity, fastness properties, and process reliability are key factors in the development of competitive textile products. With BEMACID Brilliant Blue F-WN, the CHT Group is adding another versatile blue component to its dyes portfolio. BEZAKTIV Solar Yellow ONE for flexible dyeing processes With BEZAKTIV Solar Yellow ONE, the CHT Group is enhancing its high-performance reactive dyes portfolio with a lightfast, non-photochromic golden yellow dye. It enables reliable and uniform dyeing results across a broad range of color depths, from light to darker shades. BEZAKTIV Solar Yellow ONE also offers very good wash-off properties and is suitable for both exhaust dyeing and continuous dyeing processes. The dye can also be effectively used in trichromatic dyeing in combination with BEZAKTIV Coral Red ONE and BEZAKTIV Aquamarine ONE . It thus supports flexible shade development while meeting high-performance requirements. For textile manufacturers, color consistency and process efficiency are key factors. With BEZAKTIV Solar Yellow ONE, the CHT Group is adding another component for sophisticated yellow shades to its dyes portfolio while providing the application flexibility required by modern dyehouses.

articles.x: Techtextil North America is inviting visitors, exhibitors and industry experts to participate in its 2027 edition, taking place from 11–13 May at the Georgia World Congress Center in Atlanta, Georgia. Co-located with Texprocess Americas, the event will bring together manufacturers, suppliers, researchers and technology specialists from across the technical textiles and nonwovens industries. With material performance expectations rising, product development cycles shortening and manufacturers facing increasing pressure on quality, functionality and costs, the exhibition will provide a platform for exploring new technologies, evaluating sourcing opportunities and addressing the challenges facing the sector. Registration is now open for visitors seeking to discover new materials, assess technical capabilities and establish relationships with potential suppliers. Organisers say the exhibition will offer opportunities to examine products first-hand, discuss specific application requirements and identify solutions that may not be apparent through conventional sourcing channels. The event will cover a broad range of technical textile applications, bringing together companies involved in fibres, yarns, fabrics, nonwovens, textile machinery, processing technologies and advanced materials. For manufacturers and product developers, the emphasis will be on identifying commercially viable solutions that meet increasingly demanding performance specifications. Exhibition space also remains available for companies seeking to present their technologies and expertise to an international audience of sourcing professionals, product developers, engineers and purchasing decision-makers. articles.o: Only three of 13 textile recycling methods attract commercial loans
articles.s: Global textile recycling faces a major financial bottleneck as commercial funding lags behind proven technology. According to the Systemic Bankability of Textile-to-Textile Recycling report released b...
articles.x: Global textile recycling faces a major financial bottleneck as commercial funding lags behind proven technology. According to the Systemic Bankability of Textile-to-Textile Recycling report released by Accelerating Circularity in October 2026, circular fiber systems remain stuck in a financial missing middle. While pilot plants confirm that textile waste can become new raw materials, mainstream banks refuse to fund full commercial facilities through standard project finance. Figure: Across Europe, only 23% of separately collected post-consumer textiles are suitable for any textile-to-textile recycling process.Courtesy: Collected Authored by Olga Melekhina, Responsible Leadership Fellow at Accelerating Circularity and supported by ESMT Berlin, the study scores 13 textile recycling pathways across 12 financial risk factors. The results highlight a clear gap for global apparel supply chains. As recycling methods advance toward turning complex, blended post-consumer garments into virgin-quality fibers, securing bank loans becomes significantly harder. Currently, only three of the 13 evaluated pathways qualify for standard commercial funding. These include mechanical recycling for post-industrial waste, mechanical recycling for post-consumer waste, and industrial polyamide depolymerization. Mechanical recycling remains the sole bankable route for post-consumer garments, yet it can process at most 6.6% of collected textile waste. Across Europe, only 23% of separately collected post-consumer textiles are suitable for any textile-to-textile recycling process. Four commercial barriers block project finance for the remaining 10 pathways. articles.o: Karl Mayer’s comprehensive approach to textile production
articles.s: Karl Mayer will present new tricot machine technologies and a broader approach to textile production at this week’s ITMA Asia + CITME 2026 in Shanghai, highlighting developments designed to address changing customer requirements for productivity, flexibility, fabric quality and investment costs. The
articles.x: Karl Mayer will present new tricot machine technologies and a broader approach to textile production at this week’s ITMA Asia + CITME 2026 in Shanghai, highlighting developments designed to address changing customer requirements for productivity, flexibility, fabric quality and investment costs. The German textile machinery manufacturer is placing particular emphasis on opportunities in sportswear, athleisurewear and casual fashion, where demand for comfortable, functional and versatile fabrics continues to grow. In an interview ahead of the exhibition, Michael Ahrendt, Global Head of Performance Fabrics at Karl Mayer, outlined the company’s latest innovations and explained how its expanding portfolio is being tailored to different market segments. According to Ahrendt, warp knitted fabrics are increasingly finding applications beyond traditional sportswear, with their inherent breathability, crease resistance and freedom of movement making them attractive for everyday clothing. “We are seeing sustained high demand for apparel that combines a trendy look with comfort and functionality,” he said. “Sportswear and athleisurewear are experiencing dynamic growth and are increasingly bringing their comfortable, high-performance fabric concepts into fashion and everyday wear.” Karl Mayer is responding with developments targeting three key trends: Smart Casual, WovenLike Warp Knit and Lightweight Outdoor. These applications will be supported by new machinery designed to combine high productivity with greater flexibility and improved fabric quality. Among the highlights in Shanghai will be the HKS 2-SE in E40 gauge, featuring a working width of 312 inches. articles.o: Space Dyeing, Fiber Dyeing, and Beyond: The Exclusive Technologies Behind Akij Textile Mills Ltd
articles.s: From a spinning floor of more than 51,000 spindles to Italian package-dyeing vessels and a finishing line built for yarn-dyed woven cloth, Akij Textile Mills Ltd. in Manikganj is betting that the future of Bangladeshi wovens lies in controlling color at the earliest possible stage. We look at space
articles.x: From a spinning floor of more than 51,000 spindles to Italian package-dyeing vessels and a finishing line built for yarn-dyed woven cloth, Akij Textile Mills Ltd. in Manikganj is betting that the future of Bangladeshi wovens lies in controlling color at the earliest possible stage. We look at space dyeing, fiber dyeing, and the other firsts that set the mill apart. The Mill That Starts with the Fiber Most woven fabric buyers think of color as something that happens late, in a dye house or on a printing table. Akij Textile Mills Ltd. (ATML) argues the opposite. A concern of the Akij Group, the mill at Golora, Charkhanda, Manikganj presents itself as a single-source supplier from yarn to finished woven fabric, serving the export-oriented ready-made garment sector. The scale behind that claim is considerable. According to the company, the mill runs 51,328 spindles, produces about 40,000 kg of yarn a day and employs around 1,600 people. The spinning division began the story: the company says it has well over a decade and a half of spinning experience, and from that base it moved upstream into yarn dyeing, weaving, and fabric dyeing and finishing. That sequence matters. A mill that spins its own yarn knows its cotton, its twist, and its count variation intimately, and those are exactly the variables that decide whether a dyed yarn looks right in the final cloth. It is also why conversations about space dyeing and fiber dyeing at ATML begin on the spinning floor, not in the dye house. Space Dyeing: Color That Moves Along the Yarn Space dyeing is a method in which a single yarn is colored in several shades at intervals along its length, rather than in one uniform color.
