articles.s: Bangladesh remained the European Union’s largest denim supplier in January–September 2026, but its exports fell faster than the market, according to Eurostat data. EU denim imports fell 3.24% year on year to €3.42 billion. Imports from Bangladesh fell 5.48% to €1.01 billion, and its market share sli
articles.x: Bangladesh remained the European Union’s largest denim supplier in January–September 2026, but its exports fell faster than the market, according to Eurostat data. EU denim imports fell 3.24% year on year to €3.42 billion. Imports from Bangladesh fell 5.48% to €1.01 billion, and its market share slipped to 29.48% from 30.18%. The market returned to growth in August (+11.91%) and September (+3.66%). Bangladesh grew only 0.70% in September, to €143.12 million. Pakistan, the second-largest supplier, fell 6.63% to €609.70 million, giving it a share of 17.85%. Turkey fell 20.27% to €498.10 million, and its share dropped to 14.58% from 17.70%. Egypt rose 34.97% to €225.76 million, a gain of €58.49 million that almost matches Bangladesh’s €58.35 million loss. China grew 20.23% to €230.54 million. According to BAV’s analysis, Bangladesh is not picking up the share that Turkey and Pakistan are losing. Egypt and China are taking much of it. Source: Eurostat, compiled by Bangladesh Apparel Voice (BAV). The post Bangladesh keeps top spot in EU denim market but loses share as Egypt, China gain appeared first on Textile Focus .

articles.s: 국내 패션 유통시장의 경쟁 구도가 전문 플랫폼의 시장 지배력 확대와 글로벌 SPA 브랜드의 성장, 소비자 세분화를 중심으로 재편되고 있다. 무신사·29CM가 결제금액 기준 선두를 유지하는 가운데 유니클로는 폭넓은 연령층을 기반으로 추격하고 있으며, 크림·지그재그·에이블리 등 특화 플랫폼도 주요 소비 채널로 자리 잡았다. 특히 젊은 소비자는 온라인 패션 플랫폼, 중장년층은 SPA 및 전통 패션기업 유통망에 상대적으로 높은 지출 비중을 보이면서 고객층별 경쟁 전략의 중요성이 커지고 있다.와이즈앱·리테일이 발표한 자료에 따르면 2026년

articles.t: 아이더 ‘그래티넘 라이트 다운’, 10월 판매량 3배 껑충
articles.o: 아이더 ‘그래티넘 라이트 다운’, 10월 판매량 3배 껑충
articles.s: 아웃도어 브랜드 '아이더'의 ‘그래티넘 라이트 다운’이 10월 판매량이 전월 대비 약 3배 증가하며 가을·겨울 시즌 판매 호조를 이어가고 있다.인기 컬러인 라이트 그레이는 초도 물량이 완판돼 리오더에 들어갔으며, 일부 매장에서는 예약판매까지 이어지고 있다.그래티넘 라이트 다운은 지난 8월 28일 얼리버드 프로모션을 시작으로 9월부터 판매가 늘었다. 10월에는 한 달 판매량이 9월 대비 약 3배 증가하며 아이더의 가을·겨울 주력 다운으로 자리 잡고 있다.컬러별 판매 성과가 두드러진다. 특히 라이트 그레이는 지난 9월 말 판매율 50%

articles.s: 제40회 섬유의 날에서 금탑산업훈장을 수상한 세왕섬유 최재락 회장의 소식이 미국 섬유산업 뉴스 플랫폼 ‘Textile Industry Today’에 소개됐다.미국 EIN News가 운영하는 Textile Industry Today는 지난 11일 서울경제신문 영문판이 보도한 ‘한국, 섬유산업 유공자 77명 포상(Korea Honors 77 for Contribu-tions to Textile Industry)’ 기사를 섬유산업 뉴스 목록에 게재했다.해당 기사에는 최 회장의 사진과 함께 금탑산업훈장 수상 사실과 주요 공적이 소개됐다.

articles.t: 美 연말 소비, 성장 속 가성비 경쟁 심화
articles.o: 美 연말 소비, 성장 속 가성비 경쟁 심화
articles.s: 미국 연말 소매시장이 물가 상승과 가계 재정 부담에도 불구하고 성장세를 이어갈 전망이다. 미국소매협회(NRF)는 올해 11~12월 소매판매액이 전년보다 4.2% 증가한 1조130억 달러에 이를 것으로 전망했다. 이는 지난해 증가율 3.1%를 웃도는 수준으로, 자동차와 주유소, 음식점 매출은 집계에서 제외됐다.그러나 소비자들의 구매 방식에는 뚜렷한 변화가 나타나고 있다. 소비자들이 상품 구매에 더욱 신중해지면서 가격과 할인 혜택이 구매를 결정하는 주요 변수로 떠오르고 있다.NRF 조사에서 연말 쇼핑객의 56%는 경제 상황이 소비 계획

articles.o: 부산섬유패션(연) 창립 30주년 기념식
articles.s: 부산섬유패션산업연합회(회장 이성근)가 오는 25일 창립 30주년을 맞아 롯데호텔부산 크리스탈볼룸에서 성대한 기념행사를 갖는다.“30년의 동행, 부산섬유산업의 미래를 열다” 주제로 1부 ‘산업용 섬유 얼라이언스 기술 교류회’에 이어 2부 30주년 기념행사 순으로 진행된다.부산섬유패션산업연합회와 한국섬유산업연합회가 공동 주관하는 30주년 기념행사는 서울과 부울경 섬유패션업계 대표와 단체 연구소 관계자 다수가 참가한 가운데 다채롭게 진행된다.이 30주년 기념행사는 롯데호텔부산 크리스탈볼룸에서 오후 4시부터 8시까지 만찬을 겸해 진행된다.

articles.t: 낫포너드, 고딕 무드 담은 더현대 서울 팝업
articles.o: 낫포너드, 고딕 무드 담은 더현대 서울 팝업
articles.s: 낫포너드(NOT4NERD, 대표 김준성)가 11월 19일부터 25일까지 일주일간 더현대 서울 지하 2층 아이코닉 존에서 시즌 팝업스토어를 운영한다. 2026 가을·겨울(FW) 컬렉션 ‘애프터 어웨어(AFTER AWARE)’와 인플루언서 정보배, PINN예진이 참여한 협업 캡슐 컬렉션을 선보인다.낫포너드는 정형화된 틀에서 벗어나 자유로움과 개성을 디자인으로 표현해 온 브랜드다. 이번 팝업은 빈티지 워싱과 디스트레스 디테일, 개성 있는 실루엣을 적용한 시즌 의류를 중심으로 모자와 가방 등 잡화, 브랜드 시그니처 제품을 함께 구성했다.공

articles.o: Fabric waste is an information problem says Smartex.ai
articles.s: Portuguese textile technology company Smartex.ai will debut its integrated fabric inspection and quality management platform at SmartCollab taking place at the DX Design Hub in Hong Kong on November 27th, followed by private demonstrations to companies in the region. Designed to give mills, garment
articles.x: Portuguese textile technology company Smartex.ai will debut its integrated fabric inspection and quality management platform at SmartCollab taking place at the DX Design Hub in Hong Kong on November 27th, followed by private demonstrations to companies in the region. Designed to give mills, garment manufacturers and brands access to reliable fabric quality data throughout the supply chain, the platform was developed in collaboration with a strategic supplier to H&M Group. It combines artificial intelligence, machine vision and centralised quality management software to identify defects during fabric production and make the resulting information available before material reaches garment factories. The company believes this could significantly reduce the precautionary fabric purchases, repeated inspections and quality disputes that continue to generate unnecessary costs throughout the apparel industry. Headquartered in Porto, Smartex.ai has spent eight years developing its own machine vision technology and already has more than 800 systems installed in ten countries. Its AI models have been trained on some 50 billion images of actual fabrics captured on operating production lines. Integrated elements The new platform consists of two integrated elements – Inspect, a hardware system that can be fitted to existing fabric inspection machines, and IQ, software that makes the resulting quality data accessible to mills, garment factories and brands. Inspect uses cameras, sensors and AI to examine fabric continuously, identifying defects larger than 2mm and recording their precise positions along each roll. articles.x: Gerrerd Taylor serves as Regional Senior Sales Manager, Product Group Spinning Components Division at Groz-Beckert East Asia LLP, bringing extensive experience in sales leadership, business development, and customer relationship management across the textile industry. India International Textile Machinery Exhibitions Society, popularly known as India ITME Society will host 12th edition
articles.x: The six-day exhibition, scheduled from 4–9 December, will feature over 1,000 exhibitors from 91 countries across 20 chapters and is expected to attract more than 1.5 lakh visitors. India International Textile Machinery Exhibitions Society, popularly known as India ITME Society will host 12th edition of India International Textile Machinery Exhibition (India ITME 2026) from 4 to 9 December 2026 at India Exposition Mart Limited (IEML), Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh. The exhibition will bring together textile machinery manufacturers, technology providers and industry stakeholders from India and overseas to discuss developments in the sector, explore new technologies and build business connections. India’s ₹44.45 billion PM-MITRA scheme is expected to catalyse significant textile investments, projected to drive ₹700 billion in industry growth and create 2 million new jobs . PLI incentives, ZLD compliance mandates and rising demand for smart manufacturing make this a pivotal moment for the sector’s growth and transformation. India ITME 2026 will host Textile Horizons on 5 and 6 December, alongside one of the world’s largest textile machinery exhibitions. articles.x: At ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026 in Shanghai, Saurer will demonstrate how its advanced technologies enable maximum flexibility across the entire spinning process, from bale to yarn and twisting. Visitors to hall 6.1, booth A58, can explore solutions designed to optimise production, improve efficiency and help mills respond quickly to changing market demands. Saurer’s experts will be available to discuss individual production challenges and tailored solutions. All machines follow Saurer’s E³ concept, focusing on energy efficiency, economics and ergonomics while processing a broad range of fibres, including cotton, wool, synthetic, technical, recycled and regenerated materials. Innovations from pre-spinning with process optimisation Saurer will present the Autocard SC8s with Autocoil 6, a high-performance carding and drawing solution designed to improve fiber utilization and reduce energy consumption. Suitable for cotton, synthetic fibers, viscose and recycled materials, the Autocard SC8s feature an advanced large-cylinder design, digital machine settings and automated control systems, including online waste detection and automatic flat adjustment, ensuring excellent sliver quality and operational flexibility. Equipped with the integrated PDS pre-draft leveling module, the Autocoil 6 delivers highly even slivers and, depending on yarn requirements, can eliminate one drawing passage before rotor spinning, reducing floor space and investment costs. Maximum flexibility with rotor- and air-spinning Making its debut at the exhibition, the new BD 8 SE expands Saurer’s semi-automatic rotor spinning portfolio. articles.x: Fourteen Bangladeshi companies are participating in the three-day Global Sourcing Expo in Melbourne, Australia, aiming to expand export opportunities, attract international buyers, and strengthen Bangladesh’s position in the global apparel market. The exhibition, which began today and will continue until November 19, has brought together more than 900 exhibitors from 20 countries, according to a press release received here. Nine Bangladeshi readymade garment companies are participating under arrangements made by the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) and the Bangladesh High Commission in Australia, while five others have joined independently. A total of 23 representatives from the participating companies are attending the international trade exhibition. Bangladesh High Commissioner to Australia F M Borhan Uddin inaugurated the Bangladesh Pavilion, showcasing the country’s export products. Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Commerce Tanvir Ahmed, EPB Secretary Md Bazlur Rashid, Commercial Counsellor Rony Chakma and Julie Holt, director of the organising company, were present. The Global Sourcing Expo is regarded as Australia’s premier international sourcing exhibition, providing a platform for manufacturers, suppliers and sourcing professionals to explore business opportunities and establish commercial partnerships. The exhibition features products from various sectors, including readymade garments, footwear, fashion accessories, textiles and homeware. A special seminar focusing on Bangladesh’s readymade garment industry is scheduled for the opening day to highlight the country’s manufacturing capabilities, production expertise and export potential. articles.o: AI set to take control of warehousing by 2028
articles.s: More than half of organisations expect artificial intelligence (AI) to make or execute over a quarter of their operational warehouse decisions autonomously by 2028, according to a new study by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and Spanish warehouse technology specialist Mecalux. The gl
articles.x: More than half of organisations expect artificial intelligence (AI) to make or execute over a quarter of their operational warehouse decisions autonomously by 2028, according to a new study by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and Spanish warehouse technology specialist Mecalux. The global study, involving 1,967 supply chain and warehousing professionals across 21 countries, also found that 90% of organisations expect to increase their investment in AI over the next two to three years. Conducted by the Intelligent Logistics Systems Lab at the MIT Center for Transportation & Logistics (CTL) in collaboration with Mecalux, the research examines the adoption of generative and agentic AI in warehouse operations, the benefits being achieved and the challenges of introducing greater autonomy. Adoption is already widespread, with 61% of organisations reporting large-scale deployment or full integration of generative AI (GenAI), compared with 56% for agentic AI, which can independently carry out tasks and make decisions within defined parameters. Most implementations remain relatively new, however, with around three-quarters having been at their current stage of deployment for less than a year. The findings suggest that AI is already delivering operational benefits, although relatively few organisations have comprehensively documented the results. Among the applications examined in detail, 87% of GenAI and 81% of agentic AI use cases were reported to have achieved at least moderate improvements in their target performance indicators. However, significant improvements had been quantified and documented in only 39% and 36% of cases respectively. articles.s: Saurer will demonstrate how its advanced technologies enable maximum flexibility across the entire spinning process, from bale to yarn and twisting. Visitors to hall 6.1, booth A58, can explore solut...
articles.x: Saurer will demonstrate how its advanced technologies enable maximum flexibility across the entire spinning process, from bale to yarn and twisting. Visitors to hall 6.1, booth A58, can explore solutions designed to optimize production, improve efficiency and help mills respond quickly to changing market demands. Saurer's experts will be available to discuss individual production challenges and tailored solutions. All machines follow Saurer's E³ concept, focusing on energy efficiency, economics and ergonomics while processing a broad range of fibres, including cotton, wool, synthetic, technical, recycled and regenerated materials. Figure 1: Belcoro and Belleo rotors – Quality crafted by Saurer. Innovations from pre-spinning with process optimization Saurer will present the Autocard SC8s with Autocoil 6, a high-performance carding and drawing solution designed to improve fiber utilization and reduce energy consumption. Suitable for cotton, synthetic fibers, viscose and recycled materials, the Autocard SC8s features an advanced large-cylinder design, digital machine settings and automated control systems, including online waste detection and automatic flat adjustment, ensuring excellent sliver quality and operational flexibility. Equipped with the integrated PDS pre-draft levelling module, the Autocoil 6 delivers highly even slivers and, depending on yarn requirements, can eliminate one drawing passage before rotor spinning, reducing floor space and investment costs. Maximum flexibility with rotor- and air-spinning Making its debut at the exhibition, the new BD 8 SE expands Saurer's semi-automatic rotor spinning portfolio. articles.t: ANDRITZ, 지속 가능한 포장을 위한 셀룰로오스 기반 경로 선보일 예정
articles.o: ANDRITZ to showcases cellulose-based pathways to sustainable packaging
articles.s: ANDRITZ will host the Sustainable Packaging Days 2027 on March 18–19, 2027, at the ANDRITZ France facility in Montbonnot, France. The event will bring together brand owners, converters, packaging prod...
articles.x: ANDRITZ will host the Sustainable Packaging Days 2027 on March 18–19, 2027, at the ANDRITZ France facility in Montbonnot, France. The event will bring together brand owners, converters, packaging producers, researchers, and technology providers to explore how renewable fibers and advanced production technologies can drive the transition away from fossil-based packaging materials. The transition toward more sustainable products and packaging is gaining momentum worldwide, driven by ambitious sustainability goals, new regulations and growing demand for renewable and circular solutions. In the EU, for example, all packaging must be recyclable by 2030, while global initiatives are pushing for greater reuse, recycling and alternatives to fossil-based plastics. Cellulose can play an important role in this transition, offering renewable and recyclable opportunities across packaging, nonwovens and textiles. Collaboration across the entire ecosystem is key to driving this development forward. The Cellulose Valley Chair gathering in Grenoble in October is one recent example of how industry, academia and research are connecting around cellulose-based innovation. For ANDRITZ, cellulose is more than a raw material. It is the common thread connecting expertise across pulp production, nonwovens, textiles, and packaging. From fiber processing technologies to innovative molded fiber applications, cellulosic fibers create opportunities to replace fossil-based materials with renewable and recyclable alternatives. This supports the company’s broader sustainability ambition: by 2030, more than 50% of total revenue is targeted to come from environmental impact solutions. The new Uster Contamination Control solution and latest Uster Vision Shield 3i put spinners in command of contaminant removal, ensuring yarn quality, minimizing waste and protecting profits. These exciting developments – and even more news – will be featured at India ITME 2026. Uster Vision Shield 3i – intelligent fiber cleaning The major gathering of the Asian textile industry in 2026, at India ITME, taking place from December 4 to 9 at IEML, Greater Noida, UP, offers Uster a great opportunity to present its latest innovations: Uster Contamination Control, Uster Vision Shield 3i and Uster Trade. Starting with raw material The new Uster Contamination Control concept unites a range of valuable services for spinners in a holistic approach that combines data from the incoming raw material, the fiber cleaning system and the yarn clearers. It’s a next-level evolution of the well-proven Total Contamination Control (TCC). It’s a comprehensive approach for consistent contamination control and optimized spinning performance – from raw material to yarn. articles.o: Cloud Sound explores acoustic knitting
articles.s: Dutch textile design and research studio Studio Eva de Laat is exploring the potential of seamless knitting technology to create three-dimensional acoustic surfaces that combine sound absorption with expressive textile design. Cloud Sound, the fifth edition of the studio’s ongoing Studio Work resear
articles.x: Dutch textile design and research studio Studio Eva de Laat is exploring the potential of seamless knitting technology to create three-dimensional acoustic surfaces that combine sound absorption with expressive textile design. Cloud Sound, the fifth edition of the studio’s ongoing Studio Work research series, investigates how engineered knitted structures, fibre selection and textile construction could contribute to acoustic comfort and the sensory qualities of interior spaces. The project examines how variations in stitch density, thickness, texture and volume might influence the way knitted surfaces interact with reflected sound, potentially reducing reverberation in offices, public spaces and residential interiors. © Studio Eva de Laat Central to the research is the ability of seamless knitting technology to engineer different structural properties within a single textile construction. Variable stitch densities, layered surfaces, spacer structures and integrated cavities offer possibilities for developing three-dimensional acoustic panels. These structures could be combined with porous fillings and carefully designed air gaps to enhance sound absorption. Techniques including floats, raised textures and quilted constructions introduce additional volume and surface relief, allowing acoustic functionality and visual expression to be developed together. By controlling construction at stitch level, the studio is investigating how knitted textiles themselves could contribute to acoustic performance, rather than simply acting as decorative coverings for conventional sound-absorbing materials. © Studio Eva de Laat Fibre and yarn selection is another important consideration. articles.t: YKK는 겸손한 지퍼를 움직입니다.
articles.o: YKK sets the humble zip in motion
articles.s: The zip may be one of the most taken for granted components in textile manufacturing, but Japan’s YKK is demonstrating how a motorised version could open up new possibilities for assembling large fabric structures. Its Zippilot self-propelled zipper, which will be demonstrated at international consu
articles.x: The zip may be one of the most taken for granted components in textile manufacturing, but Japan’s YKK is demonstrating how a motorised version could open up new possibilities for assembling large fabric structures. Its Zippilot self-propelled zipper, which will be demonstrated at international consumer electronics exhibition CES 2027 in Las Vegas from January 6 th -9th, replaces the conventional hand-operated slider with a motorised mechanism that can travel along a fastening system to open or close it. While the prospect of a jacket that zips itself up might initially spring to mind, the technology’s more immediate potential lies in industrial textiles, particularly temporary shelters and architectural membranes that are difficult to assemble manually. The concept has already been tested in Japan in collaboration with Taiyo Kogyo, a specialist in membrane structures, with encouraging results. In one demonstration, Zippilot was used to join a five-metre-high membrane structure in approximately 40 seconds. In another, two temporary shelters were connected in around 50 seconds, including a roof section that would otherwise have been difficult for workers to reach from the ground. The trials illustrate how a relatively simple change to a familiar fastening system could offer significant practical advantages. Large textile structures often require workers to access elevated or awkwardly positioned seams, with the associated need for ladders, platforms or other access equipment. By allowing a slider to travel along the fastening system without being pulled manually, Zippilot could reduce the amount of work required at height while making the assembly and dismantling of temporary structures quicker and more straightforward. © YKK Potential applications could extend to exhibit

articles.t: 글로벌 품질 컨벤션 ICQCC 2026 다카에서 개최
articles.o: Global Quality Convention ICQCC 2026 Opens in Dhaka
articles.s: 8,000 Quality Professionals and 800 QCC Teams from 16 Countries Take Part The 51st International Convention on Quality Control Circles (ICQCC-2026), one of the world’s largest international platforms for quality management, productivity improvement, and continuous improvement, officially opened toda
articles.x: 8,000 Quality Professionals and 800 QCC Teams from 16 Countries Take Part The 51st International Convention on Quality Control Circles (ICQCC-2026), one of the world’s largest international platforms for quality management, productivity improvement, and continuous improvement, officially opened today in Dhaka under the theme “QCC for Sustainable Development.” Jointly organized by the Bangladesh Society for Total Quality Management (BSTQM) and the University of Asia Pacific (UAP), the three-day convention is being held from 18 to 20 November. Around 800 Quality Control Circle (QCC) teams and more than 8,000 participants from 16 countries and regions are taking part in the event. Among them, 141 teams are presenting onsite and 652 teams are participating virtually. The opening ceremony, held at Pan Pacific Sonargaon Dhaka, was attended by a distinguished gathering of quality professionals, industry leaders, academics, and international delegates. Mohammad Hatem, President of the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA), attended as Chief Guest, Qayum Reza Chowdhury, Member of the Board of Trustees of UAP, and Dr. A K M Moazzem Hussain, Adviser of BSTQM, attended as Special Guests. In his welcome address, A K M Shamsul Huda, President of BSTQM and Convener of ICQCC-2026, said that hosting the convention in Bangladesh for the third time reflects the country’s commitment to quality excellence and continuous improvement. He noted that ICQCC plays an important role in promoting global knowledge sharing and workplace improvement. Chief Guest Mohammad Hatem highlighted the importance of Quality Control Circles in improving productivity, reducing waste, enhancing competitiveness, and promoting responsible business practices. articles.o: Vietnam’s garment exports rise 3.9%, but fabric imports expose supply chain gaps
articles.s: Vietnam's textile and garment industry is facing a growing gap between export performance and domestic textile production. Although the country has 17 free trade agreements (FTAs) covering nearly 70...
articles.x: Vietnam's textile and garment industry is facing a growing gap between export performance and domestic textile production. Although the country has 17 free trade agreements (FTAs) covering nearly 70 trading partners, its dependence on imported fabrics continues to limit the benefits of preferential market access. Figure:Vietnam’s garment exports rise 3.9%, but fabric imports expose supply chain gaps. Courtesy: Collected Vietnam's textile and garment exports reached $39.84 billion in January–October 2026, up 3.9% year on year, according to figures reported by Vietnam News Agency (VNA). October exports reached $4.08 billion, up 9.8% from the same month last year. The industry is targeting $48–49 billion in exports for 2026. However, fabric imports remain a major challenge. Vietnam imported $12.87 billion worth of fabrics in the first ten months of 2026, reflecting the industry's dependence on foreign suppliers, according to October trade statistics. The domestic supply gap is particularly important for trade agreements. According to Vietnam's Ministry of Industry and Trade, domestic production meets around 50% of the industry's demand for materials and accessories, while local fabric production covers only 36% of demand. The country imported $11.6 billion worth of fabrics in the first nine months of 2026, compared with $15.2 billion in the whole of 2025. One major challenge is the yarn-forward rule under the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP). Under this requirement, production stages from yarn spinning and fabric production to garment manufacturing must take place within CPTPP member economies to qualify for preferential tariffs. articles.o: Special TMAS forum aims to strengthen ties with India
articles.s: Leading Swedish textile technology companies will showcase their latest developments at the Sweden-India Textile Technology & Innovation Forum which will take place on Monday December 7th, 2026, at the India Expo Centre & Mart in Greater Noida. Organized by Business Sweden and TMAS – the Swedish tex
articles.x: Leading Swedish textile technology companies will showcase their latest developments at the Sweden-India Textile Technology & Innovation Forum which will take place on Monday December 7th, 2026, at the India Expo Centre & Mart in Greater Noida. Organized by Business Sweden and TMAS – the Swedish textile machinery association – the event will be held alongside India ITME 2026, in collaboration with the Confederation of Indian Textile Industry (CITI). It will bring together Swedish technology suppliers, Indian textile manufacturers, international brands and industry representatives to explore investment needs, technological developments and new business opportunities. Photo: Therese Premler-Andersson A key market “As one of the world’s largest textile manufacturing countries, India’s leading companies are now looking to invest in automation and more resource-efficient production and the demand for advanced manufacturing technology is creating opportunities for specialised Swedish suppliers,” says Therese Premler-Andersson, Secretary General of TMAS. “Developing business in a market like India, however, requires the right contacts and a good understanding of local needs, which is exactly what we want to support through this initiative.” Meeting industry needs The technology requirements and investment priorities of India’s textile industry will be first on the agenda, followed by a panel discussion between well-known Swedish fashion brands including Lindex and Rusta, exploring what international brands expect from their manufacturing partners. A dedicated Swedish Technology Showcase will give each participating company an opportunity to present its innovations and applications for the Indian market. The participating companies – ACG Kinna Automatic, BW Converting, Eltex ES

articles.o: Swedish forum aims to strengthen ties with India
articles.s: Leading Swedish textile technology companies will showcase their latest developments at the Sweden-India Textile Technology & Innovation Forum which will take place on Monday December 7th, 2026, at the India Expo Centre & Mart in Greater Noida. Organised by Business Sweden and TMAS – the Swedish tex
articles.x: Leading Swedish textile technology companies will showcase their latest developments at the Sweden-India Textile Technology & Innovation Forum which will take place on Monday December 7th, 2026, at the India Expo Centre & Mart in Greater Noida. Organised by Business Sweden and TMAS – the Swedish textile machinery association – the event will be held alongside India ITME 2026, in collaboration with the Confederation of Indian Textile Industry (CITI). It will bring together Swedish technology suppliers, Indian textile manufacturers, international brands and industry representatives to explore investment needs, technological developments and new business opportunities. A key market “As one of the world’s largest textile manufacturing countries, India’s leading companies are now looking to invest in automation and more resource-efficient production and the demand for advanced manufacturing technology is creating opportunities for specialised Swedish suppliers,” says Therese Premler-Andersson, secretary general of TMAS. “Developing business in a market like India, however, requires the right contacts and a good understanding of local needs, which is exactly what we want to support through this initiative.” Meeting industry needs The technology requirements and investment priorities of India’s textile industry will be first on the agenda, followed by a panel discussion between well-known Swedish fashion brands including Lindex and Rusta, exploring what international brands expect from their manufacturing partners. A dedicated Swedish Technology Showcase will give each participating company an opportunity to present its innovations and applications for the Indian market. The participating companies – ACG Kinna Automatic, BW Converting, Eltex ES Automatex, imogo and Vandewiele

articles.o: AFFOA Releases Digital Manufacturing Playbook To Help U.S. Textile Manufacturers Take Practical First Steps
articles.s: BEDFORD, Mass. — November 10, 2026 — Advanced Functional Fabrics of America (AFFOA), a Manufacturing USA Institute, today released its Digital Manufacturing Playbook, a practical resource to help U.S. textile manufacturers identify opportunities for improvement and take actionable steps toward digit
articles.x: BEDFORD, Mass. — November 10, 2026 — Advanced Functional Fabrics of America (AFFOA), a Manufacturing USA Institute, today released its Digital Manufacturing Playbook, a practical resource to help U.S. textile manufacturers identify opportunities for improvement and take actionable steps toward digital manufacturing. The Playbook is available for download here: https:// affoa.org/case_study/digital-manufacturing-for-textiles/ “We spoke with dozens of manufacturers while developing this Playbook: small businesses and larger operations, yarn spinners, fabric mills, and end-item manufacturers. Some build custom digital tools for every bottleneck they see and others still operate predominantly analog, relying on deep employee expertise,” said Caitlin Knowles, Ph.D., Senior Textile Engineer and Product Group Leader at AFFOA. “Adopting digital manufacturing isn’t one size fits all. We built the Playbook with many entry points, so manufacturers can find a practical path forward based on how they operate today and the challenges they want to solve.” The Playbook connects digital manufacturing concepts to everyday needs such as production visibility, quality documentation, product development, and preserving workforce knowledge. articles.o: Combating intake clogs: Why cotton fly causes unplanned compressor downtime in spinning mills
articles.s: When a compressor unexpectedly stops midshift and your team discovers an intake filter packed with cotton fly, getting the line running again takes precedence. Yet treating each stoppage as an isolate...
articles.x: When a compressor unexpectedly stops midshift and your team discovers an intake filter packed with cotton fly, getting the line running again takes precedence. Yet treating each stoppage as an isolated equipment maintenance chore misses a critical warning sign. What if your current intake diagnostics are already trying to tell you when your next failure will happen? The financial and operational toll of compressor downtime Your mill's losses depend on which machines lose air and whether you can make up the missed output. A useful calculation includes overtime and restart waste, as well as the value of production you cannot recover. This number gives maintenance spending a financial basis specific to your operation. Courtesy: Collected A global survey of 3,600 senior decision-makers across multiple sectors found that 83% estimated unplanned downtime costs at least $10,000 per hour. With 76% estimating downtime costs reaching $500,000 hourly, the findings illustrate industrial exposure without establishing a textile mill benchmark. Electricity also deserves attention even while the compressor continues running. According to an Oak Ridge National Laboratory report, compressed air can account for up to 30% of the total plant energy costs in some facilities. Only 5% to 10% of input power reaches the point of use after accounting for system losses. Those figures describe whole systems, so your assessment needs measurements from your own installation. Comparing power consumption and delivered airflow under similar operating conditions can help you evaluate the financial benefit of intake maintenance without attributing every system loss to filter condition. articles.x: W. CONSHOHOCKEN, Pa. — November 16, 2026 — ASTM International is exploring the establishment of a new committee dedicated to hemp products, with a virtual meeting scheduled for Dec. 16, 2026. The proposed committee’s scope will include farm products and raw hemp ingredients for food, textiles, plastics, building and construction, and more. Hemp products have thousands of practical applications in different fields. In agriculture, it is used for phytoremediation and cropping systems, in the industrial space, its uses include nutrition, fuels, animal feed, and textile applications, and it has various other developing applications in construction and energy sectors. A new committee would support research, technical applications, and collaboration to explore hemp standardization. “It’s not unusual to hear that hemp has 50,000 uses,” says Hunter Buffington, chair of subcommittee D37.07 on industrial hemp. “Our hemp industry has a world of opportunities, applications, and sectors with which we will partner. I believe that this committee will create a new, centralized home for businesses and technical experts who can address the gaps in research and standardization for industries wanting to use hemp as an ingredient or input. The formation of one space for this activity will be impactful for our stakeholders spread out across these industries.” Buffington also highlights several top priorities for a new committee, with the goal of integrating hemp into existing industries and supply chains. Work is ongoing to build foundational tests and methods needed to understand the characteristics and properties of hemp materials. articles.o: Natural fibres raise the bar but will others follow?
articles.s: Natural fibres have built comprehensive systems for traceability and assessment. Applying the same expectations to all materials is the next step for responsible sourcing. By International Wool Textile Organisation BRUSSELS – Across recent textile conferences and trade fairs, natural fibre discussio
articles.x: Natural fibres have built comprehensive systems for traceability and assessment. Applying the same expectations to all materials is the next step for responsible sourcing. By International Wool Textile Organisation BRUSSELS – Across recent textile conferences and trade fairs, natural fibre discussions have returned to a recurring theme: how to reduce impacts while investing in the health of the landscapes and communities that produce these materials. These discussions reflect a growing expectation that responsibility should reach back to the source of a fibre, and that claims about progress should withstand scrutiny. For those working with wool and other natural fibres, this progress can coexist with a sense of an uphill battle. Producers are repeatedly challenged to demonstrate more, measure more and improve further. Meeting those expectations requires time, expertise and money, often before a natural fibre producer knows whether the market will recognise the investment. While these expectations are justified – natural-fibre production has environmental and social challenges that need attention – they raise a question about the market in which producers compete: how consistently are equivalent expectations applied across all fibre supply chains? Transparent sourcing Natural-fibre industries have built a substantial infrastructure for transparent sourcing. Wool, cotton, mohair and cotton all have several certification traceability schemes that audit and trace different aspects from animal welfare, to organic, regenerative agriculture and more. These schemes differ in scope and rigour, but together they demonstrate a substantial commitment to transparency and accountability in production practices. articles.o: Getting to grips with the new French scoring system
articles.s: Fashion brands selling into France face growing commercial and reputational risks under new environmental scoring rules that allow third parties to assess their products, even without their involvement. Since October 1st, 2026, organisations including NGOs, retailers and product comparison platforms
articles.x: Fashion brands selling into France face growing commercial and reputational risks under new environmental scoring rules that allow third parties to assess their products, even without their involvement. Since October 1st, 2026, organisations including NGOs, retailers and product comparison platforms have been permitted to calculate and publish environmental scores for clothing sold in France, using conservative assumptions where manufacturers have failed to provide sufficient product data. The development represents a significant change in how the environmental performance of clothing is assessed and communicated, with implications for international brands regardless of where their products are manufactured. The French system, previously known as Eco-Score and now officially called Environmental Cost (Coût Environnemental), is based on the government’s Ecobalyse methodology, which evaluates the environmental impact of textile products. Although publication of environmental scores remains largely voluntary, brands making other environmental claims are required to disclose their scores. More significantly, companies that choose not to participate may find their products assessed by independent third parties using default values that could result in less favourable ratings. The implications extend beyond environmental transparency, because the same assessment framework is also being used to determine durability scores under France’s new legislation targeting ultra-fast fashion. Financial penalties Under French Law 2026-602, products falling within the scope of the ultra-fast fashion legislation may face additional financial contributions linked to their durability. articles.o: Opportunities in EV battery protection
articles.s: Aerogels, advanced polymers and fire-resistant coatings are expected to capture almost 40% of the expanding market for electric vehicle battery fire protection materials by 2037, according to a new study by technology research consultancy IDTechEx. The global market for these materials is forecast t
articles.x: Aerogels, advanced polymers and fire-resistant coatings are expected to capture almost 40% of the expanding market for electric vehicle battery fire protection materials by 2037, according to a new study by technology research consultancy IDTechEx. The global market for these materials is forecast to grow at a compound annual rate of 13% over the next decade, exceeding $10 billion by 2037, as electric vehicle manufacturers seek improved solutions for preventing or delaying the spread of battery fires. The findings are contained in the new IDTechEx report, Fire Protection Materials for EV Batteries 2027-2037: Markets, Trends, and Forecasts , which examines the changing requirements for thermal insulation and fire protection as battery technologies continue to evolve. Currently, established materials including encapsulating foams and mica sheets account for more than 80% of the market. Their combined share, however, is expected to decline as alternative materials offering improved thermal performance, lower weight and greater design flexibility gain wider acceptance. The development presents opportunities for suppliers of specialist nonwovens, advanced insulation materials, coatings and engineered polymers, particularly as battery manufacturers seek to combine several protective functions within increasingly compact battery packs. Preventing thermal runaway A central challenge for EV manufacturers is thermal runaway, in which overheating within a lithium-ion battery cell can trigger a self-sustaining reaction, potentially spreading to neighbouring cells and eventually beyond the battery pack. articles.x: INDIA ITME 2026 , which will take place from December 4 to 9, 2026, at the India Exposition Mart Ltd (IEML) in Greater Noida (Delhi), is the largest textile exhibition of its kind in India. As India is one of the most prominent textile hubs in in the world, this event represents the ideal platform for Picanol to showcase its latest breakthrough innovations. Picanol will be exhibiting at Booth E10 in Hall 15, where three high-tech airjet weaving machines will be on display. The spotlight will undoubtedly be on the two AirOne weaving machines, one of which will be equipped with SmartShed, marking the world premiere of this innovative solution. “Together with my team, I’m particularly excited and proud that we have the opportunity to bring two of the new AirOne airjet machines to the stage here in India. This once again reflects Picanol’s recognition of India’s growing importance and the key role it is playing in shaping the future of the textile industry, both in the region and globally. We are convinced that AirOne successfully responds to the latest trends we are observing in the industry. articles.s: US cotton futures settled marginally higher on Thursday, supported by strong export sales in recent weeks and expectations of continued demand. However, a stronger US dollar, weakness in grain markets and ongoing harvest pressure restricted gains. Traders remained cautious ahead of the delayed weekl
articles.x: US cotton futures settled marginally higher on Thursday, supported by strong export sales in recent weeks and expectations of continued demand. However, a stronger US dollar, weakness in grain markets and ongoing harvest pressure restricted gains. Traders remained cautious ahead of the delayed weekly export sales report from the US Department of Agriculture (USDA). The most active March 2027 cotton contract on ICE Futures US gained 12 points, or 0.15 percent, to settle at 82.51 cents per pound. The December 2026 contract rose 15 points to 78.67 cents per pound, compared with Wednesday’s settlement of 78.52 cents. The December/March spread stood at 384 points, with March trading at a premium. The US dollar climbed to its highest level in nearly 19 months on Thursday, following stronger inflation data that prompted markets to reassess the Federal Reserve’s interest rate outlook. A stronger dollar makes US cotton more expensive for overseas buyers, particularly when competing with supplies from Brazil and Australia. Chicago corn, wheat and soybean futures also declined as the dollar’s appreciation weighed on export sentiment across agricultural commodities. According to market analysts, the cotton market showed little reaction to the USDA’s monthly supply and demand report released on Tuesday. The agency reduced its estimate of US cotton production by 267,000 bales to 13.18 million bales but also lowered its domestic demand projection. Weakness in Chicago grain markets, the stronger dollar and the continuing harvest were influencing cotton prices. The arrival of newly harvested cotton has also increased market availability, limiting the potential for a stronger recovery. articles.s: Benninger, a complete system supplier with leading technologies for continuous wet processing and discontinuous dyeing, offers proven solutions that meet the needs of Indian textile manufacturers,...
articles.x: Benninger, a complete system supplier with leading technologies for continuous wet processing and discontinuous dyeing, offers proven solutions that meet the needs of Indian textile manufacturers, who are under growing pressure to process a wider range of fabrics faster while using less water, energy and chemicals. At ITME 2026, from December 4 to 9, 2026, Benninger will present FabricMaster, SynthMaster and CPB Knit – reliable solutions for demanding woven and knitted articles, from sportswear and heavy jersey to sensitive synthetic blends and high-value underwear fabrics. In every dyehouse, some articles place considerably greater demands on the machinery than others. Fabrics may mark easily, develop uneven shades or require longer processing times. As fashion cycles shorten and product diversity increases, the ability to process demanding qualities reliably is becoming an important competitive advantage for Indian mills serving both domestic and export markets. Benninger FabricMaster: Versatile dyeing, from sportswear to heavy jersey Discontinuous dyeing is one area in which fabric quality and machine performance are particularly closely linked. Processors must handle an increasingly diverse range of woven and knitted fabrics while reducing cycle times, water consumption and energy use. The ability to switch efficiently between fabric qualities without compromising colour consistency is therefore essential. Benninger addresses these requirements with the FabricMaster jet dyeing machine. It processes woven and knitted fabrics marks rope-mark-free, including articles that are difficult or impossible to process on other machines. articles.s: Austria’s Lenzing Group is investing a further €27 million at its lyocell fibre production facility in Mobile, Alabama, bringing its recently announced investment programme for speciality nonwovens fibres to €50 million. The latest investment will expand the US plant’s capabilities in short-cut lyoc
articles.x: Austria’s Lenzing Group is investing a further €27 million at its lyocell fibre production facility in Mobile, Alabama, bringing its recently announced investment programme for speciality nonwovens fibres to €50 million. The latest investment will expand the US plant’s capabilities in short-cut lyocell fibres and other speciality products, providing greater production flexibility and supporting the development of customised wood-based fibres for nonwoven applications. It follows the announcement of a €23 million investment to expand production capabilities at the company’s main manufacturing site in Lenzing, Austria. Short-cut lyocell fibres are particularly relevant to specialised nonwoven production processes, requiring controlled fibre lengths and consistent performance characteristics. The additional capabilities will allow Lenzing to develop a broader range of products tailored to individual applications. “Nonwovens are a strategic growth area for Lenzing and our investment in Mobile reflects our strong commitment to expanding our capabilities in this business and strengthening our presence in the Americas and globally,” said Georg Kasperkovitz, CEO of the Lenzing Group. “The investment will expand Mobile’s capabilities in specialty fibres, including lyocell short-cut fibres, and future innovations. This will enable Lenzing to offer a broader range of speciality fibres for nonwovens.” Fibre substitution A further objective is to increase the use of wood-based cellulosic fibres as alternatives to fossil-based synthetic materials in nonwoven products. articles.o: An energy and steam saving alternative to conventional high-temperature polyester dyeing
articles.s: Innovation Masterminds: Sadia Afrin Mou1, Anik Naha2 , Mita Akhter3 1-3 University of Scholars Factory Supervisor: Khaled Faisal, GM, NAZ Bangladesh Ltd Technical Supervisor: Md. Mesbah Uddin, Tech...
articles.x: Innovation Masterminds: Sadia Afrin Mou 1 , Anik Naha 2 , Mita Akhter 3 1-3 University of Scholars Factory Supervisor: Khaled Faisal, GM, NAZ Bangladesh Ltd Technical Supervisor: Md. Mesbah Uddin, Technical Sales Manager, Transfar Chemicals Project Coordinator: Najmus Sakib, Sr. Executive, Textile Today Abstract Polyester is a hydrophobic, highly crystalline synthetic fiber with limited dye affinity, and it is conventionally dyed with disperse dyes at 130–140 °C. This high-temperature route requires substantial steam, energy, and time, especially for polyester–cotton (PC) and CVC blends. In this study, a low-temperature carrier-assisted dyeing process was evaluated for 80/20 CVC single jersey fabric at 115 °C. The trial formulation used a carrier, a dispersing agent, a levelling agent, an auxiliary stabilizer, and acetic acid for pH control. The process produced a level, uniform shade with no visible patchiness. Compared with a conventional 130 °C baseline, the low-temperature trial reduced peak dyeing temperature by 15 °C, specific steam consumption by 16.7% (1.286 to 1.072 kg steam/kg fabric). Total process time decreased from 222 min to 170 min, saving 52 min per batch and giving a calculated productivity gain of 23.4%. Dry and wet rubbing fastness remained comparable, with most grades between 4 and 5 on a 1–5 scale. These results indicate that carrier-assisted low-temperature dyeing can reduce steam, energy, and process time while maintaining acceptable shade quality and rubbing fastness. However, because the baseline and trial differed in fabric structure, GSM, batch size, and shade, further matched industrial trials are needed to confirm scalability and performance across other shades and blends. articles.s: MORGANTON, N.C. — November 16, 2026 — Goodwill Industries of Northwest North Carolina, UpCycle Fiber Inc., Material Return, the NSF Textile Innovation Engine of North Carolina, and The Industrial Commons are building a connected regional system that brings together the multiple capabilities needed t
articles.x: MORGANTON, N.C. — November 16, 2026 — Goodwill Industries of Northwest North Carolina, UpCycle Fiber Inc., Material Return, the NSF Textile Innovation Engine of North Carolina, and The Industrial Commons are building a connected regional system that brings together the multiple capabilities needed to eliminate textile waste by maximizing reuse and resale and then turning the remaining textiles into resilient recycled raw materials. Textile‑to‑textile circularity requires more than a single technology or organization. It depends on connecting collection, resale, sorting, deconstruction, fiber processing, and manufacturing capabilities so materials can move efficiently toward their highest‑value next use. The North Carolina Textile Innovation Engine, working with Goodwill Industries of Northwest North Carolina, UpCycle Fiber, Material Return and The Industrial Commons, is helping build that connected regional system by bringing together organizations with complementary expertise, infrastructure and resources. This Textile to Textile Ecosystem approach follows a clear hierarchy: maximize reuse and resale first, then identify the highest‑value pathway for the materials that remain. Each partner contributes a complementary capability to that pathway, allowing materials to move from collection and resale through identification, sorting, and processing, and ultimately back into raw materials for new textile manufacturing. Building those connections, and filling gaps where capabilities do not yet exist, is central to creating a viable textile‑to‑textile circularity ecosystem. articles.x: The 51st International Convention on Quality Control Circles (ICQCC-2026) will be held in Dhaka from 18 to 20 November under the theme “QCC for Sustainable Development.” Details of the convention were shared at a press conference held at Pan Pacific Sonargaon Dhaka on Monday. The briefing was attended by BSTQM President and ICQCC-2026 Convener A K M Shamsul Huda, BSTQM Adviser Engr. A.M.M. Khairul Bashar, UAP Registrar Brig. Gen. (Retd.) Prof. Dr. A K M Nazrul Islam, BSTQM Secretary General M M Kabir, ICQCC-2026 Technical and Evaluation Committee Member Md. Rokibul Islam, representatives of BSTQM and UAP, and members of the media. Jointly organized by the Bangladesh Society for Total Quality Management (BSTQM) and the University of Asia Pacific (UAP), the convention is expected to bring together approximately 800 Quality Control Circle (QCC) teams and around 8,000 QCC members from 16 countries and regions. Among the participating teams, 141 will present onsite and 652 online. The main presentation sessions will be held on 19 and 20 November at UAP, where teams will present workplace improvement projects on productivity, quality enhancement, cost reduction, and problem-solving. Nearly 100 local and international judges will evaluate the presentations. Participating countries include Japan, China, India, South Korea, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, the Philippines, Taiwan, Namibia, Zambia, Mozambique, and Mauritius, along with Bangladesh. Internationally coordinated by JUSE (Union of Japanese Scientists and Engineers), Japan, ICQCC is widely known as the “Quality Olympics” and is one of the world’s largest annual platforms for promoting Quality Control Circles (QCC) and Total Quality Management (TQM). articles.s: 글로벌 패션기업 인디텍스가 섬유·의류·신발 산업 공급망의 탈탄소화를 위해 최대 5000만 달러를 투자한다. 신흥시장 제조업체의 친환경 설비와 기술 도입에 필요한 장기 자금을 지원하는 펀드에 참여해 공급망 전환을 뒷받침할 계획이다.인디텍스는 최근 출범한 ‘섬유·의류·신발 공급업체 탈탄소화 펀드(Decarbonization of Textile, Apparel, & Footwear Suppliers Fund·D-TAFS)’의 주요 투자자로 참여한다고 17일 밝혔다. 투자 예정액은 보도자료 환산 기준 약 666억2500만 원이다.D-TAF

articles.t: 루이 비통, 키스 해링 재단과 협업 컬렉션
articles.o: 루이 비통, 키스 해링 재단과 협업 컬렉션
articles.s: 루이 비통이 키스 해링 재단(Keith Haring Foundation)과 협업한 ‘루이 비통 키스 해링 컬렉션(The Keith Haring Collection)’을 공개했다. 가방과 가죽 소품, 여행용 제품, 여성 레디투웨어, 슈즈, 액세서리, 향수 등 여성 제품군 전반에 작가의 작품과 캐릭터를 적용했으며, 2027년 1월 1일부터 전 세계 루이 비통 매장에서 출시한다.이번 컬렉션은 여성 컬렉션 아티스틱 디렉터 니콜라 제스키에르(Nicolas Ghesquière)가 뉴욕 프릭 컬렉션(Frick Collection)에서 선보인 2

articles.o: 中 화섬업 이익 81.7% 급증…폭리
articles.s: 중국 화학섬유 제조업의 이익이 올해 1~9월 80% 넘게 급증했다. 매출 증가율은 3%대에 그쳤지만 이익은 큰 폭으로 늘어나면서 중국 섬유·의류 산업 내 업종별 실적 격차가 뚜렷해졌다.중국 국가통계국이 지난달 27일 발표한 산업기업 경영실적에 따르면 올해 1~9월 중국 화학섬유 제조업의 이익 총액은 326억8000만위안으로 전년 동기보다 81.7% 증가했다. 같은 기간 매출액은 7890억위안으로 3.2% 늘어나는 데 그쳤다. 이익 증가율이 매출 증가율의 25배를 웃돈 셈이다.이익 급증에는 매출원가 증가세가 상대적으로 낮았던 점이 영

articles.s: 롬앤(rom&nd)을 운영하는 아이패밀리에스씨(114840)가 올해 3분기 매출 증가에도 수익성은 하락한 실적을 기록했다.아이패밀리에스씨는 16일 공시를 통해 2026년 3분기 매출액 556억원, 영업이익 19억원을 기록했다고 밝혔다. 매출은 전년 동기 대비 4% 증가했으나 영업이익은 70% 감소했다.회사 측은 미국과 유럽 등 주요 해외 시장 확대를 위한 투자와 유통 구조 개선에 따른 일회성 비용이 영업이익 감소에 영향을 미쳤다고 설명했다.특히 2024년 하반기 글로벌 수요 증가 과정에서 발생한 일부 제품의 과잉 공급 문제를 해소하

articles.t: 베트남 공장은 늘었지만 주문 하락세

articles.o: Kevlar Exo raises the bar for motorsport fuel tank safety
articles.s: The first major revision of international motorsport fuel tank safety regulations in more than 25 years has prompted the development of new protective materials incorporating the latest generation of Kevlar aramid fibres. Aero Tec Laboratories (ATL), a specialist in racing fuel systems based in Rams
articles.x: The first major revision of international motorsport fuel tank safety regulations in more than 25 years has prompted the development of new protective materials incorporating the latest generation of Kevlar aramid fibres. Aero Tec Laboratories (ATL), a specialist in racing fuel systems based in Ramsey, New Jersey, has worked with materials science company Arclin, of Alpharetta, Georgia, to develop two new fuel bladder materials incorporating Kevlar Exo – an advanced reinforcement fibre offering approximately 40% greater strength-to-weight performance than conventional Kevlar. The materials have been designed to meet the requirements of the new 8875-2025 standard introduced by international motorsport governing body FIA, involving tougher tests for puncture resistance, impact protection and fire survivability. The regulations also address compatibility with a wider range of fuels, including the sustainable alternatives increasingly being introduced into motorsport. Fuel bladders are flexible, reinforced containers installed inside racing vehicles to reduce the risk of fuel leakage and fire in the event of a collision. Unlike conventional rigid fuel tanks, they are designed to deform under impact while retaining their contents, making the performance of their reinforcing materials particularly important. Two new grades ATL has become the first manufacturer to develop fuel bladder materials meeting the requirements of both grades of the new FIA standard. Its 922-C material has achieved Grade 1 approval for Advanced Safety Fuel Tanks, while its 927-B material has successfully completed the testing requirements for Grade 2 Competition Safety Fuel Tanks. articles.t: YRC를 위한 9가지 Mahlo 교정 시스템
articles.o: Nine Mahlo straightening systems for YRC
articles.s: Thailand’s YRC Textile has invested in nine Orthopac RXVMC-20 fabric straightening systems from Germany’s Mahlo as it seeks to improve quality consistency in the production of knitted fabrics for leading international sportswear brands. Based in Samut Sakhon, YRC employs around 3,500 people and has
articles.x: Thailand’s YRC Textile has invested in nine Orthopac RXVMC-20 fabric straightening systems from Germany’s Mahlo as it seeks to improve quality consistency in the production of knitted fabrics for leading international sportswear brands. Based in Samut Sakhon, YRC employs around 3,500 people and has extensive warp and circular knitting operations supported by four dyehouses with a combined capacity of up to 100 tons of fabric per day. The company, which has been operating for more than 55 years, supplies fabrics to major sportswear brands including Adidas, Decathlon, Nike and Under Armour. The investment follows the successful installation of an initial Orthopac RXVMC-20 system, with YRC subsequently ordering a total of nine units within a year. Further investments are planned for 2027. The YRC management team (left to right): Surasak Bunnag, Kittikom Wachirapichet, Napong Nitipongwanich and Praphat Nitipongwanich, with Viroch Youttananukorn, MD of Texmac-Next on the far right. © Mahlo Rapid correction The systems are designed to address one of the persistent challenges in knitted fabric finishing – the rapid changes in bow and skew distortion that can occur during processing, particularly in highly elastic fabrics containing elastane. Such distortions can become especially pronounced at fabric seams, where sudden changes may occur before conventional straightening equipment has time to respond. Mahlo’s Orthopac RXVMC-20 addresses this problem through two independently controlled straightening modules, supported by scanning systems at both the inlet and outlet. The inlet scanner detects distortion before the fabric reaches the correction rollers, allowing adjustments to be made immediately rather than after the affected material has passed through the machine. articles.o: BUTEX team secures second place in Hong Kong with sustainable aviation fuel innovation
articles.s: Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX) student Arian Aidid has brought international recognition to Bangladesh by securing second place at the Data Development Prize (DDP) 2026 Hong Kong Case Compe...
articles.x: Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX) student Arian Aidid has brought international recognition to Bangladesh by securing second place at the Data Development Prize (DDP) 2026 Hong Kong Case Competition as a member of Team Lazarus. The team earned the accolade for its innovative project, “Nexa Fuel: From Waste to Wings,” which explores the production of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) from used cooking oil. The initiative aims to address two pressing global challenges simultaneously: waste management and the growing demand for cleaner energy sources. Arian, a student from the 47th batch of the Department of Textile Engineering and Management at BUTEX, represented Bangladesh alongside teammates from several universities and institutions. The team consisted of Hossain (IUBAT), Syeda Fabiha (University of Dhaka), Surabhi (Green University), Atiq Rahman (BGMEA), and Arian Aidid, while Amit from BUTEX served as an alternate team member. The team's journey began at the national round of DDP 2026 in Bangladesh, where participants were selected through an online competition and later grouped into teams through a lottery-based process. Team Lazarus emerged as the national champion, earning the opportunity to represent Bangladesh in Hong Kong. For the international competition, the team developed Nexa Fuel into a comprehensive business model focused on converting waste cooking oil into sustainable aviation fuel. The concept highlights how discarded cooking oil from restaurants and hotels can be collected and utilized as a valuable raw material for producing cleaner aviation fuel, reducing environmental pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. articles.x: Italian insulation specialist Thermore has partnered with Canadian skiwear brand Orage on its Autumn/Winter 2026 collection, combining three different recycled polyester insulation technologies to provide targeted warmth and freedom of movement. The new collection incorporates Thermore Freedom, Ecodown Fibers and Classic insulation materials in a range of ski jackets and trousers, with each selected according to the performance requirements of specific areas of the garments. The approach allows Orage to balance thermal protection with flexibility, particularly in areas where skiers require greater freedom of movement. Thermore Freedom, a stretch insulation designed to recover its original shape after repeated movement, is used in the Glades Insulated Jacket and Pant alongside Orage’s two-way stretch Prime 20 outer fabric. © Thermore The women’s Glades jacket incorporates 80g of Freedom insulation in the body, with 60g of Thermore Classic in the sleeves and Ecodown Fibers in the helmet-compatible hood. The corresponding trousers combine 60g of Freedom in the upper legs with 40g of Classic in the lower sections. Body-mapped insulation A more targeted approach is employed in the Glades Hybrid Insulated Jacket, which uses Thermore Ecodown Fibers in the upper body, shoulders and hood, while 60g of Classic insulation is positioned in the sleeves, underarms, side panels and lower body. The jacket also incorporates underarm ventilation, a detachable helmet-compatible hood and an insulated phone pocket. Ecodown Fibers is a synthetic down alternative manufactured entirely from recycled polyester, with a claimed loft equivalent to 660-fill-power natural down. articles.o: Athens Knit Lab challenges craft boundaries
articles.s: Can computer-controlled flat knitting machines be considered tools of craftsmanship, or does automation fundamentally change the nature of textile making? This question was at the centre of a presentation by Marianna Fasoi of Athens Knit Lab at the recent European Textile Network (ETN) conference in
articles.x: Can computer-controlled flat knitting machines be considered tools of craftsmanship, or does automation fundamentally change the nature of textile making? This question was at the centre of a presentation by Marianna Fasoi of Athens Knit Lab at the recent European Textile Network (ETN) conference in Athens, Greece. Entitled Reimagining Traditional Textile Practices: From Craft to 3D Knitting , the presentation challenged conventional distinctions between traditional textile crafts and advanced manufacturing technologies, arguing that digitalisation does not eliminate craftsmanship but transforms how specialist knowledge and creativity are applied. The European Textile Network brings together practitioners working across traditional textile disciplines, including weaving, hand knitting, tufting and embroidery. Its membership is predominantly European, with strong representation from Germany, making the conference an appropriate setting to examine the evolving relationship between established craft practices and contemporary textile production. Athens Knit Lab, a specialist in advanced flat-bed machine knitting and its applications, was invited to contribute to the discussion, offering a perspective from a sector increasingly characterised by sophisticated computer programming, automated machinery and three-dimensional textile construction. Marianna Fasoi questioned whether the use of automated machinery necessarily removes the human skills traditionally associated with craftsmanship. While modern knitting machines can execute programmed movements, repeat complex sequences with precision and expand manufacturing possibilities, they remain dependent on human expertise throughout the development process. The company will showcase two Mayer & Cie. circular knitting machines for mattress fabrics and single jersey applications, alongside a machine from Chinese manufacturer Huixing. The Value Portfolio combines German engineering and knitting heads manufactured in Albstadt with a competitive manufacturing base in China. articles.t: 액체 코어 섬유는 말라리아에 대한 새로운 무기를 제공합니다
articles.o: Liquid-core fibres offer new weapon against malaria
articles.s: Swiss researchers have developed a new type of insecticide-containing fibre that could help overcome growing resistance to conventional mosquito nets – potentially providing longer-lasting protection against malaria in some of the world’s most vulnerable regions. Developed by Empa, the Swiss Federal
articles.x: Swiss researchers have developed a new type of insecticide-containing fibre that could help overcome growing resistance to conventional mosquito nets – potentially providing longer-lasting protection against malaria in some of the world’s most vulnerable regions. Developed by Empa, the Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology, in collaboration with industrial partners Vestergaard and Monosuisse, the technology uses a liquid-core fibre to incorporate insecticides that cannot withstand the high temperatures involved in conventional synthetic fibre production. The development addresses an increasingly urgent public health challenge. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), more than 280 million people contracted malaria across 80 countries in 2024, resulting in approximately 610,000 deaths. Insecticide-treated mosquito nets remain among the most important means of preventing infection, particularly in regions where access to medical treatment is limited. Growing resistance among mosquito populations to the pyrethroid insecticides traditionally used in these products, however, is reducing their effectiveness. The challenge for manufacturers has been finding a way to incorporate alternative insecticides into synthetic fibres without damaging their active ingredients during processing. Conventional insecticide-containing yarns are produced by melt spinning, in which polymers are heated and extruded through fine nozzles. Many newer insecticides are unsuitable for this process because they evaporate or degrade at elevated temperatures. Researchers at Empa’s Advanced Fibers laboratory in St Gallen have now developed an alternative approach through the three-year MalCoFil project, supported by Swiss innovation agency Innosuisse. articles.x: Free webinar on 25 November will explore how effective humidity management can improve profits and productivity, reduce fibre loss and support consistent textile quality For textile manufacturers, seemingly small changes in environmental conditions can have a significant impact on production performance. Humidity is one factor that can influence fibre behaviour, yarn processing, production efficiency and finished product quality. On 25 November 2026 at 5:00pm IST, Condair will host a free webinar, ‘Improving Profits in Textile Manufacturing with Humidity Control’, aimed at professionals involved in textile manufacturing, production and operations. The session will be presented by Dave Bull of Condair and Jaydeep Dasgupta of Regent Machine & Servicing, bringing together international humidity-control expertise and practical experience of the Indian textile industry. Why humidity matters in textile production Textile fibres are hygroscopic, meaning their properties can be affected by the amount of moisture in the surrounding air. Maintaining appropriate humidity conditions can therefore offer manufacturers opportunities to reduce fibre loss and yarn breakages, while improving production efficiency and product quality. Humidity control should not simply be considered an environmental requirement. When applied correctly, it can become a tool for improving manufacturing performance and profitability. Practical advice for textile manufacturers During the webinar , Dave Bull and Jaydeep Dasgupta will examine the different stages of textile manufacturing and explain where humidity control can provide benefits. The collection translated literary themes into contemporary denim fabrics, showcasing the company’s blend of creativity, craftsmanship, and technical expertise. The Envoy delegation included Managing Director Tanvir Ahmed, Chief Executive Officer Tushar Tripathi, Marketing Director (USA Office) Viresh Verma, and other team members. During the two-day exhibition, the team engaged with international buyers, fashion brands, sourcing professionals, and industry partners while exploring new opportunities for collaboration. Envoy Textile also participated in the event’s Denim Talks program. articles.o: Garden Silk Mills boosts speciality yarn production
articles.s: Indian polyester manufacturer Garden Silk Mills has expanded its production of bi-shrinkage yarns (BSYs) using a new single-stage spinning process developed by Barmag. The company has now been operating 24 retrofitted positions on its existing Barmag Wings FDY polyester spinning machines for around
articles.x: Indian polyester manufacturer Garden Silk Mills has expanded its production of bi-shrinkage yarns (BSYs) using a new single-stage spinning process developed by Barmag. The company has now been operating 24 retrofitted positions on its existing Barmag Wings FDY polyester spinning machines for around a year, reporting improvements in yarn quality and production efficiency. The investment reflects growing demand in India for speciality polyester yarns capable of creating distinctive fabric textures and finishes, particularly for apparel and home textiles. Alternative to texturing Bi-shrinkage yarns, also known as intermingled textured yarns (ITYs), combine partially oriented yarn (POY) and fully drawn yarn (FDY), which have different shrinkage characteristics. When subsequently exposed to heat during fabric processing, the two components shrink at different rates, creating bulk and texture without the need for conventional false-twist texturing. The resulting yarns can be used to produce lightweight chiffon, crinkle and pleated fabrics, as well as fleece materials and curtains. Traditionally, the production of these yarns has involved separate spinning operations for the POY and FDY components, followed by an additional process to combine them. Barmag’s new approach, based on its Wings FDY Plus eco technology, brings these operations together in a single continuous spinning process. The system can produce up to 16 yarn ends simultaneously and operates at significantly higher speeds than conventional two-stage BSY production systems, according to Barmag. Independent control A key feature of the technology is the ability to adjust the properties of the two yarn components independently before they are combined. articles.t: Unspun과 Arvind가 제휴하여 의류 제조를 위한 3D 직조 확장
articles.o: Unspun and Arvind partner to scale 3D weaving for apparel manufacturing
articles.s: US-based textile technology company Unspun has partnered with Indian textile manufacturer Arvind. It aims to introduce its yarn-to-garment 3D weaving technology in industrial-scale apparel manufacturi...
articles.x: US-based textile technology company Unspun has partnered with Indian textile manufacturer Arvind. It aims to introduce its yarn-to-garment 3D weaving technology in industrial-scale apparel manufacturing. Courtesy: Collected Under the initial phase of the agreement, two OneWeave machines will be installed at Arvind's facility in Ahmedabad, India. Operations are scheduled to begin by December 2026. The partnership aims to move Unspun's 3D weaving technology beyond its microfactory setting and integrate it into large-scale apparel production. The technology converts yarn directly into finished garment components, offering an alternative to conventional cut-and-sew manufacturing. Unspun will provide machine installation, commissioning, software, training, and ongoing technical support. Arvind will manage production operations. Brands interested in using the technology will contract directly with Arvind. The companies have also outlined a phased expansion plan that could include more than 30 additional machines across India and North America between 2027 and 2028. According to Unspun, the technology is designed to support demand-led manufacturing. It allowing brands to produce garments closer to actual market demand rather than relying heavily on forecasts and bulk orders. Arne Arens, board chair of Unspun, said the partnership would help scale the technology globally and bring production closer to major markets in the US and Europe. He added that the system could help brands respond to demand in weeks instead of months, reduce waste and lower markdown exposure. Karan Ojha, CEO of Arvind's Wovens Business and Center of Excellence, said the technology could reduce manufacturing complexity, improve material utilization and enable faster replenishment for global apparel brands.

articles.x: Leaving behind the familiar world of cotton, yarn and colours, students and faculty members of the Department of Textile Engineering at Northern University Bangladesh (NUB) embarked on a memorable tour to Cox’s Bazar, enjoying the natural beauty of the world’s longest unbroken natural sandy sea beach. Organized by the Textile Society of Northern University Bangladesh on 14 November 2026, the tour aimed to provide students with a refreshing break from their regular academic activities while strengthening friendship, mutual understanding and relationships between faculty members and students. The tour was attended by G. M. Faysal, Head of the Department and Associate Professor. Also present were Associate Professor Mazaharul Islam, Assistant Professor and Coordinator Nazmul Islam, and Assistant Professor Russell Hawlader. Their participation added warmth and enthusiasm to the entire journey. During the tour, students explored some of Cox’s Bazar’s most popular destinations, including Laboni, Sugandha and Kolatoli sea beaches, Himchari, Inani Sea Beach and the scenic Marine Drive. The breathtaking views of the sea, waves, hills and sandy coastline created an enjoyable atmosphere. Students spent memorable moments through group activities, photography, music, conversations and lively gatherings. Beyond recreation, the tour served as an opportunity to strengthen the bond between teachers and students. Such extracurricular activities play an important role in developing teamwork, leadership, communication skills and mutual understanding among students. articles.o: 147 RMG factories declared fully closed: BGMEA
articles.s: Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) President Mahmud Hasan Khan has said a total of 147 garment factories across the country have been declared fully closed amid ongoing protests by garment workers demanding a minimum wage. He disclosed the information while speaking t
articles.x: Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) President Mahmud Hasan Khan has said a total of 147 garment factories across the country have been declared fully closed amid ongoing protests by garment workers demanding a minimum wage. He disclosed the information while speaking to the media on Saturday afternoon. The BGMEA chief said a vested quarter is deliberately trying to create unrest in the garment sector. As a result, normal factory operations were being disrupted, seriously affecting the country’s major source of export earnings. He said 55 factories in Savar and Ashulia had to remain closed today (Saturday) under Section 13(1) of the Labour Act due to the workers’ unrest, which has continued for more than two weeks. Meanwhile, 92 factories are running partial production. He warned that continued unrest in the garment sector would make it difficult to continue discussions on wage increases at the wage board. However, business owners will present their wage proposal at the wage board tomorrow (Sunday). The BGMEA president also said that workers’ federations are failing to bring the situation under control. The post 147 RMG factories declared fully closed: BGMEA appeared first on Textile Focus .

articles.x: Rethinking shop-floor agility and eliminating hidden operational bottlenecks anchored a specialized technical seminar at the Textile Innovation Expo 2026 in Dhaka. Held at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB) on November 14, the session titled "Industrial Engineering for Smarter, Leaner and Efficient Apparel Manufacturing" explored how precision engineering can reshape garment production economics. The session attracted top industry leaders, industrial and production engineers, consultants, and technology experts to discuss modern approaches to reducing waste, optimizing line balancing, and improving delivery reliability in readymade garment (RMG) factories. Modern apparel manufacturers face intense pressure to enhance operational efficiency, product quality, and delivery speed while optimizing the use of manpower, materials, and machinery. Industrial engineers highlighted that common factory challenges—such as bottlenecks, excessive material handling, work-in-progress (WIP) buildup, line imbalances, and avoidable rework—often negate the advantages of expanding production capacity. During the session, speakers emphasized that implementing lean manufacturing principles, 5S methodologies, effective production planning, and digital line monitoring tools can successfully resolve these shop-floor inefficiencies. Experts noted that improving line balancing, reducing cycle times, and tracking real-time OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) metrics are vital for maintaining competitive margins in global markets.
