articles.x: Industry leaders and trade experts emphasized building a structured innovation ecosystem, accelerating supply chain data sharing, and strengthening industry-academia collaboration at a high-level plenary seminar in Dhaka today. Held at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB) on November 14 during the Textile Innovation Expo 2026, the session titled "Strategy for Systemic Innovation Implementation" brought together policymakers, factory executives, and global brand representatives. They discussed practical strategies to address high business costs, bank interest rates, and energy challenges while transitioning toward high-value manufacturing. Figure 1: The session titled "Strategy for Systemic Innovation Implementation" brought together policymakers, factory executives, and global brand representatives. Bangladesh's textile and apparel sector is entering a decisive transition ahead of LDC graduation, which will eventually end duty-free market access. Global sourcing dynamics are rapidly reshaping due to Fourth Industrial Revolution (IR4) technologies, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) rules, due diligence mandates, traceability, Digital Product Passport (DPP) requirements, and tariff uncertainty. Figure 2: Engr. ATM Mahbubul Alam Milton, Executive Director, Masco Group and Steering Board Member, Textile Innovation Exchange (TIE) Engr. ATM Mahbubul Alam Milton, Executive Director, Masco Group and Steering Board Member, Textile Innovation Exchange (TIE), delivered the keynote presentation. He highlighted various types of innovation, including open, incremental, radical, architectural, and disruptive innovation, and outlined a structured innovation model comprising idea generation, evaluation, impact assessment, R&D and testing, and commercialization.

articles.x: The Clothing Manufacturers Association of India (CMAI) and NIFT VisioNxt, a unit of the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), under the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, have joined hands to strengthen knowledge exchange, industry collaboration and professional capabilities in fashion forecasting and design. Speaking on the occasion, Santosh Katariya, President, CMAI, said, “The Indian apparel industry is operating in a market where consumer preferences, technology and design sensibilities are changing rapidly. articles.s: ANDRITZ will host the Sustainable Packaging Days 2027 on March 18–19, 2027, at the ANDRITZ France facility in Montbonnot, France. The event will bring together brand owners, converters, packaging producers, researchers, and technology providers to explore how renewable fibers and advanced production
articles.x: ANDRITZ will host the Sustainable Packaging Days 2027 on March 18–19, 2027, at the ANDRITZ France facility in Montbonnot, France. The event will bring together brand owners, converters, packaging producers, researchers, and technology providers to explore how renewable fibers and advanced production technologies can drive the transition away from fossil-based packaging materials. The transition toward more sustainable products and packaging is gaining momentum worldwide, driven by ambitious sustainability goals, new regulations, and growing demand for renewable and circular solutions. In the EU, for example, all packaging must be recyclable by 2030, while global initiatives are pushing for greater reuse, recycling and alternatives to fossil-based plastics. Cellulose can play an important role in this transition, offering renewable and recyclable opportunities across packaging, nonwovens and textiles. Collaboration across the entire ecosystem is key to driving this development forward. The Cellulose Valley Chair gathering in Grenoble in October is one recent example of how industry, academia, and research are connecting around cellulose-based innovation. For ANDRITZ, cellulose is more than a raw material. It is the common thread connecting expertise across pulp production, nonwovens, textiles, and packaging. From fiber processing technologies to innovative molded fiber applications, cellulosic fibers create opportunities to replace fossil-based materials with renewable and recyclable alternatives. This supports the company’s broader sustainability ambition: by 2030, more than 50% of total revenue is targeted to come from environmental impact solutions. articles.s: 영국 럭셔리 브랜드 버버리(Burberry)가 중국과 미국 시장의 판매 회복에 힘입어 영업흑자로 전환했다. 고가 제품 중심의 전략에서 벗어나 트렌치코트와 스카프 등 핵심 상품을 강화하고 가격대를 다변화한 경영 정상화 전략 ‘버버리 포워드(Burberry Forward)’가 성과를 내고 있다. 다만 중국 성장률 둔화와 현금 유출 확대는 향후 수익성 개선의 과제로 남았다.버버리가 11월 12일 발표한 2026/27 회계연도 상반기(3월 29일~9월 26일) 실적에 따르면 매출은 10억 9800만 파운드로 전년 동기 대비 6% 증가했다.

articles.s: The DSL presents Textile Innovation Awards 2026, by Textile Today, was held at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB), Dhaka, recognizing outstanding innovations that contribute to the p...
articles.x: The DSL presents Textile Innovation Awards 2026, by Textile Today, was held at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB), Dhaka, recognizing outstanding innovations that contribute to the productivity, competitiveness, and sustainability of Bangladesh's textile and apparel industry. Organized by Textile Innovation Exchange (TIE) in collaboration with the Institution of Textile Engineers and Technologists (ITET), the event was held in association with BKMEA and BGBA and implemented by Textile Today Innovation Hub. The evening began with an opening overview by Enamul Hafiz Latifee, Strategic and Reporting Lead, Textile Innovation Exchange was the Moderator and Anchor of the Textile Innovation Award. Following the introduction, Dr. Md. Hasib Uddin, Director of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), delivered the first welcome address. Figure 1: The event was graced by the presence of Honourable Member of Parliament Sanjida Islam Tulee Next, Mohammad Mofazzal Hosen Pabel, Managing Director and CEO of Dongyi Sourcing Limited (DSL), presented the second welcome address. A.S.M. Tareq Amin, Founder and CEO of the Textile Today Innovation Hub (TTIH) led both rounds of the award announcements then shared the vision behind the Textile Innovation Awards on behalf of Textile Today. The Textile Innovation Awards 2026 recognized 18 organizations across seven main categories, covering manufacturing, process, technology, product development, environmental sustainability, and HR and organizational development innovations. The awards were presented in two tiers based on the scores achieved during the evaluation process. articles.s: Industry experts have emphasized the need for Bangladesh’s textile wet processing sector to adopt low-water dyeing, digital printing and other advanced processing technologies to reduce resource consu...
articles.x: Industry experts have emphasized the need for Bangladesh’s textile wet processing sector to adopt low-water dyeing, digital printing and other advanced processing technologies to reduce resource consumption, improve production efficiency and meet growing sustainability requirements. The recommendations came at a technical seminar titled “New Generation Dyeing & Printing Processes”, held as part of the Textile Innovation Expo 2026 at Hall 08 (Expo Village, Innovation Demonstration Zone) of the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB), Dhaka. Figure 1: Distinguish guests of the seminar. The session brought together dyehouse managers, chemical innovators, academics and machinery suppliers to explore advanced technologies designed to reduce water, energy and chemical consumption while improving manufacturing performance. Md. Ashraful Alam, Director, Production (Printing), M.N. Dyeing, Printing & Washing Mills Ltd., and Dr. Mohammad Abbas Uddin Shiyak, Associate Professor, Department of Dyes and Chemical Engineering, Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX), delivered keynote presentations. Figure 2: Md. Ashraful Alam, Director, Production (Printing), M.N. Dyeing, Printing & Washing Mills Ltd., Ashraful Alam discussed overall traditional printing, printing processes, water issues, color preparation, and automatic color kitchens during the seminar. He highlighted the challenges of resource-intensive processes in the dyeing and printing sectors, particularly focusing on high water consumption. He explained how adopting an automatic color kitchen helps save significant amounts of water and allows for repeated reuse. articles.x: Global cotton markets are heading into 2026/27 with a wider supply gap. USDA’s November WASDE puts world consumption at 122.75 million bales against production of 117.48 million, a shortfall of about 5.3 million bales. Ending stocks are forecast to fall from 75.64 million to 70.57 million bales, the lowest level in 15 years. Unless global harvests are revised up sharply, this could support prices in the months ahead. Bangladesh and Vietnam, the world’s two largest cotton importers, are moving in different directions. Bangladesh’s consumption is forecast at 7.4 million bales and imports at 7.2 million, both cut again this month. Use is flat on last year and well below the 8.2 million bales of 2024/25. In my view, the main reason is energy. Falling domestic gas output, disrupted LNG imports from the Middle East and a fire at an LNG terminal left mills short of gas through the summer. Many spinning units ran well below capacity, some at under 30 percent, and others stopped altogether. The government’s recent decision to replace duty-free bonded imports of 10–30 count yarn with a bank-guarantee system was meant to shift demand to local spinners. Mills without steady gas could not take up that demand, while garment exporters now face higher input costs. Bangladesh’s ending stocks of 1.62 million bales, about 22 percent of annual use, are little changed from last year, as importers have cut purchases in line with lower mill use. Gas supply has improved since the summer crisis, but it remains short of demand and vulnerable to terminal outages, as the 4–7 November maintenance shutdown showed. articles.s: 일본 룸웨어 브랜드 젤라또 피케(gelato pique)가 산리오캐릭터즈와의 두 번째 협업 컬렉션을 11월 12일 국내에 선보였다. 기존 헬로키티와 시나모롤에 마이멜로디, 쿠로미, 리틀트윈스타를 추가해 총 5종의 캐릭터 라인업으로 확대했다.이번 협업은 지난 4월 선보인 ‘GELATO PIQUE ♡ Sanrio character’ 컬렉션에 이은 두 번째다. 브랜드 측에 따르면 첫 번째 컬렉션 당시 한국은 일본을 제외한 유일한 해외 판매국으로 선정됐으며, 국내 소비자를 위한 한정 제품은 선보인 지 이틀 만에 준비 물량이 소진됐다.두 번

articles.s: 여성 컨템포러리 디자이너 브랜드 에펠르(Ēpelle)가 11월 13일부터 26일까지 롯데백화점 인천점 2층에서 올해 네 번째 팝업스토어를 연다. 주요 백화점을 중심으로 오프라인 유통을 확대하는 가운데 겨울 주력 상품과 단독 선공개 상품을 선보인다.에펠르는 소재의 질감과 자연스럽게 흐르는 실루엣을 중심으로 디자인을 전개하는 브랜드다. 풍성한 텍스처와 섬세한 디테일, 편안한 착용감을 고려하면서 절제된 디자인을 지향한다.이번 팝업에서는 캐시미어 100% 니트웨어와 시어링 아우터 등 겨울 주요 상품을 집중적으로 구성했다. 울·캐시미어 니트

articles.o: HAMS Garments launches CITT for textile transformation with Textile Innovation Exchange
articles.s: HAMS Garments Ltd. has launched its Center of Intelligence for Textile Transformation (HAMS CITT) in collaboration with Textile Innovation Exchange (TIE) at the TIE–ITET Textile Innovation Expo 2026,...
articles.x: HAMS Garments Ltd. has launched its Center of Intelligence for Textile Transformation (HAMS CITT) in collaboration with Textile Innovation Exchange (TIE) at the TIE–ITET Textile Innovation Expo 2026, held at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB) in Dhaka. The initiative, incubated and implemented by TIE, aims to strengthen factory-level innovation by integrating shop-floor intelligence, production data, academic research and advanced technologies into a structured innovation ecosystem. Figure: HAMS Garments Ltd. has launched its Center of Intelligence for Textile Transformation (HAMS CITT) in collaboration with Textile Innovation Exchange (TIE) at the TIE–ITET Textile Innovation Expo 2026. Designed as an internally hosted innovation platform, HAMS CITT will connect factory operations with researchers, universities, technology providers, brands and industry experts to develop practical, scalable and measurable solutions to manufacturing challenges. Its objectives include advancing digitalization and automation across HAMS operations, improving workforce capabilities, supporting Digital Product Passport (DPP) readiness and strengthening product traceability. Under an agreement between HAMS Garments and TIE, TIE will support the center through six strategic service components: building institutional innovation capabilities; developing data readiness and decision-support systems; facilitating global innovation intelligence and technology adoption; coordinating applied research and sustainable product development; supporting the commercialization and wider adoption of innovations; and strengthening communication and global positioning. articles.o: Industry leaders discuss smarter, resource-efficient denim manufacturing
articles.s: A technical seminar titled “Technical Seminar on Denim & Denim Processing” was successfully held as part of the Textile Innovation Expo 2026. The event brings together denim manufacturers, brand r...
articles.x: A technical seminar titled “Technical Seminar on Denim & Denim Processing” was successfully held as part of the Textile Innovation Expo 2026. The event brings together denim manufacturers, brand representatives and technology solution providers to discuss practical innovations, production efficiency and sustainability in denim manufacturing. The session took place today from 4:30 PM to 5:10 PM at Hall 08 (Expo Village, Innovation Demonstration Zone) of the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB), Dhaka. The panel discussion was moderated by Shafiur Rahman, Country Manager, G-Star RAW and Steering Board Member of Textile Innovation Exchange (TIE). The distinguished panelists included Adil Hossain Chowdhury, Fabric Technical Manager, Next Sourcing BD; Mohammad Jamal Abdun Naser, Director (Operation), Shasha Denims Ltd.; Muhammad Amin, Chief Executive Officer, Ha-Meem Textile Zone (Denim & Woven); and Muhammad Naveed, Chief Marketing Officer, Jamuna Denims Ltd. The discussion focused on product development, process consistency and strategies to minimize unnecessary resource consumption and reprocessing. Speakers discussed how emerging technologies and solutions can be evaluated based on commercial requirements, actual production conditions and product quality. They also emphasized the importance of selecting appropriate innovations to address factory-level challenges and strengthening collaboration across the value chain, from fabric development and processing to final market delivery. A significant part of the discussion focused on reducing the industrial carbon footprint, carbon emissions, water consumption and steam consumption in denim production. The panelists shared technical insights into denim dyeing processes, nitrogen dyeing technologies and washing tech

articles.o: Industry experts call for greater use of synthetic and recycled fibres to boost textile competitiveness
articles.s: Industry experts have called for greater adoption of synthetic, new and recycled fibres to diversify Bangladesh’s textile and apparel products, strengthen export competitiveness and capture higher-val...
articles.x: Industry experts have called for greater adoption of synthetic, new and recycled fibres to diversify Bangladesh’s textile and apparel products, strengthen export competitiveness and capture higher-value international markets. The call came at a technical seminar titled “Innovation in the Use of Synthetic, New & Recycled Fibers”, held on 13 November as part of the Textile Innovation Expo 2026 at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB), Dhaka. The session took place at the Expo Village Innovation Demonstration Zone. Figure: The seminar brought together industry experts, manufacturers, academics and brand representatives to discuss practical innovations in synthetic, recycled and blended fibres, particularly their potential to help Bangladesh diversify beyond traditional cotton-based products. The seminar brought together industry experts, manufacturers, academics and brand representatives to discuss practical innovations in synthetic, recycled and blended fibres, particularly their potential to help Bangladesh diversify beyond traditional cotton-based products. Global fibre production reached a record 132 million tonnes in 2024, with synthetic fibres accounting for 69% of the total. Polyester alone represented 59%. However, despite growing demand from brands for sustainable alternatives, recycled fibres accounted for only 7.6% of global production, while textile-to-textile recycling remained below 1%. The discussion highlighted Bangladesh’s heavy dependence on cotton, which accounts for approximately 72.7% of the country’s garment exports, compared with the global average of 41.6%. articles.o: Data integrity and traceability key to Digital Product Passport readiness: Experts
articles.s: Industry experts have emphasized the importance of reliable product data, material traceability and supply chain coordination as Bangladesh’s textile and apparel sector prepares for emerging Digital P...
articles.x: Industry experts have emphasized the importance of reliable product data, material traceability and supply chain coordination as Bangladesh’s textile and apparel sector prepares for emerging Digital Product Passport (DPP) requirements. The discussion took place at a technical seminar titled “Preparing for Digital Product Passport & Beyond”, held as part of the Textile Innovation Expo 2026 at Hall 08 (Expo Village, Innovation Demonstration Zone) of the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB), Dhaka. Figure 1: The session brought together garment manufacturers, traceability specialists, supply chain leaders and brand representatives to discuss strategies for improving material transparency and digital data readiness. The session brought together garment manufacturers, traceability specialists, supply chain leaders and brand representatives to discuss strategies for improving material transparency and digital data readiness. Global textile and apparel supply chains face growing expectations to provide reliable and verifiable information about raw materials, manufacturing processes and final product performance. Speakers highlighted that preparing for a DPP involves much more than attaching a digital tag or QR code to a garment. It requires consistent records, traceable material flows, high-quality data and clearly defined responsibilities for sharing product information across complex supply chains. Figure 2: Dr. Aminul Haque, Chief Executive Officer of Montrims Ltd. The seminar also highlighted challenges arising from gaps between supplier records, factory production systems and buyer requirements, which could undermine product data integrity. articles.o: Open Innovation Zone by Centro highlights 18 research projects at Textile Innovation Expo 2026
articles.s: The Open Innovation Zone by Centro at the Textile Innovation Expo 2026 took place on November 12 at Hall 8 (Expo Village), International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB), Dhaka. Organized by Texti...
articles.x: The Open Innovation Zone by Centro at the Textile Innovation Expo 2026 took place on November 12 at Hall 8 (Expo Village), International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB), Dhaka. Organized by Textile Innovation Exchange and the Institution of Textile Engineers and Technologists (ITET), with the Open Innovation Zone, the event brought together industry leaders, researchers, and academic innovators. Figure1: Distinguished guests present certificates of participation to all 18 participating innovators at the Open Innovation Zone of the Textile Innovation Expo 2026 . Following a nationwide call for innovation proposals, the organizers received around 60 applications from various institutions. A panel of judges evaluated and mentored the applicants, shortlisting 18 projects to showcase their research, prototypes, and technological solutions at the dedicated Open Innovation Area. Figure 2: Tareq Amin, Member Secretary, Textile Innovation Exchange Tareq Amin, Member Secretary, Textile Innovation Exchange, opened the ceremony by sharing the background of the initiative. He noted that after collecting around 60 innovation proposals from across the country over several months, a dedicated panel of judges worked closely with the participants to mentor, develop, and shortlist the final 18 innovations. He also expressed his sincere appreciation to the judging panel for their extensive efforts in evaluating the projects and selecting the best innovation of the expo. Several industry leaders attended the ceremony as distinguished guests, including Fazlee Shamim Ehsan, President, Bangladesh Employers' Federation (BEF); Nafis-Ud-Doula, Director, Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), and Director, Impress-Newtex Composite Textiles Ltd.; and Engr. articles.s: 하고하우스가 전개하는 드파운드(depound)가 겨울 아우터 판매 증가와 함께 단독 매장 확대를 추진한다. 올해 롯데백화점 김포공항점·동탄점·광복점을 기존 하고하우스 입점 형태에서 드파운드 단독 매장으로 전환했으며, 현재 전국 24개 단독 매장을 기반으로 2027년에도 주요 상권에 매장을 늘릴 계획이다.드파운드는 배우 임윤아와 함께한 겨울 캠페인 이후 주요 아우터 판매가 늘었다고 12일 밝혔다. 지난 10월 19일 공개한 겨울 컬렉션의 대표 제품 ‘덤블 리버시블 점퍼’는 11월 첫째 주 판매량이 캠페인 공개 전 주 대비 약 303%

articles.s: 겨울 이너웨어의 경쟁 기준이 달라지고 있다. 얇은 한 겹으로 체온을 유지하는 발열·보온 기능을 넘어 하루 종일 피부에 닿는 소재의 촉감과 착용감, 수분 관리 기능까지 제품 선택의 주요 요소로 부상하고 있다. 겹쳐 입는 옷이 늘어날수록 가장 안쪽에 착용하는 이너웨어의 역할이 중요해지면서 소재와 원사 단계부터 차별화를 꾀하는 움직임이 주목된다.이러한 흐름 속에서 신성통상(대표 염태순)의 SPA 브랜드 탑텐(TOPTEN10)이 겨울 발열내의 ‘온에어(ON Air)’의 소재 경쟁력을 강화하며 시장 공략에 나섰다. 텐셀™ 모달과 컴팩트 원사

articles.x: Karl Mayer is preparing to introduce two new Jacquard double needle bar raschel machines at its in-house Product Show in Changzhou, China, held alongside ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026, from 20-24 November. Designed primarily for the footwear industry, the RDJ 7/3 and RDJ 6/2 promise greater productivity, flexibility and design freedom in the production of advanced spacer fabrics. Central to both developments is Karl Mayer’s new Wireless Jacquard technology, which simplifies machine operation while opening up new possibilities for fabric patterning, functionality and future machine configurations. The company claims the new machines can deliver productivity improvements of up to 70% compared with similar equipment on the market, while enabling manufacturers to produce increasingly sophisticated textile structures for footwear, sportswear and athleisure applications. Ahead of the exhibition, Karl Mayer’s Ulrike Schlenker explores the latest developments with Kay Hilbert, Global Head of Design Fabrics & Specials at Karl Mayer, who explains how the company is responding to changing market requirements and where he sees the greatest potential for future innovation. US: What are the principal market requirements driving the development of your new RDJ machines? KH: Our new Jacquard double needle bar raschel machines are specifically designed to meet the needs of the footwear industry, where efficient production, flexibility and design versatility are increasingly important. The RDJ 7/3 and RDJ 6/2, which we are presenting at our Product Show at Karl Mayer (China), are extremely versatile and up to 70% more productive than comparable machines currently available. articles.o: TIE–ITET Textile Innovation Expo 2026 opens to showcase Bangladesh’s industrial innovation
articles.s: The TIE–ITET Textile Innovation Expo 2026 opened today at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB), Dhaka, bringing together textile manufacturers, technology providers, industry leaders,...
articles.x: The TIE–ITET Textile Innovation Expo 2026 opened today at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB), Dhaka, bringing together textile manufacturers, technology providers, industry leaders, engineers, researchers, and international stakeholders to showcase innovations and explore opportunities for technological advancement in Bangladesh’s textile and apparel industry. Figure 1:TIE–ITET Textile Innovation Expo 2026 opens to showcase Bangladesh’s industrial innovation. The three-day expo, running from November 12 to 14 at ICCB Hall 8, aims to strengthen the industry's global competitiveness through engineering excellence, industrial innovation, automation, resource efficiency, and sustainable manufacturing. In welcome speech, Engr. ASM Hafizur Rahman Nixon, Secretary General of The Institution of Textile Engineers & Technologists (ITET), emphasized the vital role of textile innovation in ensuring the future growth and global standing of Bangladesh’s apparel and textile sector. During his remarks, he highlighted the necessity of adopting advanced manufacturing technologies, sustainable practices, and continuous research to transition the industry toward high-value-added production. He also underscored how collaborative platforms like the Textile Innovation Expo bridge the gap between academia, technologists, and industry leaders to drive long-term resilience and modernization. The ceremony was then chaired by Engr. Ehsanul Karim Kaiser, Chairman of Textile Innovation Exchange (TIE). Enamul Hafiz Latifee, Strategic and Reporting Lead at TIE, anchored and moderated the session. The systems, which have been in operation… The post Barmag’s single-stage Bi-Shrinkage concept impresses with yarn quality and efficiency appeared fir
articles.x: The Indian company Garden Silk Mills Pvt. Ltd. adopts Barmag’s new single-stage Bi-Shrinkage Yarn (BSY) spinning concept based on WINGS FDY PLUS eco. The systems, which have been in operation for about a year, deliver excellent yarn quality with very good productivity. Due to the increasing demand for specialty yarns, particularly in the Indian market, Garden Silk Mills Pvt. Ltd. retrofitted 24 positions of its WINGS FDY polyester machines last year for the production of Bi- Shrinkage yarns. The decisive factor for the investment was Barmag’s single-stage process: Based on the WINGS FDY PLUS eco, this concept enables BSY production of up to 16 yarn ends at much higher speeds than two-stage BSY-concepts. Based on the WINGS FDY PLUS eco, Barmag’s single-stage concept enables BSY production of up to 16 yarn ends at much higher speeds than two-stage BSY-concepts. Maximum flexibility through fully separated processes The solution developed by Barmag stands out thanks to its special process flow, which allows for independent adjustment of yarn properties. After drawing, POY and FDY yarns are plied, intermingled, and finally wound onto a bobbin as BSY. The special yarn path and low friction ensure high yarn evenness and high-quality tangle knots. Incidentally, the WINGS’ characteristic simple setup ensures low waste rates even in the BSY process. Shashi Sharma, Chief Operating Officer and Group Project Head at Garden Silk Mills Pvt. Ltd., a long-standing Barmag customer, considers the retrofit a success: “The quality of the yarn is excellent. At the same time, we benefit from the efficiency advantages of the single-stage process. The exhibition will provide a platform for compan
articles.x: Registration is now open for Techtextil North America 2027, which will take place from 11-13 May 2027 in Atlanta, Georgia, bringing together manufacturers, suppliers and industry professionals from across the technical textiles and nonwovens sectors. The exhibition will provide a platform for companies to explore new materials, manufacturing technologies and sourcing opportunities, while addressing the performance, efficiency and sustainability challenges facing a wide range of industrial markets. Visitors will be able to examine high-performance fibres, technical fabrics, composites and nonwovens, with opportunities to evaluate materials first-hand and identify solutions for specific product development and manufacturing requirements. A key focus will be connecting buyers and product developers with material suppliers and technology specialists, enabling discussions around manufacturing capabilities, technical specifications and potential partnerships. The event will also highlight developments in technical textile applications across automotive, aerospace, medical, filtration and industrial markets, where demand for advanced materials continues to create opportunities for innovation. For manufacturers and product developers, the exhibition offers an opportunity to investigate technologies that can improve durability, functionality and production efficiency, while identifying emerging applications for technical textiles and nonwovens. Organised by Messe Frankfurt, Techtextil North America is an established industry platform serving the North American technical textiles market. The expanded workspace also features dedicated areas for product demonstrations, customer meetings, technical training, and collaborative discussions. articles.s: 세왕섬유 최재락 회장은 지난 11일 서울 삼성동 섬유센터에서 열린 ‘제40회 섬유의 날’ 기념식에서 금탑산업훈장을 수훈했다. 최재락 회장은 국내 생산기반을 유지하면서 친환경·고기능성 원단 개발과 수출 확대를 이끌고 스마트 제조혁신을 통해 국내 섬유산업 경쟁력을 높인 주역이다.최 회장은 44년간 섬유산업에 종사하며 품질혁신과 고부가가치 섬유소재 개발에 주력해 왔다. 국내 염색업계 최초로 블루사인(Bluesign) 인증을 획득하고 국내 섬유업계 최초로 글로벌 아웃도어 브랜드 파타고니아(Patagonia)에 원단을 공급하며 친환경·고기능

articles.s: 신성통상(대표 염태순)의 남성복 브랜드 지오지아(ZIOZIA)가 브랜드 앰버서더 주우재, 크리에이터 침착맨과 이어온 출근룩 콘텐츠를 겨울 상품 기획으로 확장했다. 11월 11~26일 전국 지오지아 매장과 자사몰 굿웨어몰에서 두 사람의 화보 착장을 포함한 2026 가을·겨울 신상품 36개 스타일로 ‘직데이’를 진행한다.두 사람과의 협업은 지난 4월 침착맨 유튜브 채널의 ‘직장인 패션 훈수두기’ 콘텐츠에서 시작됐다. 주우재가 직장인의 실제 패션 고민을 바탕으로 침착맨에게 출근룩 스타일링을 제시한 콘텐츠다. 지오지아에 따르면 영상은 공개

articles.o: 외국인 방한 이천만 시대, K패션 유통 지형 바뀐다
articles.s: 방한 외국인 관광객이 사상 처음으로 연간 2,000만 명을 돌파하면서 국내 패션산업의 유통 지형이 달라지고 있다. 과거 명품과 면세점 중심이었던 외국인 쇼핑 수요가 국내 디자이너 브랜드와 캐주얼웨어, 패션 편집숍 등으로 확대되면서 K패션 매장이 새로운 관광 목적지로 부상했다. 특히 주요 패션 매장을 찾은 외국인 관광객의 소비가 주변 음식점과 카페, 의류 매장으로 이어지는 현상도 확인되고 있다. 외국인 관광객 증가가 개별 브랜드의 판매 확대를 넘어 지역 상권의 소비 구조와 패션 유통기업의 출점 전략에도 영향을 미치고 있는 것이다.패션

articles.o: More flexible airbag fabric, more airbag design options
articles.s: As vehicle interiors evolve and safety systems become more complex, airbag modules are being asked to fit into less space while still meeting demanding performance requirements. Cushion design is a careful balance of pack size, performance, manufacturability and cost. So, what happens when the fibre
articles.x: As vehicle interiors evolve and safety systems become more complex, airbag modules are being asked to fit into less space while still meeting demanding performance requirements. Cushion design is a careful balance of pack size, performance, manufacturability and cost. So, what happens when the fibre itself gives engineers more design flexibility? On 15 December, Jenna Ott, Global Nylon Fiber R&D Director at Invista, will explore that question in a free 30-minute webinar introducing Invista Ultra-fine 1 dpf Nylon 6,6 fibre. © Invista The session will look at how a finer filament structure changes the way airbag fabric behaves, and what those differences could mean for future cushion and module design. Using comparative test data across 1 dpf Nylon 6,6, conventional 3 dpf and 6 dpf Nylon 6,6, as well as 3 dpf PET, Jenna will examine the relationships between fabric feel, packability and air permeability – and the design possibilities they may open up. For engineers working in airbag cushions, modules, materials or restraint systems, it’s a concise look at what a more flexible fabric could make possible. Event details 15 December 2026 | 10:00 am ET / 4:00 pm CET | 30 minutes | Live | Free Register for the webinar The post More flexible airbag fabric, more airbag design options appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

articles.o: Benninger to present advanced solutions for dyeing and processing at India ITME 2026
articles.s: Benninger, a complete system supplier with leading technologies for continuous wet processing and discontinuous dyeing, offers proven solutions that meet the needs of Indian textile manufacturers, who are under growing… The post Benninger to present advanced solutions for dyeing and processing at In
articles.x: Benninger, a complete system supplier with leading technologies for continuous wet processing and discontinuous dyeing, offers proven solutions that meet the needs of Indian textile manufacturers, who are under growing pressure to process a wider range of fabrics faster while using less water, energy and chemicals. At ITME 2026, Benninger presents FabricMaster, SynthMaster and CPB Knit – reliable solutions for demanding woven and knitted articles, from sportswear and heavy jersey to sensitive synthetic blends and high-value underwear fabrics. In every dyehouse, some articles place considerably greater demands on the machinery than others. Fabrics may mark easily, develop uneven shades or require longer processing times. As fashion cycles shorten and product diversity increases, the ability to process demanding qualities reliably is becoming an important competitive advantage for Indian mills serving both domestic and export markets. Benninger FabricMaster: versatile dyeing, from sportswear to heavy jersey Discontinuous dyeing is one area in which fabric quality and machine performance are particularly closely linked. Processors must handle an increasingly diverse range of woven and knitted fabrics while reducing cycle times, water consumption and energy use. The ability to switch efficiently between fabric qualities without compromising colour consistency is therefore essential. Benninger addresses these requirements with the FabricMaster jet dyeing machine. It processes woven and knitted fabrics marks rope-mark-free, including articles that are difficult or impossible to process on other machines. articles.o: Born Slippy challenges conventional wetsuit insulation
articles.s: A new made-to-measure wetsuit developed with British big-wave surfer Andrew Cotton uses micro-chamber insulation technology in place of conventional fleece linings, in an attempt to improve thermal performance without adding bulk. The Aptus 1.0 wetsuit has been developed by Born Slippy, a new techni
articles.x: A new made-to-measure wetsuit developed with British big-wave surfer Andrew Cotton uses micro-chamber insulation technology in place of conventional fleece linings, in an attempt to improve thermal performance without adding bulk. The Aptus 1.0 wetsuit has been developed by Born Slippy, a new technical watersports brand founded by British entrepreneur Charles Gadsdon, who is based in Valencia, Spain. Combining Japanese Yamamoto neoprene with an engineered micro-chamber insulation structure incorporated into the torso panels, the suit has been designed to address the competing requirements of warmth, flexibility and fit in cold-water surfing. Conventional wetsuits rely on the insulating properties of neoprene, with additional thermal linings increasingly used to improve warmth. These extra layers, however, can add bulk and potentially restrict freedom of movement. Born Slippy’s alternative approach employs a micro-chamber structure designed to retain warmth around the chest and back without requiring a conventional fleece lining. The company has combined this construction with Yamamoto limestone-based neoprene, selected for its flexibility and thermal properties. The wetsuit also incorporates glued, blindstitched and triple-taped seams to limit water ingress and improve durability under demanding surfing conditions. Individual fit A second distinguishing feature is the use of individual body measurements rather than conventional standard sizing. Each Aptus 1.0 wetsuit is manufactured to order using 26 measurements to create a personalised pattern, with the objective of minimising gaps between the suit and the wearer’s body. Fit is particularly important to wetsuit thermal performance because excess space can allow cold water to circulate between the neoprene and the skin

articles.o: Get Into Pole Position For ITMA 2027: Pre-Register For Germany’s Textile Technology Delegations
articles.s: BERLIN — November 11, 2026 — International textile manufacturers are invited to express their interest now in the Global Textile Technology Mission, taking place in Germany from 12 to 17 September 2027. Ahead of ITMA 2027 in Hanover, these thematic delegations will offer selected participants the op
articles.x: BERLIN — November 11, 2026 — International textile manufacturers are invited to express their interest now in the Global Textile Technology Mission, taking place in Germany from 12 to 17 September 2027. Ahead of ITMA 2027 in Hanover, these thematic delegations will offer selected participants the opportunity to visit leading VDMA textile machinery member companies and textile research institutes at their own premises — discovering innovation at its source before continuing their technology conversations at the exhibition. The initiative is a part of the Foreign Market Entry Programme for SMEs, financed by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy, and supported by the VDMA Textile Machinery Association. The programme is organised by COMMIT Project Partners in cooperation with InfoAid and supported by VDMA Textile Machinery. Interested companies are now invited to pre-register their participation by no later than 11 December 2026 on commit-group.com/ITMA-2027/ Four routes to explore technology at its source The programme is organised around four core technology routes, enabling participants to indicate the areas most relevant to their business: Spinning, Winding & Nonwovens Knitting, Weaving & Braiding Dyeing, Finishing, Coating & Process Control Textile Recycling & Circularity Company visits will provide first-hand insights into where and how textile machinery technology is developed and manufactured. Research institutes will present their fields of research and approaches to technology transfer, connecting industrial practice with research expertise. articles.o: Recognition for Nuyarn’s proprietary wool process
articles.s: A new open-net wool fabric construction developed by Nuyarn Technologies, headquartered in Levin, New Zealand, in collaboration with Japan’s Takisada Corporation, received a 2026 Performance Days award for textile innovation. The development is designed to maximise breathability and manage moisture
articles.x: A new open-net wool fabric construction developed by Nuyarn Technologies, headquartered in Levin, New Zealand, in collaboration with Japan’s Takisada Corporation, received a 2026 Performance Days award for textile innovation. The development is designed to maximise breathability and manage moisture in vapour form, opening up potential applications ranging from lightweight summer running and endurance sportswear to base layers for demanding alpine conditions. It is produced with Nuyarn’s proprietary twist-free spinning technology which differs from conventional wool yarn production by avoiding the tight twisting of fibres that can restrict their natural performance characteristics. The technology is designed to preserve more of wool’s inherent elasticity, moisture management and thermal regulation properties while improving fabric durability and reducing weight. Combined with a new open-net construction, it offers fabric developers an alternative approach for achieving the ventilation and moisture management required in high-intensity performance apparel, while retaining the advantages of natural fibres. The fabric is 67% Merino wool and 33% polyamide, weighing just 105gsm and is said to dry up to five times faster than conventional Merino, with abrasion resistance up to 8.8 times higher. There is a growing interest in wool-based alternatives to synthetic performance fabrics, particularly for applications in which comfort, temperature regulation and moisture management are essential. “This award reflects our ongoing drive to push the boundaries of performance textiles,” said Andy Wynne, CEO of Nuyarn Technologies. “Alongside our partners at Takisada Corporation, it demonstrates what’s possible when strong partnerships come together.” www.nuyarn.com The post Recognition f

articles.o: Dyeing excellence for every fabric challenge
articles.s: Swiss textile machinery manufacturer Benninger will showcase advanced dyeing technologies for knitted and woven fabrics at India ITME 2026, addressing growing demand for flexible, resource-efficient processing across the Indian textile industry. At the exhibition, the company will present its Fabric
articles.x: Swiss textile machinery manufacturer Benninger will showcase advanced dyeing technologies for knitted and woven fabrics at India ITME 2026, addressing growing demand for flexible, resource-efficient processing across the Indian textile industry. At the exhibition, the company will present its FabricMaster, SynthMaster and CPB Knit systems, designed to handle demanding textiles, ranging from sportswear and heavy jersey to sensitive synthetic blends and high-value underwear fabrics. As fashion cycles shorten and fabric diversity increases, textile manufacturers face mounting pressure to reduce processing times and resource consumption without compromising quality. Benninger says its technologies offer solutions to these challenges, particularly for fabrics susceptible to marking, uneven dyeing or extended processing cycles. FabricMaster The FabricMaster jet dyeing machine is designed for versatile discontinuous processing of knitted and woven fabrics, including articles that are difficult to handle using conventional equipment. Applications include heat-set polyester sportswear, smooth viscose-elastane blends and heavy cotton jersey. Its intelligent liquor circulation, efficient penetration, high rope speeds and gentle fabric transport enable shorter processing cycles while minimising rope marks and reducing water and energy consumption. The system allows manufacturers to switch between different fabric qualities while maintaining consistent dyeing results. The FabricMaster jet dyeing machine. © Benninger For more sensitive materials, Benninger offers the FabricMaster horizontal jet dyeing machine, developed specifically for fabrics prone to compression marking. articles.t: AEI는 새로운 완전 전기식 Monforts 제품군의 이점을 누리고 있습니다.
articles.o: AEI reaps the benefits of all-electric new Monforts range
articles.s: The impact of the rising cost of energy on the textile industry has been well documented, with some European countries paying up to seven times more to run their manufacturing operations than in other regions of the world. In France, however, powering plants with electricity offers particular advant
articles.x: The impact of the rising cost of energy on the textile industry has been well documented, with some European countries paying up to seven times more to run their manufacturing operations than in other regions of the world. In France, however, powering plants with electricity offers particular advantages, since the national energy system is already structured around low-carbon generation. With a large share of electricity produced from nuclear power alongside growing renewable capacity, French industry can also operate with a significantly lower emissions profile than in many other countries. Seeking to benefit as much as possible from this situation, AEI – Ateliers d’Ennoblissement d’Irigny – has recently installed a new six-chamber Montex stenter line from Monforts which is 100% electrically powered. Bespoke configuration With a working width of 3.2 metres, the new Montex line has a bespoke configuration with extended inlet arms, enabling the processing of fabrics in widths from 70 centimetres and weights ranging from 15 to 1,000gsm. It replaces a machine originally installed in the 1980s and represents a significant step forward in both efficiency and sustainability. In addition to being fully electrically heated, the new stenter is equipped with an integrated heat recovery system, forming part of a long-term energy efficiency plan that has also included the installation of an electric transformer to replace the previously gas-powered system. “We continue to monitor our consumption through targeted management and this new Montex stenter will significantly reduce our carbon emissions thanks to 100% electric power and the energy recovery system,” says general manager Céline de Montigny. “In addition, it allows for safe operation for our operators, with carefully designe

articles.o: Circulose resumes operations
articles.s: Circulose has restarted commercial-scale production at its plant in Ortviken in Sundsvall, Sweden, marking a significant step in scaling next-generation materials for the global fashion industry. The Ortviken plant is the world’s first commercial-scale chemical textile recycling facility and its res
articles.x: Circulose has restarted commercial-scale production at its plant in Ortviken in Sundsvall, Sweden, marking a significant step in scaling next-generation materials for the global fashion industry. The Ortviken plant is the world’s first commercial-scale chemical textile recycling facility and its restart demonstrates that the fashion industry is seeking ways to scale proven solutions that move beyond pilots and into commercial production. In 2024, under new ownership by private equity firm Altor, Circulose set a renewed strategic direction focused on securing volume commitments from partner brands to bring Circulose fibre back to market at scale. “Our focus has been to align the production restart with confirmed demand,” says executive chair Helena Helmersson. “With commitments from 16 brands, and more on the way, we are now there. Today Circulose is backed by leading brands and fibre producers, has an organisation of around 130 people with deep expertise where it matters, and a plant ready to produce.” After two years leading the restart, CEO Jonatan Janmark and the board have decided that this is the right moment to hand over to a new leader for the next phase. CFO Amanda Geijer has been appointed interim CEO until a permanent CEO is in place. “When Jonatan joined, Circulose had just been given a second chance,” says Helena Helmersson. “Since then, he has made Circulose a leading player in textile-to-textile recycling again. That has taken a lot of energy, creativity and teamwork. On behalf of the board and our owners, I want to thank him for everything he has built.” www.circulose.com The post Circulose resumes operations appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

articles.x: ATLANTA, GA— November 10, 2026 — A fabric is no longer defined simply by what it covers. In today’s industrial landscape, it may need to withstand extreme conditions, reduce weight, improve protection, support filtration, or deliver functions once associated with entirely different materials. As performance expectations expand across industries, so does the need for specialized materials, technical expertise, and manufacturing solutions. Registration is now open for Techtextil North America 2027, returning May 11–13 to the Georgia World Congress Center in Atlanta, Georgia. The event will bring together the technical textiles and nonwovens industry at a time when material selection and manufacturing capabilities are increasingly central to product development and industrial performance. A Closer Look at the Materials Behind Modern Manufacturing The role of technical textiles continues to expand across aerospace, automotive, medical, construction, filtration, protective applications, and industrial manufacturing. With each application comes a different set of requirements, from thermal resistance and strength-to-weight performance to durability, flexibility, and production efficiency. For companies developing products or evaluating new manufacturing capabilities, finding the right material is only part of the equation. Understanding how it performs, how it is processed, and whether it can meet production requirements is just as important. At the centre of the campaign is Jingle, a black and white terrier featured on a limited-edition seaso
articles.x: British heritage knitwear manufacturer John Smedley has launched Heart of the Home, a festive campaign celebrating the warmth, familiarity and sense of belonging associated with the holiday season. At the centre of the campaign is Jingle, a black and white terrier featured on a limited-edition seasonal knit. Made from 100% fine merino wool, the garment combines a playful festive design with the natural fibres and craftsmanship for which the British brand is known, reflecting its emphasis on quality knitwear designed to be worn year after year. To bring Jingle to life beyond knitwear, John Smedley has collaborated with award-winning artist and fashion illustrator Jess Rose Bird, who has created her own interpretation of the character. Her bespoke, hand-drawn installation will feature in the windows of the brand’s Jermyn Street boutique in London, unveiled during a festive gathering for friends of the company. Scottish-born and London-based, Bird is recognised for her expressive illustration style, using paint, chalk pastel and charcoal to capture movement and character. Her previous clients include Prada, Versace, Harrods and Vivienne Westwood. © John Smedley The Heart of the Home campaign also includes a content series featuring the dogs belonging to John Smedley employees. Staff from across the business will share stories about their pets and the companionship they bring to everyday life, extending the campaign’s theme of home and belonging. Customers and followers are also invited to share stories about their own dogs using the hashtag #HeartOfMyHome. Bangladesh's textile and apparel industry faces a major policy challenge. Disputes over cotton yarn imports show a growing tension in the sector. The government wants to protect local spinning mills and their heavy investments. At the same time, garment exporters need cheap raw materials to stay competitive in global markets. Balancing these two needs has become difficult for policymakers. The issue gained heightened attention following a November 9 meeting between Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and industry leaders. He directed an inter-ministerial committee, led by Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, Minister for Commerce, Industry, and Textiles & Jute, to submit recommendations by November 20. The committee is reviewing the bonded warehouse system and analyzing practices adopted by competing nations. The core dispute stems from the National Board of Revenue's (NBR) September 7 decision to withdraw bonded warehouse import facilities for 10–30 count cotton yarn under specific customs classifications. articles.o: John Hogg acquires Nanoflam
articles.s: Manchester-based speciality chemicals group John Hogg Technical Solutions has acquired UK textile coatings specialist Nanoflam, further expanding its portfolio of flame retardants, functional finishes and processing chemicals for technical textile applications. The acquisition follows John Hogg’s pu
articles.x: Manchester-based speciality chemicals group John Hogg Technical Solutions has acquired UK textile coatings specialist Nanoflam, further expanding its portfolio of flame retardants, functional finishes and processing chemicals for technical textile applications. The acquisition follows John Hogg’s purchase of Avocet Dye and Chemical in November 2024 and represents another step in the group’s strategy of building a diversified textile chemicals business through complementary technologies and specialist manufacturing capabilities. Nanoflam specialises in water-based textile coatings, halogen-free flame retardants and blackout and dimout technologies for applications for furnishing fabrics, transport interiors, outdoor textiles and advanced building materials. Its product range is supported by expertise in emulsion polymer chemistry and the development of customised formulations. Complementary technologies The acquisition is particularly significant in the flame-retardant textile coatings market, where manufacturers face increasingly demanding requirements for fire performance, durability and compliance with environmental regulations. articles.s: SUNDSVALL, Sweden — November 10, 2026 — Circulose announced its restart of commercial-scale production plant at Ortviken in Sundsvall, Sweden, marking a significant step in scaling next-generation materials for the global fashion industry. The Ortviken plant is the world’s first commercial-scale che
articles.x: SUNDSVALL, Sweden — November 10, 2026 — Circulose announced its restart of commercial-scale production plant at Ortviken in Sundsvall, Sweden, marking a significant step in scaling next-generation materials for the global fashion industry. The Ortviken plant is the world’s first commercial-scale chemical textile recycling facility. Its restart demonstrates that the fashion industry is seeking ways to scale proven solutions that move beyond pilots and into commercial production. In 2024, under new ownership by private equity firm Altor, Circulose set a renewed strategic direction focused on securing volume commitments from partner brands to bring CIRCULOSE® back to market at scale. “Our focus has been to align the production restart with confirmed demand. With commitments from 16 brands, and more on the way, we are now there. Today Circulose is backed by leading brands and fiber producers, has an organization of around 130 people with deep expertise where it matters, and a plant ready to produce,” says Helena Helmersson, Executive Chair of Circulose. With the Ortviken plant back in operation, Circulose continues supplying fashion brands and fiber producers with high-quality recycled raw material at commercial scale, supporting industry efforts to divert textile waste from landfills and incineration. After two years leading the restart, CEO Jonatan Janmark has, together with the Board, decided that this is the right moment to hand over to a new leader for the next phase. CFO Amanda Geijer has been appointed interim CEO until a permanent CEO is in place. She will be supported by Helena Helmersson in the role of Executive Chair. “When Jonatan joined, Circulose had just been given a second chance. articles.o: European restructuring drives recovery for Indorama
articles.s: Indorama Ventures has removed approximately 3.5 million tons of production capacity through the closure or restructuring of ten manufacturing sites since 2023, with the majority of the affected operations in Europe. The Bangkok, Thailand-headquartered chemicals and fibres group says the rationalisat
articles.x: Indorama Ventures has removed approximately 3.5 million tons of production capacity through the closure or restructuring of ten manufacturing sites since 2023, with the majority of the affected operations in Europe. The Bangkok, Thailand-headquartered chemicals and fibres group says the rationalisation has helped eliminate approximately $298 million in annual fixed costs compared with 2023, contributing to a sharp recovery in profitability despite lower production volumes. Announcing its financial results for the first nine months of 2026 on November 9th, Indorama reported a 63% year-on-year increase in EBITDA to approximately $1.3 billion, while its EBITDA margin improved from 8% to 11%. The improvement came despite a 5% decline in sales volumes, partly reflecting the company’s deliberate withdrawal from less competitive manufacturing operations and its decision to align production more closely with demand. The restructuring forms part of Indorama’s IVL 2.0 transformation programme, which is intended to establish a leaner, more competitive global manufacturing network. Overcapacity The company specifically identifies Europe as the principal location of its capacity reductions, with its Combined PET (CPET) and Fibers divisions particularly affected by structural difficulties in the aromatics market and persistent industry overcapacity. These pressures have forced Indorama to concentrate production at its most competitive facilities while withdrawing from operations that can no longer deliver acceptable returns. The scale of the restructuring is significant. articles.x: By MK Prabhakar Surat-based Kansal Spinning Mills Private Limited has established itself as a manufacturer of a wide range of natural and synthetic yarns. Kansal Spinning Mills is part of the diversified Kansal Group, with interests spanning yarn trading, spun yarn, fabrics and real estate. We caught up with Ayush Kansal, Director, Kansal Spinning Mills, for an exclusive chat, to learn more about the company’s journey, product portfolio, manufacturing capabilities and future plans. Ayush Kansal, Director, Kansal Spinning Mills A Strong Textile Legacy Kansal Spinning Mills may have been established only in 2023, but the group behind it has a much longer association with the textile industry. “Kansal Spinning Mills was established in 2023. But we were not new to textiles. The Kansal Group, which was established in 1988, has always been a well-known name in the textile industry. Yarn trading has been one of our key businesses, and we were also pioneers in the introduction of texturizing machines,” Ayush said. The experience gained over decades in textile trading and allied businesses has helped the company understand changing customer requirements and build a diverse product portfolio. A Wide Product Basket One of the major strengths of Kansal Spinning Mills is the variety of yarns it offers. The company works with both natural and synthetic fibres and caters to several segments of the textile industry. “We offer a huge product basket, ranging from natural fibres such as linen blends to synthetic fibres such as polyester, rayon fibres, aramid and other technical textile yarns. We cater to a wide range of applications, including home furnishings, technical textiles, weaving, garmenting and filtration,” Ayush explained. Through this partnership, A.T.E. will… The post A.T.E. Group broadens textile digitalis
articles.x: A.T.E. Enterprises Private Limited has joined hands Smartex AI, a Portugal-based technology company specialising in artificial intelligence (AI)-powered fabric inspection and digital factory management solutions. Through this partnership, A.T.E. will promote Smartex AI’s solutions to the Indian textile industry, supporting manufacturers in strengthening quality control, improving production visibility, and advancing factory digitalisation. As textile manufacturing evolves towards greater automation and data-driven operations, consistent fabric quality and access to real-time production information are becoming increasingly important. Smartex AI addresses these needs through AI and machine learning-based inspection technology that identifies fabric defects in both knits and woven fabrics in real time, along with digital tools that provide visibility into production performance and quality. The Smartex AI system uses high-resolution cameras, sensors, and advanced light analysis to detect fabric defects and irregularities during production. Its digital factory management platform enables manufacturers to monitor production output, machine productivity, and quality-related information, supporting more informed operational decisions. For A.T.E., the partnership represents a further step in expanding its portfolio of technology solutions for the textile industry. With its established presence across the textile value chain and experience in introducing global technologies to Indian manufacturers, A.T.E. will work towards making these solutions accessible to textile mills seeking to strengthen quality assurance and operational efficiency. articles.o: ShinWon Accelerates AI Transformation with New ERP System SPHERE
articles.s: – Integrates end-to-end operations across order management, product development, sourcing, production, logistics and finance through SAP S/4HANA– Standardizes business processes across headquarters and overseas subsidiaries to enhance global operational efficiency– Expands AI transformation initiati
articles.x: – Integrates end-to-end operations across order management, product development, sourcing, production, logistics and finance through SAP S/4HANA – Standardizes business processes across headquarters and overseas subsidiaries to enhance global operational efficiency – Expands AI transformation initiatives through demand forecasting and workflow automation powered by integrated ERP data ShinWon Accelerates AI Transformation with Integrated ERP System ‘SPHERE’ ShinWon Corporation (CEO: JJ Park), a global apparel manufacturer, is strengthening its global manufacturing competitiveness through the implementation of SPHERE, a next-generation integrated Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system. The initiative marks a significant step in the company’s efforts to unify enterprise-wide business data and accelerate its AI transformation (AX). Built around SAP S/4HANA, SPHERE integrates key business systems, including Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), Supplier Relationship Management (SRM), Manufacturing Execution System (MES), e-Accounting and SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC). The platform connects the entire apparel manufacturing process—from order management and sample development to costing, sourcing, procurement, production, logistics, shipment and settlement—through a unified data framework. By consolidating workflows and data previously managed across spreadsheets, emails and standalone applications, ShinWon has established standardized business processes centered on SAP. The system also improves data consistency and accessibility at the product level, enabling more systematic management of Bills of Materials (BOM) and production processes for individual styles. articles.o: Textile innovation from India wins Global Change Award
articles.s: Stockholm City Hall is no stranger to big ideas. Ahead of the Nobel Prize banquet returning to the Blue Hall in December, ten Global Change Award winners took the stage… The post Textile innovation from India wins Global Change Award appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
articles.x: Stockholm City Hall is no stranger to big ideas. Ahead of the Nobel Prize banquet returning to the Blue Hall in December, ten Global Change Award winners took the stage last night. One of the winners is Agro-Lyocell from India – turning agricultural waste into textile fibres, aiming to make more of an existing resource while creating new opportunities for farmers. Each year, ten winners receive a EUR 200,000 grant from H&M Foundation to develop their early-stage innovation. What made Agro-Lyocell stand out among thousands of applications was their way of challenging where the textile industry looks for raw materials. Agro-Lyocell turns agricultural waste into textile fibres, aiming to make more of an existing resource while creating new opportunities for farmers. In India, around 90 million tonnes of crop residue are burned every year. Meanwhile, the textile industry continues to rely on wood-based fibres that put pressure on forests. Agro-Lyocell responds to both challenges by turning overlooked materials like linseed residue into new fibres. “Every year, millions of tonnes of agricultural waste are burned while the industry cuts down trees for fibre. We’re connecting those two problems and turning waste into a resource”, says Shreyans Kokra, CEO Canvaloop. Shreyans Kokra, CEO Canvaloop Agricultural waste is emerging as a valuable raw material for textiles. Agro-Lyocell uses a part that is often overlooked: the dense, woody fraction of crop residue. While the natural fibres can already be used in textiles, Agro-Lyocell turns the remaining woody material into a new textile fibre, offering an alternative to conventional lyocell made from wood pulp. articles.x: The Retailers Association of India (RAI) held the fourth edition of its Kochi summit on October 28, 2026, at Radisson Blu Kochi. The event was organised in close association with the Kerala Management Association (KMA) and welcomed an encouraging turnout from across the retail ecosystem. The summit provided a platform for retailers, brand owners, technology providers and management professionals to share perspectives and build new partnerships. Deliberations focused on the priorities that are steering the sector, including brand positioning, social and visual commerce, retail innovation, emerging technologies and digital growth strategies. Keynote addresses and moderated expert panels brought depth and direction to the conversations. Sharing his thoughts on the occasion, Kumar Rajagopalan, CEO, Retailers Association of India (RAI), said, “ Kerala is a particularly interesting retail market because the distinction between urban and rural consumption is less pronounced than in many other states. With a large Malayali diaspora worldwide, consumers are familiar with international shopping trends and have high expectations of quality, choice, and service. Retailers understand these expectations and are adapting. Combined with strong regional businesses and growing opportunities beyond the major cities, this makes Kerala an exciting market for retail growth. At RAI, we look forward to supporting this growth by connecting retailers with industry knowledge, new opportunities and each other .” The Kochi Retail Summit 2026 added to the ongoing dialogue between industry, institutions and partners in Kerala. Honourable President of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh, Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir , attended the inaugural session as the Chief Guest. articles.o: AEI invests in all-electric Monforts stenter
articles.s: French textile finishing specialist AEI – Ateliers d’Ennoblissement d’Irigny – has installed a new fully electric Monforts MONTEX stenter line as part of its strategy to improve energy efficiency, reduce emissions and strengthen its domestic manufacturing capabilities. The six-chamber stenter, with
articles.x: French textile finishing specialist AEI – Ateliers d’Ennoblissement d’Irigny – has installed a new fully electric Monforts MONTEX stenter line as part of its strategy to improve energy efficiency, reduce emissions and strengthen its domestic manufacturing capabilities. The six-chamber stenter, with a working width of 3.2 metres, replaces equipment dating from the 1980s and represents a significant investment in modernising AEI’s finishing operations near Lyon. The investment takes advantage of France’s predominantly low-carbon electricity supply, which is supported by nuclear generation and growing renewable energy capacity. With energy costs remaining a major challenge for European textile manufacturers, electrification offers French producers opportunities to reduce their environmental impact while improving operational efficiency. The new MONTEX line features a bespoke configuration with extended inlet arms, enabling AEI to process fabrics from 70 centimetres in width and weighing between 15 and 1,000gsm. This flexibility supports the company’s extensive range of textile finishing applications. In addition to its fully electric heating system, the stenter incorporates integrated heat recovery technology to minimise energy consumption. The installation forms part of AEI’s wider efficiency programme, which has included replacing its previous gas-powered system with an electric transformer. “We continue to monitor our consumption through targeted management and this new MONTEX stenter will significantly reduce our carbon emissions thanks to 100% electric power and the energy recovery system,” says AEI general manager Céline de Montigny. “In addition, it allows for safe operation for our operators, with carefully designed ergonomics to minimise handling strain, while ens

articles.x: German textile machinery manufacturer Brückner will showcase its latest energy-efficient finishing technologies at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026 in Shanghai, China, from 20-24 November, highlighting solutions designed to reduce energy consumption, lower emissions and improve production efficiency. With rising energy costs, increasingly stringent environmental requirements and growing competitive pressure, textile manufacturers are seeking ways to make their finishing operations more sustainable and cost-effective. Brückner will demonstrate how its machinery and process technologies can help manufacturers address these challenges while maintaining high standards of fabric quality. A key focus will be the company’s established heat recovery and exhaust air purification systems, which enable textile finishers to recover valuable energy from production processes while reducing emissions. These technologies can significantly lower overall energy requirements and operating costs, while helping manufacturers comply with environmental regulations. Brückner will also highlight the latest generation of its Power-Frame stenter, which combines high-quality fabric finishing with a range of energy-saving features. Optimised airflow systems, efficient burner technology, intelligent controls and automation solutions are designed to minimise energy consumption while maintaining productivity and process reliability. articles.o: Addressing a common challenge in cold-weather running
articles.s: Lululemon has developed a new cold-weather running vest combining PrimaLoft synthetic insulation with strategically positioned mesh panels to regulate heat and moisture during exercise. The Ventscape PrimaLoft ThermoPlume+ Run Vest, unveiled at the China International Import Expo on November 6th, fe
articles.x: Lululemon has developed a new cold-weather running vest combining PrimaLoft synthetic insulation with strategically positioned mesh panels to regulate heat and moisture during exercise. The Ventscape PrimaLoft ThermoPlume+ Run Vest, unveiled at the China International Import Expo on November 6th, features a patent-pending construction designed to balance thermal insulation and ventilation as the wearer’s activity level changes. The development addresses a common challenge in cold-weather running, when the insulation required at the beginning of a run can become uncomfortable as physical exertion increases and the body generates more heat and moisture. Rather than requiring runners to remove or adjust layers, the Ventscape design uses a combination of insulating fill and mesh ventilation zones to maintain a more consistent microclimate around the body. PrimaLoft ThermoPlume+ synthetic insulation provides warmth during the initial stages of exercise, while strategically positioned mesh panels allow air to circulate as the runner’s pace and body temperature increase. The resulting airflow helps remove accumulated heat and humidity from inside the garment, reducing the risk of overheating during more intensive activity. Optimising construction Lululemon used modelling and simulation to investigate different combinations of insulation and mesh, seeking to establish an optimal balance between warmth and breathability. Thermal mannequin testing was subsequently employed to assess the performance of the insulation under windy conditions and at simulated running speeds. The development programme involved more than 250 hours of testing over 2,500 kilometres, combining laboratory evaluations with outdoor wear trials. articles.t: Unspun과 Arvind가 협력하여 3D 직조 확장
articles.o: Unspun and Arvind partner to scale 3D weaving
articles.s: US fashion technology company unspun has entered into a strategic partnership with Arvind, one of India’s leading textile and apparel manufacturers, to bring OneWeave 3D weaving technology into industrial-scale apparel production. The agreement marks Arvind’s first installation of OneWeave technolog
articles.x: US fashion technology company unspun has entered into a strategic partnership with Arvind, one of India’s leading textile and apparel manufacturers, to bring OneWeave 3D weaving technology into industrial-scale apparel production. The agreement marks Arvind’s first installation of OneWeave technology and the first time unspun’s 3D weaving platform will move beyond its own microfactory into the production environment of a major global apparel manufacturer. Under the partnership, Arvind will initially deploy two OneWeave machines at its facility in Ahmedabad, India, with operations expected to begin by December 2026. The phased agreement also provides a pathway for more than 30 additional machines across India and North America in 2027-28, depending on demand from global apparel brands. Unspun will provide installation, commissioning, training, software and ongoing service and support, while brands will contract directly with Arvind to manufacture garments using the technology. Demand for the new capacity is already building, with a pipeline of leading global apparel brands preparing programmes. With initial capacity limited to the first two machines, production slots will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. Direct yarn-to-garment production OneWeave technology weaves yarn directly into three-dimensional garment forms, eliminating conventional two-dimensional fabric production and most cutting and sewing operations. A trouser leg can be woven in approximately ten minutes, with each machine capable of producing around 20,000 pairs of trousers annually. The technology is designed to enable faster, more flexible apparel manufacturing while significantly reducing material waste and production complexity. articles.o: Redesigning paper machine press felts
articles.s: German technology group Voith is incorporating Econyl regenerated nylon from Italy’s Aquafil into its paper machine press felts, as part of a wider effort to improve the recyclability of industrial textiles without compromising their performance. Press felts are essential components in paper manufac
articles.x: German technology group Voith is incorporating Econyl regenerated nylon from Italy’s Aquafil into its paper machine press felts, as part of a wider effort to improve the recyclability of industrial textiles without compromising their performance. Press felts are essential components in paper manufacturing, where they remove water from the paper web under high mechanical pressure and must maintain their dimensional stability and performance over extended operating periods. Traditionally manufactured from combinations of different polyamides and smaller quantities of other materials, these highly engineered textiles present considerable challenges when it comes to recycling at the end of their working lives. Voith is now seeking to address these challenges through both the introduction of regenerated polyamide 6 (PA6) and a redesign of the material structures used in its press felts. Mechanical performance A critical requirement has been ensuring that regenerated nylon can withstand the extreme mechanical stresses encountered in paper manufacturing. “From a technical perspective, the decisive factor was that Econyl regenerated nylon provides a quality and performance level equal to virgin nylon,” explains Lidia Loskan, R&D project manager for sustainability at Voith. “For press felts, this is essential because the material must withstand extreme mechanical stress while maintaining stability, durability and reliable performance.” Voith carried out extensive internal evaluations before selecting the material. Previous trials with mechanically recycled polyamides had failed to deliver the required performance, but Econyl successfully met the company’s technical requirements. articles.x: Three years after its launch in English, Spanish, French and Turkish, Barmag’s Digital Academy online training center for the BCF process is now also available in Chinese. Online training courses disrupt production processes less than in-person events, are more targeted, and are available more quickly. 450 active users have already recognized the benefits of Barmag’s digital classroom for themselves. Most of them are based in the U.S.; with the launch of the Chinese version, this offering is now accessible to an even larger customer base. Taicang Universal Fibers Co. Ltd. is already taking advantage of the opportunity to train its employees at the machine to ensure optimal machine operation. “With the Digital Academy, we can provide our employees with optimal support and further increase the efficiency of our equipment,” says Tom Yu, Facility Manager at Taicang Universal Fibers. Customers using other Barmag and Neumag processes are also set to benefit from the Digital Academy. The training program for the POY process is just about to be rolled out. Online training courses for the staple fiber process are currently in preparation. Digital learning is the future The online training center, available on the e-commerce platform myBarmag.com, offers a wide range of e-learning modules on the operation, maintenance, and repair of the Neumag BCF S+ and S8 systems. The training program is aimed at operators, process engineers and technicians, as well as quality managers. The advantage of the Digital Academy: Compact, role-based learning units accessible via mobile and desktop devices allow users to quickly apply the content. articles.o: Sourcing Velvet and Burnout Fabric from China: A Buyer’s Checklist
articles.s: Velvet has quietly moved from occasion wear into year-round programs: burnout velvet dresses, devore blouses, upholstery-grade pile for hospitality projects. Demand is up, and so is the number of suppliers claiming they can make it. Having spent the last decade on the mill side in Zhejiang, here is
articles.x: Velvet has quietly moved from occasion wear into year-round programs: burnout velvet dresses, devore blouses, upholstery-grade pile for hospitality projects. Demand is up, and so is the number of suppliers claiming they can make it. Having spent the last decade on the mill side in Zhejiang, here is what actually separates a workable velvet order from an expensive lesson. First, agree on which “velvet” you are buying The word covers at least three different constructions, and the price gap between them is wider than most buyers expect. Knitted velour is the volume product – a loop or cut-pile knit, usually polyester/spandex, cheap per meter, stretchy, and the default for casualwear and costumes. Woven velvet has a proper warp pile on a woven ground, which is why it drapes instead of clinging. Burnout velvet is a woven or knit pile fabric that has been chemically etched. Ask for the construction, not the trade name. A supplier who answers “velvet” to a construction question is a trader, not a mill. Ask for GSM, pile height in millimeters, and the ground composition. A 280 GSM pile and a 180 GSM pile look identical in a photo and behave nothing alike on a cutting table. Burnout velvet is a chemical process, not a print This is where most sourcing mistakes originate. Burnout – devore in French – works because sodium hydroxide destroys cellulose fibers while leaving polyester intact. The pattern is not printed on; it is eaten into the cloth. Two consequences follow. First, the fabric must be a blend of cellulose and synthetic – typically polyester/cotton or polyester/viscose. A 100% polyester cloth cannot be burnt out, no matter what the supplier claims.
