articles.o: TERROT ADVANCES HIGH-PERFORMANCE CIRCULAR KNITTING FOR PREMIUM MATTRESS AND UPHOLSTERY FABRICS AT ITMA ASIA 2026
articles.s: The UCC 672-ME combines electronic three-way needle selection on cylinder and dial with exceptional design flexibility, production efficiency and application-driven textile innovation. Terrot Textilmaschinen GmbH, the German circular knitting machinery manufacturer and a premium engineering provider
articles.x: The UCC 672-ME combines electronic three-way needle selection on cylinder and dial with exceptional design flexibility, production efficiency and application-driven textile innovation. Terrot Textilmaschinen GmbH, the German circular knitting machinery manufacturer and a premium engineering provider within the Santoni China Group, will showcase its UCC 672-ME at ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026 in Shanghai, China. Designed for premium mattress ticking, upholstery and other demanding textile applications, the double electronic circular knitting machine combines independently programmable three-way needle selection on both cylinder and dial with high production output and extensive patterning capabilities. The technology enables manufacturers to develop sophisticated, double-sided fabric structures while increasing design flexibility and supporting efficient, application-specific textile manufacturing. Dual-sided technology expands design possibilities At the heart of the UCC 672-ME is electronic three-way needle selection on both cylinder and dial. By independently programming knit, tuck and miss actions at every feeder on both needle systems, manufacturers can create intricate jacquard patterns, three-dimensional textures, ventilation zones and reversible fabric structures with extensive design freedom. At ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026, Terrot will highlight a 38-inch UCC 672-ME configured in E20 gauge with 88 feeders and electronic three-way selection on both needle systems. The exhibition machine features a specialized mattress-fabric concept combining differentiated fabric zones, comfort-oriented construction and ventilation structures on both fabric sides. articles.o: ZSK brings AI-powered production analysis to embroidery
articles.s: Embroidery machine manufacturer ZSK has introduced an open API and direct integration with Anthropic’s Claude AI platform to its MY.ZSK 4.0 monitoring system, allowing manufacturers to analyse production data and build their own performance dashboards without programming expertise. The development i
articles.x: Embroidery machine manufacturer ZSK has introduced an open API and direct integration with Anthropic’s Claude AI platform to its MY.ZSK 4.0 monitoring system, allowing manufacturers to analyse production data and build their own performance dashboards without programming expertise. The development is intended to make the extensive operating data generated by industrial embroidery machines more accessible to production managers, enabling them to identify inefficiencies, investigate recurring problems and compare performance across machines, shifts and manufacturing sites. Every connected ZSK machine generates information on stitch counts, operating speeds, thread breaks, downtime, setup times and individual embroidery designs. While this information has previously been accessible through the company’s MY.ZSK monitoring portal, the new API allows it to be integrated into manufacturers’ own enterprise resource planning (ERP), manufacturing execution systems (MES) and other production management tools. Natural language The integration with Claude takes this a stage further by allowing users to interrogate the data through natural language commands rather than having to develop their own software. Production managers can, for example, ask which embroidery designs are responsible for the most thread breaks, how much production time is lost during colour changes or whether a particular order is likely to meet its delivery deadline. Claude can retrieve and analyse the relevant machine data and present the results as charts or complete web-based dashboards, incorporating key performance indicators, machine comparisons and production trends over periods of seven, 30 or 60 days. articles.x: From November 20 to 24, 2026, the Trützschler Group will present its latest fiber processing technologies at ITMA Asia in Shanghai, China. Visitors are invited to meet our experts in Hall 5.1, Booth D20 and discover solutions designed to increase productivity, simplify operations and support greater efficiency across spinning preparation and nonwoven production. Key highlights include the automated can transport system T-CAN, the next-generation card TC 30, innovative card clothing solutions such as STEELTOP and SUPERFLOW, as well as advanced nonwoven technologies for hygiene, wipes and filtration applications. T-CAN is Trützschler’s automation solution designed to reduce labor dependency and support greater automation in spinning mills. Trützschler Spinning At ITMA Asia 2026, Trützschler Spinning will showcase technologies that help spinning mills increase productivity, improve operational efficiency and make better use of valuable raw materials. A key highlight will be T-CAN, Trützschler’s automated can transport system. Designed to reduce labor dependency and support greater automation in spinning mills, T-CAN automates sliver transport throughout spinning preparation. It connects cards and drawing passages while ensuring reliable material allocation. By reducing manual handling and supporting continuous production, the system helps lower labor requirements, minimize downtime and improve operational efficiency. Visitors will also have the opportunity to learn more about the next-generation card TC 30 . Customers achieve up to 40% higher productivity in man-made fiber applications while maintaining or even improving yarn quality. articles.x: The growing importance of bio-based materials in performance apparel was a central theme at the latest Functional Fabric Fair in Portland, Oregon, which attracted record attendance and more than 350 exhibitors. Held at the Oregon Convention Center from October 26-28th, the event recorded a 7% increase in attendance compared with its autumn 2025 edition, with a sold-out exhibition hall that included more than 50 companies participating for the first time. The exhibition, organised by Functional Fabric Fair powered by Performance Days, brought together textile suppliers, apparel manufacturers, designers and sourcing specialists to explore material developments for the autumn/winter 2027/28 season. A particular emphasis was placed on bio-based materials as the performance apparel industry seeks alternatives to fossil-derived fibres and finishes, while addressing increasingly demanding requirements for durability, functionality and environmental performance. The programme examined not only the potential of renewable raw materials, but also the practical challenges involved in bringing new technologies to commercial scale, including feedstock availability, traceability and certification. Cellulose Forum A new Cellulose Forum was introduced to highlight developments in natural and regenerated cellulosic fibres, ranging from hemp, flax and nettle to lyocell, modal and viscose. It joined established forums dedicated to cotton and wool, reflecting growing interest in the performance potential of natural and renewable materials. Other specialist areas explored advances in garment construction, finishing technologies and functional fabrics for sportswear, outdoor clothing, bodywear and workwear. On 27 August 202
articles.x: A national programme backed by bulk procurement and carbon revenue could make the switch to energy-efficient BLDC fans affordable for low-income households Key takeaways Household fans for space cooling alone account for up to 5,212 megawatts (MW) of Bangladesh’s summer power demand. Yet energy-efficient brushless direct current (BLDC) fans make up less than 2% of household fans. Replacing energy-inefficient household fans with BLDC fans could cut summer power demand by up to 2,590MW and avoid over USD4 billion in future investment in coal-fired plants. It could also save 6,913 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of electricity a year, worth BDT89.87 billion (USD0.73 billion). Households lack information on the availability of BLDC fans and their energy-saving potential. In addition to raising awareness, the Sustainable and Renewable Energy Development Authority (SREDA) should finalise standards and labels for fans to nudge consumers towards efficient models. The government could design a national programme to cut the upfront cost of BLDC fans through bulk procurement and recycle the programme’s carbon revenue to make them affordable for low-income households. Household fans add up to 5,212 megawatts (MW) to Bangladesh’s summer power demand, with usage peaking around 9PM. On 27 August 2026, the country’s peak demand hit 19,027MW at 9PM. Replacing energy-inefficient fans with the energy-efficient brushless direct current (BLDC) models could cut peak demand by up to 2,590MW, according to a new report by the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA). articles.t: Shantnu Nikhil의 John Jacobs x S&N: 인도 패션과 이탈리아 디자인의 만남
articles.o: John Jacobs x S&N by Shantnu Nikhil: Indian Couture Meets Italian Design
articles.s: Shantnu and Nikhil make their first-ever foray into eyewear with a collaboration with John Jacobs for a bold, fashion-forward collection, now available at Lenskart stores. Two distinct design worlds. One statement-making collaboration. John Jacobs joins forces with celebrated couturiers Shantnu and
articles.x: Shantnu and Nikhil make their first-ever foray into eyewear with a collaboration with John Jacobs for a bold, fashion-forward collection, now available at Lenskart stores. Two distinct design worlds. One statement-making collaboration. John Jacobs joins forces with celebrated couturiers Shantnu and Nikhil’s pret label, S&N by Shantnu Nikhil, to launch a 32-piece eyewear collection that marks the designers’ first-ever venture into eyewear. Bringing together John Jacobs’ Italian design sensibilities and S&N’s distinctive design language, the collection reimagines iconic eyewear through bold design, elevated detailing and a strong point of view. Inspired by The Shape of India , the collection draws from the spirit of influential Indian leaders whose eyewear became symbols of conviction, intellect and authority. Reinterpreted for a new generation, these timeless forms get a contemporary, fashion-forward edge. The details make the statement. From the iconic S&N mark on the curve of the frame to precision metal streak detailing across the temples, every element is designed to stand out. The finishing touch? S&N’s iconic navy blue and cherry-red tape accents, tucked into the folding hinges. Together, these signature details give the range a distinctive identity, bringing the unmistakable S&N aesthetic to eyewear. Spanning eyeglasses and sunglasses across wayfarers, aviators, round frames and bold square silhouettes, the collection explores rich colours, premium refined materials and statement-making shapes. Designed to move effortlessly from everyday dressing to occasion wear, these frames bring a new edge to festive outfits, wedding looks and everything in between. Launching right in the middle of the festive season, the collection makes eyewear more than the finishing touch.

articles.o: Linking the modern mill’s islands of data
articles.s: While the textile industry has spent much of the past decade digitalising individual parts of its manufacturing chain, connecting them all together represents the next big challenge, according to the latest ITMA 2027 textile machinery exhibition blog. Design systems, product lifecycle management (PL
articles.x: While the textile industry has spent much of the past decade digitalising individual parts of its manufacturing chain, connecting them all together represents the next big challenge, according to the latest ITMA 2027 textile machinery exhibition blog. Design systems, product lifecycle management (PLM), enterprise resource planning (ERP), production planning, manufacturing execution systems (MES) and individual machines can all generate increasingly sophisticated data. Too often, however, it all remains trapped within separate systems. Few companies illustrate the potential of doing things differently as dramatically as Shein. The fashion giant’s rapid-response business model has been built around a highly digitalised supply chain connecting information on consumer demand with suppliers and manufacturing. “We reimagined the supply chain, which is a daunting task, and we’ve done it by digitising the small and medium-sized factories to give them visibility to see their own capacity, continued order flow and seamless efficiency,” Shein executive chairman Donald Tang has explained. Shein uses data analytics to test products in small initial batches and respond rapidly to actual demand, scaling production up or down accordingly. Whatever the wider debate surrounding the ultra-fast-fashion model, its approach demonstrates the competitive possibilities when information can move quickly between previously separate parts of the supply chain. Separate evolutions This principle is becoming increasingly relevant to textile manufacturers and not simply to meet demands for greater efficiency. articles.t: EU, 부직포 덤핑에 강경 대응
articles.o: EU gets tough on nonwovens dumping
articles.s: The European Commission has imposed definitive anti-dumping duties on imports of PET spunbond nonwovens originating in China, a decision welcomed by European industry association EDANA. The measures, published on October 30th, 2026, follow the introduction of provisional duties on May 12th. Effectiv
articles.x: The European Commission has imposed definitive anti-dumping duties on imports of PET spunbond nonwovens originating in China, a decision welcomed by European industry association EDANA. The measures, published on October 30th, 2026, follow the introduction of provisional duties on May 12th. Effective from October 31st for a period of five years, the definitive duties range from 39.8% to 48.1%. The Commission’s investigation concluded that Chinese imports had increased significantly during the period examined and were being sold at unfairly low prices, causing substantial harm to the EU PET spunbond industry. It also determined that the introduction of anti-dumping measures was in the wider interests of the European Union. The duties are intended to restore fair competition and safeguard European production capacity. “We welcome the Commission’s decision to impose definitive anti-dumping measures,” said Jacques Prigneaux, market analysis and economic affairs director at EDANA. “The adoption of definitive anti-dumping duties sends an important signal that the Commission is determined to effectively address unfair trade practices on the EU market. “Restoring fair competition is essential not only for safeguarding EU production, but also for supporting the investments in innovation, sustainability and employment that are required to meet the EU’s strategic industrial ambitions.” EDANA said it would continue working with EU and national customs authorities to monitor the implementation of the measures and ensure their effective application. The association also welcomed the Commission’s investigation and its commitment to maintaining fair market conditions within the European Union. www.edana.org The post EU gets tough on nonwovens dumping appeared first on Innovation in Tex

articles.s: Fakir Technologies Ltd. has signed an agreement with FKL Spinning Mills Ltd. for the implementation of a 6.13 MWp On-grid Solar Power Project, in collaboration with Solar EPC Development Ltd. The agre...
articles.x: Fakir Technologies Ltd. has signed an agreement with FKL Spinning Mills Ltd. for the implementation of a 6.13 MWp On-grid Solar Power Project, in collaboration with Solar EPC Development Ltd. The agreement marks a significant milestone in the journey towards delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions and supporting sustainable industrial development in Bangladesh. With an estimated first-year electricity generation of 8,238 MWh, the project is expected to avoid approximately 5,520 tonnes of CO₂ emissions annually. For FKL Spinning Mills Ltd., this initiative represents a major step towards reducing its environmental footprint, strengthening energy sustainability and embracing cleaner energy alternatives. For Fakir Technologies Ltd., the project further demonstrates its growing capabilities in delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions for the industrial sector. Since 2022, the company has been actively operating in Bangladesh's solar energy and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) sectors, building its expertise through global technology partnerships, project execution and integrated energy solutions. The project is being undertaken by Fakir Technologies Ltd., with Solar EPC Development Ltd. serving as its EPC partner. This 6.13 MWp project further reinforces Fakir Technologies' commitment to supporting industries in their transition towards cleaner, more efficient and sustainable energy systems. The agreement signing ceremony was held at Fakir Knitwears Ltd., Narayanganj, in the presence of senior leadership from both organizations. articles.o: Americhem acquires Noble Biomaterials
articles.s: US-based polymer specialist Americhem has acquired Noble Biomaterials, the developer of antimicrobial and conductive technologies for textiles and other soft surface applications. The acquisition brings Noble’s specialist technologies into Americhem’s global operations, strengthening the ability to
articles.x: US-based polymer specialist Americhem has acquired Noble Biomaterials, the developer of antimicrobial and conductive technologies for textiles and other soft surface applications. The acquisition brings Noble’s specialist technologies into Americhem’s global operations, strengthening the ability to support customers from initial product development through to commercial-scale production. Noble supplies proprietary materials technologies for applications in apparel, textiles, healthcare, aerospace and defence. Its established Ionic+, X-Static and Circuitex platforms provide antimicrobial, odour control and electrical conductivity functions, supported by US manufacturing operations and an extensive intellectual property portfolio developed over more than two decades. The acquisition will strengthen Americhem’s position in functional fibres and polymer solutions, particularly in healthcare and other markets requiring advanced material performance. “This is an exciting step forward for Americhem as we continue to invest in high-growth, high-demand markets,” said Americhem CEO John Richard. “Noble Biomaterials brings exceptional capabilities in antimicrobial solutions, strong commercial relationships and a reputation for quality that aligns with our values.” The financial terms of the acquisition were not disclosed. www.americhem.com www.noblebiomaterials.com The post Americhem acquires Noble Biomaterials appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

articles.s: Trident Limited has approved a ₹4,650-crore expansion and modernisation programme across its yarn, sheeting, paper and renewable energy businesses. Cleared by the board on November 2, 2026, the projects are… The post Trident powers ahead with ₹4,650-crore expansion drive appeared first on The Textil
articles.x: Trident Limited has approved a ₹4,650-crore expansion and modernisation programme across its yarn, sheeting, paper and renewable energy businesses. Cleared by the board on November 2, 2026, the projects are scheduled for completion in stages between December 2027 and September 2029, with funding through internal accruals and debt. Mr. Rajinder Gupta, Chairman, Trident Group The largest investment, ₹1,660 crore, will go towards a new yarn manufacturing facility at Dhar, Madhya Pradesh, with a capacity of 1,99,680 spindles. Trident has already acquired 179.2 acres of leasehold land for the project at an approximate cost of ₹106.09 crore. The facility is expected to be completed by September 30, 2029. At its existing yarn facility in Budhni, Madhya Pradesh, the company will invest ₹1,022 crore in expansion and modernisation, targeted for completion by December 31, 2027. The programme includes the addition of 99,840 spindles, replacement of 48,000 older spindles with 70,176 new spindles for finer-count yarns, and replacement of 960 older rotors with 2,400 new rotors. Trident’s existing yarn operations across Sanghera, Punjab, and Budhni have 7,46,064 spindles, 5,424 rotors and 320 air-jets. Capacity utilisation at Budhni stands at 94%. The sheeting business will receive ₹1,018 crore for the addition of 336 looms, taking its loom capacity from 504 to 840. Scheduled for completion by January 31, 2028, the expansion comes against reported capacity utilisation of 58%. In paper, Trident plans to invest ₹296 crore to add 28 tonnes per day, increasing manufacturing capacity from 479 to 507 tonnes per day. articles.o: Three innovations recognised at AVK Composites Awards
articles.s: Three developments in lightweight construction, automated manufacturing and advanced fibre reinforcement have taken first places in the three categories of the 2026 AVK Innovation Awards, presented at the JEC Composites Talks DACH held in Cologne, Germany, on October 20th. Organised by AVK, the Germ
articles.x: Three developments in lightweight construction, automated manufacturing and advanced fibre reinforcement have taken first places in the three categories of the 2026 AVK Innovation Awards, presented at the JEC Composites Talks DACH held in Cologne, Germany, on October 20th. Organised by AVK, the German Federation of Reinforced Plastics, the annual awards recognise advances in composite products, manufacturing processes and scientific research. Products and applications Dresden-based Anybrid secured first place in the products and applications category for a heavy-duty diamond core drill incorporating a carbon fibre-reinforced thermoplastic body in place of conventional steel. Developed with partners including Avanco Composites, Mitsui Chemicals Europe, AFPT, Hilti Kunststofftechnik and TU Dresden, the component has combined laser-based tape winding with injection moulding to produce a lightweight structure with integrated metal connections. The resulting drill assembly achieves a weight reduction of approximately 70% compared with steel, at least doubles service life and reduces its carbon footprint by around 37%. The development has successfully completed mechanical testing and practical field trials. Processes and manufacturing CompriseTec won the processes and methods category for a robotic manufacturing technology that eliminates the need for conventional moulds when producing thermoplastic composite components. Developed with the Hamburg University of Technology’s Institute of Aircraft Production Technology and Invent, the process employs two cooperating robots to shape heated, continuous fibre-reinforced thermoplastic sheets into complex geometries. articles.x: At ITMA ASIA 2026, KARL MAYER will demonstrate its expertise in processing staple fibers during warp preparation and will return to where this technology belongs: the Weaving Hall, at Booth 3/A24. The focus here will be on the latest-generation WARPDIRECT direct warping machine, featuring various yarn tensioners, as well as the sophisticated HSB Size Box – the centerpiece of the innovative PROSIZE sizing machine. Figure 1: The WARPDIRECT Both technologies are aimed specifically at manufacturers of high-quality goods in the commodity sector. "Our machines produce warp beams of the highest quality with high process efficiency. This offers particular advantages to textile manufacturers who are focused on generating real added value in a highly competitive market," says Enzo Paoli, President of the Warp Preparation Business Unit at KARL MAYER. WARPDIRECT: With the highest speed to precision warp beams Since its launch at the end of last year, the WARPDIRECT 2.0 has already been successfully deployed worldwide. Its performance is particularly valued in India, but also in China and Europe. Its strengths include identical warping lengths for all warp beams and high production output. In practice, warping speeds of up to 1,200 m/min are achieved. Figure 2: Enzo Paoli , President of the Warp Preparation Business Unit at KARL MAYER In addition, the current machine version stands out thanks to an upgrade to the press roll system. The change from hydraulic to electric operation reduces maintenance requirements while ensuring precise warping quality. In combination with an optimal yarn depositing device, this results in completely cylindrical beams with precise yarn arrangement. articles.o: JRC proposes EU-wide rules to boost textile reuse and remanufacturing
articles.s: The European Commission's Joint Research Centre (JRC) has proposed harmonized end-of-waste (EoW) criteria for textile, textile-related and footwear waste to support reuse and remanufacturing across th...
articles.x: The European Commission's Joint Research Centre (JRC) has proposed harmonized end-of-waste (EoW) criteria for textile, textile-related and footwear waste to support reuse and remanufacturing across the European Union. The technical report, published on 26 October 2026, aims to reduce regulatory differences among member states and establish common conditions for recovered textiles to re-enter the market as products rather than waste. Figure: Under the revised Waste Framework Directive, Member States must establish separate collection systems for used textiles from 2025. Courtesy: Collected The proposal addresses a regulatory gap in Europe's circular textile value chain. Currently, differences in national waste classifications create uncertainty for waste-management operators, textile sorters, reuse platforms, remanufacturers and downstream buyers. A harmonized framework could make it easier for businesses to handle recovered materials and trade reusable textile products across national borders. The European Environment Agency (EEA) estimated that the EU generated 6.95 million tons of textile waste in 2020, equivalent to around 16 kg per person. Of this amount, 82% came from post-consumer textiles, including used clothing and household textiles. Around 11.6 kg per person ended up in mixed household waste, while only 4.4 kg was collected separately for reuse and recycling. The challenge extends beyond waste collection. According to the EU's revised Waste Framework Directive, less than 1% of clothing waste is currently used to produce new clothing through textile-to-textile recycling. articles.x: CLEARWATER, Fla.— November 3, 2026 — PCP Ventures LLC, a Florida-based investor group, announced that it completed the acquisition of Pellon on October 1. Pellon is a globally recognized textile brand that makes specialty materials used in everything from clothing and quilts to home décor and crafts. Pellon’s products help give finished items shape, support, softness and cushioning, and include interfacings, stabilizers, batting, fiberfill, foams and other specialty fabrics. The company, which employs approximately 95 people, produces its products at a 220,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Clearwater, Florida. The brand’s products are often described as the “Magic in the Middle” characterized as the hidden yet essential materials inside a project that provide the support, structure, and functionality needed to bring the finished product together. Under PCP Ventures, Pellon will continue providing products for do-it-yourself sewing enthusiasts through stores such as Walmart, Hobby Lobby and Michael’s. The company sees tremendous potential in expanding its reach to users in other industries. The market is vast, given that Pellon’s products can be used in apparel, quality, sewing, furniture and a wide range of consumer applications. articles.x: Dhaka, 3 November 2026: Fakir Technologies Ltd. has signed an agreement with FKL Spinning Mills Ltd. for the implementation of a 6.13 MWp On-grid Solar Power Project , in collaboration with Solar EPC Development Ltd. The agreement marks a significant milestone in the journey towards delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions and supporting sustainable industrial development in Bangladesh. With an estimated first-year electricity generation of 8,238 MWh , the project is expected to avoid approximately 5,520 tonnes of CO ₂ emissions annually . For FKL Spinning Mills Ltd., this initiative represents a major step towards reducing its environmental footprint, strengthening energy sustainability and embracing cleaner energy alternatives. For Fakir Technologies Ltd., the project further demonstrates its growing capabilities in delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions for the industrial sector. Since 2022, the company has been actively operating in Bangladesh’s solar energy and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) sectors, building its expertise through global technology partnerships, project execution and integrated energy solutions. The project is being undertaken by Fakir Technologies Ltd., with Solar EPC Development Ltd. serving as its EPC partner. This 6.13 MWp project further reinforces Fakir Technologies’ commitment to supporting industries in their transition towards cleaner, more efficient and sustainable energy systems. The agreement signing ceremony was held at Fakir Knitwears Ltd., Narayanganj , in the presence of senior leadership from both organizations. articles.s: When the Factory Stops, Everyone’s Clock Keeps Running Imagine a factory on a November morning. Fabric is ready. Some garments are waiting for their final inspection. A merchandiser opens an email from a buyer: “Can you confirm the shipment date?” Outside, workers are gathering. Inside, management i
articles.x: When the Factory Stops, Everyone’s Clock Keeps Running Imagine a factory on a November morning. Fabric is ready. Some garments are waiting for their final inspection. A merchandiser opens an email from a buyer: “Can you confirm the shipment date?” Outside, workers are gathering. Inside, management is deciding whether production can continue safely. The shipment clock is still running. So is the worker’s rent. So is the factory’s interest bill Figure: Ruhul Talukder, Managing Director, Ruhrose.com That is what makes Bangladesh’s current garment crisis so difficult. People standing on different sides of the factory gate are worried about the same thing: their future. The challenge is finding a way forward that they can trust. Behind the headlines are two kinds of pressure: Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. Their protests also include concerns about blacklisting and the reinstatement of dismissed workers. Reports of road blockades, clashes and attacks on property show how serious the situation has become. For workers, the discussion starts with daily life: food, rent, transport and the cost of supporting a family. For factory owners, it starts with a different calculation: the price agreed with the buyer, the cost of materials, wages, energy and the money left after shipment. Neither calculation disappears because the other side is struggling. A worker cannot pay rent with an explanation about low margins. A factory cannot meet a higher wage bill simply by wishing buyers would pay more. This is where leadership matters. The industry needs a workable agreement that recognises both realities. articles.s: In an exclusive interview at TITAS 2026, Justin Huang, President of the Taiwan Textile Federation (TTF), discusses the material innovations and commercial decisions behind Taiwan’s drive to recover more value… The post Taiwan’s Textile Ambition: Making Responsibility a Competitive Advantage appeared
articles.x: In an exclusive interview at TITAS 2026, Justin Huang, President of the Taiwan Textile Federation (TTF), discusses the material innovations and commercial decisions behind Taiwan’s drive to recover more value from textile waste. By Nithin Kumar A performance fabric earns its reputation through what it does for the wearer. For Justin Huang, its value increasingly extends to what happens after use: whether its materials can be recovered and made useful again. Justin Huang, President of the Taiwan Textile Federation (TTF) Speaking exclusively to The Textile Magazine at the 30th Taipei Innovative Textile Application Show, TITAS 2026, Huang argues that material recovery can strengthen Taiwan’s position with global brands. With relatively high labour and energy costs, he says, Taiwanese suppliers must give international customers compelling reasons to choose them. He points to years of investment in materials and manufacturing processes intended to reduce environmental impact. In his account, taking responsibility for textile waste is becoming part of the value Taiwan offers its customers. Giving textiles another life A central priority is the move beyond PET-bottle recycling towards textile-to-textile recycling. Bringing discarded fabrics and garments back into fibre production would allow the industry to recover more of the materials contained in its own products. The difficulty begins with composition. Garments commonly combine different fibres, complicating the recovery process. Materials must be identified and sorted, while dyes and other unwanted substances may need to be removed. articles.s: FRANKFURT AM MAIN, Germany — November 3, 2026 — Techtextil and Texprocess 2028 bring relevant market players even closer together. The focus is on the interfaces between materials, technology and processing – where innovations, new applications and business contacts emerge. The optimised hall layout
articles.x: FRANKFURT AM MAIN, Germany — November 3, 2026 — Techtextil and Texprocess 2028 bring relevant market players even closer together. The focus is on the interfaces between materials, technology and processing – where innovations, new applications and business contacts emerge. The optimised hall layout supports this networking across the exhibition grounds, with short distances and an efficient route along the various stages of textile production and processing. Companies can register at early-booking rates until the end of November. The first renowned exhibitors have already registered. Techtextil-Texprocess 2026 Photo: Messe Frankfurt / Pietro Sutera Volatile markets, cost pressures and changing supply chains are challenging the global textile industry. At the same time, material innovations and new technologies such as AI are opening up additional applications and business opportunities. Collaboration along the value chain is essential. Techtextil and Texprocess bring together relevant market players in Frankfurt from 4 to 7 April 2028 who are shaping this transformation – from research and technology providers to manufacturers and processors as well as users from a wide range of industries. articles.x: BRIDGWATER, England— November 3, 2026 — Ned Dorbin has been announced as Chief Executive Officer of Nonwovenn and of Technical Materials Group (TMG), as the combined businesses look to accelerate growth, working towards ambitious targets over the next few years. Ned is familiar with Nonwovenn having spent six years as a non-executive director between 2016 and 2022. He has 19 years of experience as a private equity investor, supporting the growth of businesses across a wide range of sectors with funding and strategic board input. Ned Dorbin Nonwovenn and TMG plan to significantly increase their scale over the coming years through a combination of organic growth and acquisitions. As CEO, Ned will be responsible for leading the businesses through this next phase, providing strategic direction and driving commercial performance. His experience of working with management teams, supporting investment decisions and scaling businesses will be central to delivering these ambitions. Former CEO Andrew Brownlow remains an important part of the leadership team, with an increased focus on strategic projects, capital investment programmes and operational development. Ned Dorbin, Chief Executive Officer at Nonwovenn and Technical Materials Group, said: “I’m delighted to be joining Nonwovenn and TMG. articles.x: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman joined the opening ceremony of Bangladesh Solar Expo-2026 in the city this morning as the chief guest. The inaugural ceremony began at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in the capital, said Prime Minister’s Deputy Press Secretary Jahidul Islam Rony. The Power Division and the Infrastructure Development Company Limited (IDCOL) jointly organised the expo for the first time with the theme “Utilise Every Inch of Rooftop, Increase Income through Solar Power”. Chaired by Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood Tuku, it was also joined by State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit, Finance Secretary Dr Md Khairuzzaman Mozumder and Power Division Secretary Mirana Mahrukh. Ministers, state ministers, members of parliament, secretaries and senior government officials from different ministries also attended the programme. articles.o: Extending warp knitting into finer fashion fabrics
articles.s: Karl Mayer has further developed its TM Weft warp knitting machine for fashion and apparel applications, introducing a finer E 36 gauge, greater patterning flexibility and improved yarn tension control. The developments will be demonstrated at ITMA Asia 2026 in Shanghai from November 20-24, alongsid
articles.x: Karl Mayer has further developed its TM Weft warp knitting machine for fashion and apparel applications, introducing a finer E 36 gauge, greater patterning flexibility and improved yarn tension control. The developments will be demonstrated at ITMA Asia 2026 in Shanghai from November 20-24, alongside a new collection of warp knitted fabrics designed to reproduce the appearance of woven textiles while retaining the production and performance advantages of warp knitting. The company’s WovenLike concept combines the appearance and texture of woven fabrics with the flexibility, wrinkle resistance and ease of care associated with warp knitted constructions. It also offers opportunities for more efficient production, particularly when processing challenging materials such as linen, acetate and decorative effect yarns. The latest developments to the TM Weft include an E 36 gauge option for producing finer fabrics and a new EL pattern drive, allowing greater flexibility and speed in pattern development. Yarn tension is now continuously regulated rather than controlled through the previous system, simplifying operation and supporting more consistent fabric quality. The latest developments to the TM Weft include a new EL pattern drive. © Karl Mayer To illustrate the machine’s capabilities, Karl Mayer’s Textile Innovation Center has developed two contrasting fabric ranges for presentation at ITMA Asia. The first comprises dense, textured constructions intended for autumn and winter apparel. These include a crêpe fabric incorporating Lycra T400 for stretch and shape retention, a bouclé construction featuring metallic yarn accents and a floral design produced using a burnout technique to create areas of transparency within an otherwise closed surface. articles.s: 튀르키예 섬유 · 의류산업이 생산비 상승과 수출 경쟁력 약화로 어려움을 겪는 가운데 이집트가 새로운 의류 생산 · 수출 거점으로 부상하고 있다. 특히 유럽연합(EU) 데님시장에서 튀르키예산 제품의 수입이 크게 줄어든 반면 이집트산은 빠르게 증가하면서 양국의 수출 실적이 엇갈리고 있다.튀르키예의 섬유·의류업종 고용인원은 2022년 말부터 올해 7월까지 약 36만명 감소했다. 생산비 부담이 커지고 수출 여건도 악화되면서 의류 제조업을 중심으로 고용 감소가 이어진 것으로 분석된다.이 같은 산업 위축은 주요 수출시장인 EU에서도 확인된다.

articles.x: November 20-24th, China International Textile Machinery Exhibition ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026 will be held at Shanghai National Exhibition Center. CHTC Fong’s will make an appearance at booth C37 in Hall 7, presenting a dual-layer intelligent booth and delivering a brand-new "digital and intelligent dyeing and finishing" business card to the world. CHTC Fong's is inviting the visitors to witness how CHTC Fong’s uses digital twin and AI technology, combined with the entire process of dyeing and finishing equipment, to create a "One-Stop" intelligent dyeing and finishing solutions. Digital Twin + AI, Bringing Dyeing Factories a "Digital Brain" CHTC Fong’s will also showcase its AI Assistant , enabling visitors to explore textile processing knowledge through interactive conversations. The company will demonstrate AI-driven applications, including AI formulation and specialized small models, designed to shorten processing cycles, improve efficiency and reduce energy consumption. At the One-Stop service platform experience zone, visitors will be able to experience remote equipment operation via tablets and smartphones, highlighting the transition from traditional reactive services to proactive, predictive support. The hardcore equipment firmly establishes the foundation Oof "One-Stop" manufacturing In addition to its AI-powered solutions, CHTC Fong’s will present three physical machines and three high-precision models covering the complete dyeing and finishing process, from pre-treatment to finishing. Drawing on more than 60 years of manufacturing expertise, the company aims to showcase the capabilities of its integrated intelligent dyeing and finishing equipment. articles.o: 에스트라, 한국광고학회 ‘올해의 브랜드상’ 수상
articles.s: 아모레퍼시픽의 더마 브랜드 에스트라(AESTURA)가 한국광고학회가 선정한 ‘2026 올해의 브랜드상’을 수상했다. 시상식은 지난 10월 30일 부산 파라다이스호텔에서 열렸다.한국광고학회가 2006년 제정한 ‘올해의 브랜드상’은 마케팅 커뮤니케이션을 통한 고객 만족과 브랜드 자산 구축 등의 성과를 평가해 수여하는 상이다. 올해는 에스트라를 포함한 총 6개 브랜드가 수상 대상으로 선정됐다. 에스트라는 제품을 넘어 소비자의 인식과 경험에 변화를 이끌고, 차별화된 커뮤니케이션으로 브랜드 경쟁력을 높였다는 평가를 받았다.1982년 태평양제

articles.t: VistaPrint는 의류 생산 속도를 3배로 향상시킵니다.
articles.o: VistaPrint triples apparel production speed
articles.s: VistaPrint has increased its digital garment printing capacity by approximately 25,000 units per week following the installation of a Kornit Digital Apollo system, which is delivering production speeds around three times faster than its previous process. The investment is enabling the print and desi
articles.x: VistaPrint has increased its digital garment printing capacity by approximately 25,000 units per week following the installation of a Kornit Digital Apollo system, which is delivering production speeds around three times faster than its previous process. The investment is enabling the print and design company to reduce production turnaround times to approximately a day, while improving operational efficiency and lowering production costs. Serving millions of small and medium-sized businesses across Europe, the United States, Canada and Australia, VistaPrint has expanded well beyond its original business card printing activities to offer a wide range of customised products, including apparel, promotional materials, packaging and signage. The company has worked with Israel-headquartered Kornit Digital since 2007, progressively upgrading its digital garment printing operations through successive generations of technology, including the Kornit Atlas and Atlas MAX systems. The latest investment in Apollo represents a further step towards high-volume, on-demand apparel manufacturing, allowing VistaPrint to respond more quickly to incoming orders while reducing the handling and labour requirements associated with garment production. The installation was supported by online training ahead of commissioning and an on-site Kornit technician during the first six months of operation. VistaPrint reached full utilisation across three production shifts approximately three months after production began. www.kornit.com www.vistaprint.com The post VistaPrint triples apparel production speed appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

articles.o: Picanol enters basic fabrics market
articles.s: Picanol will introduce a new generation of airjet weaving machines at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026 in Shanghai from November 20–24th, extending its portfolio into the market for basic woven fabrics. The new AirOne loom has been developed specifically for this segment and features a newly designed crank sh
articles.x: Picanol will introduce a new generation of airjet weaving machines at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026 in Shanghai from November 20–24th, extending its portfolio into the market for basic woven fabrics. The new AirOne loom has been developed specifically for this segment and features a newly designed crank shedding motion, combining high productivity with low energy consumption, advanced digital capabilities and ease of operation. The launch follows extensive market research, R&D and field testing, and represents an important expansion of Picanol’s airjet weaving portfolio. AirOne will complement the established OmniPlus-i Connect, providing mills producing basic fabrics with an alternative designed around their specific production requirements. The machine incorporates a range of Picanol’s existing innovations and patented technologies, with particular emphasis on operational efficiency, sustainability and simplified machine control. “AirOne represents a special launch for Picanol,” says Johan Verstraete, vice president of weaving machines at Picanol. “This new machine platform brings together all the strengths that define Picanol today, from high performance and low energy consumption to digital capabilities and ease of operation. At the same time, it empowers us to enter a new market segment.” He adds that the company’s sales and service teams are looking forward to making Picanol technology accessible to a broader range of weaving mills. At the Shanghai exhibition, Picanol will demonstrate three machines on its stand F01 in Hall 3. The new AirOne will be producing poplin fabric, alongside an OmniPlus-i Connect weaving ladieswear fabrics and a Supermax rapier weaving machine producing denim. articles.o: Savio to Showcase Smart Winding and Air-Jet Spinning Innovations at ITMA ASIA Shanghai 2026
articles.s: AI-powered automation, digital integration and flexible spinning technology to take center stage October 2026, Italy: Savio will showcase its latest advancements in winding and spinning technology at ITMA ASIA Shanghai 2026, highlighting the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI), automation a
articles.x: AI-powered automation, digital integration and flexible spinning technology to take center stage October 2026, Italy: Savio will showcase its latest advancements in winding and spinning technology at ITMA ASIA Shanghai 2026, highlighting the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI), automation and digital integration in textile manufacturing. The company will focus on two flagship machines: Proxima Smartconer®, its next-generation winding platform, and Lybra Smartspinner®, a versatile air-jet spinning solution. The innovations are designed to help textile manufacturers improve productivity, optimize energy consumption, enhance yarn quality and reduce processing costs while supporting more flexible and data-driven production. Proxima Smartconer®: Intelligent Winding for Higher Performance Savio’s Proxima Smartconer® is available in a comprehensive range of configurations, including fully automatic, manual feeding, cone-to-cone, Duo Lot and large bobbin feeding for the carded wool sector. The platform combines energy-saving technologies, optimized bobbin flow and AI-powered functions with Savio Insight, a web-based system for real-time production monitoring and control. Savio Insight enables remote machine setup, data tracking and performance analysis, helping manufacturers make informed decisions and improve winding process management. Another key innovation is a newly designed and patented suction nozzle in the preparation area. The component improves yarn-end capture efficiency while reducing energy consumption, contributing to lower operating costs without compromising reliability and quality. articles.o: MarediModa Cannes signals renewed confidence
articles.s: The 24th edition of MarediModa Cannes closed on an encouraging note, with renewed confidence among European textile manufacturers and international buyers, alongside the introduction of new creative formats and trend directions for Spring/Summer 2028. Held from 27-29 October 2026 at the Palais des F
articles.x: The 24th edition of MarediModa Cannes closed on an encouraging note, with renewed confidence among European textile manufacturers and international buyers, alongside the introduction of new creative formats and trend directions for Spring/Summer 2028. Held from 27-29 October 2026 at the Palais des Festivals in Cannes, the exhibition brought together leading European manufacturers of fabrics and accessories for beachwear, underwear and athleisure. More than 100 collections for Summer 2028 were presented, offering buyers an overview of developments in textile design, material innovation and performance. Despite continuing geopolitical and economic uncertainty, MarediModa reported results in line with the previous year, with no decline in overall activity. Organisers highlighted a more focused approach among visiting buyers, with greater attention to collection development, material selection and planning for future seasons. Claudio Taiana, President of MarediModa, said the results suggested a gradual return to confidence following a period of stagnation. “We had expected this edition to mark an acceleration after a period of stagnation linked to the international geopolitical situation. The figures are consistent with a return to programming and planning, reflected in more considered choices, closer examination of collections and a positive, vibrant atmosphere,” he said. Taiana also emphasised the exhibition’s role in promoting European textile manufacturing, particularly its combination of technical expertise, product quality and creative development. © MarediModa A significant addition to this year’s event was the inaugural Cannes Fashion Show, a new presentation format designed to demonstrate the creative and technological potential of fabrics through finished garments

articles.s: Bangladesh RMG Industry: Navigating Challenges and Securing Future Growth Bangladesh’s Ready-Made Garment (RMG) industry stands at a pivotal moment. Escalating production costs, energy supply constraints, downward pricing pressure, global trade uncertainty, and the forthcoming graduation from Least
articles.x: Bangladesh RMG Industry: Navigating Challenges and Securing Future Growth Bangladesh’s Ready-Made Garment (RMG) industry stands at a pivotal moment. Escalating production costs, energy supply constraints, downward pricing pressure, global trade uncertainty, and the forthcoming graduation from Least Developed Country (LDC) status are collectively challenging the sector’s long-term competitiveness. Black,blue, grey and white t-shirts on hangers on gray background The path forward is not simply about producing larger volumes at lower prices. Sustained growth will require a strategic shift toward operational efficiency, productivity improvement, value-added products, stronger backward integration, and deeper collaboration between manufacturers and global retailers. The Role of International Buyers Building a resilient and sustainable apparel supply chain is a shared responsibility. To support long-term industry growth, international buyers should: • Provide greater visibility through reliable order forecasts and capacity commitments. • Avoid excessive price pressures that compromise sustainable manufacturing practices. • Participate in funding significant product, technology, and sustainability innovations where appropriate. • Engage suppliers earlier in product development, sourcing, and planning processes. • Recognize and reward measurable improvements in quality, productivity, compliance, and environmental performance. Stronger buyer-supplier partnerships will enhance both commercial outcomes and supply chain resilience. articles.s: Groz-Beckert will present a broad portfolio of textile machinery components, precision tools and digital services at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026, taking place from 20-24 November in Shanghai, China. The German manufacturer will showcase innovations across knitting, weaving, nonwovens, sewing, tufting and
articles.x: Groz-Beckert will present a broad portfolio of textile machinery components, precision tools and digital services at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026, taking place from 20-24 November in Shanghai, China. The German manufacturer will showcase innovations across knitting, weaving, nonwovens, sewing, tufting and spinning in Hall 4.1, Booth D41. Energy efficiency, process reliability and solutions for increasingly demanding textile applications will be central themes, with developments targeting technical textiles, medical products, fine-gauge fabrics and high-performance industrial materials. The new SAN FY is engineered for processing uneven effect yarns and ensures flawless fabric appearance, even with demanding materials and intricate designs. In cooperation with SINOTEX, Groz-Beckert demonstrates the production possibilities offered by its fine-gauge technology with a jointly presented knitted collar. Equipped with the spring-loaded latch needle Vosa Spec. 89.50-45 G016, the application showcases the production of finer fabrics and tighter stitch loops, making it ideal for high-quality collars and sweater components. The Legwear product group presents its exceptionally durable dur needles for use in sock and fine hosiery machines, where the highest levels of precision and load resistance are required. In the Warp Knitting segment, Groz-Beckert presents the patented compound needle Spec. 51/43.36 G 101 for fine-gauge elastic fabrics. The reinforced plastic part provides enhanced stability, while minimal tolerances support the production of uniform, high-quality fabrics with excellent knitting performance. articles.t: Dow의 불소 대체 마감재
articles.o: Fluoro-alternative finish from Dow
articles.s: Dow has launched a new silicone-organic hybrid textile finishing technology designed to provide durable water repellency alongside resistance to oil-based contaminants, without relying on conventional fluorinated chemistry. The new Dowsil IE-5619 DWOR Emulsion has been developed to help textile manu
articles.x: Dow has launched a new silicone-organic hybrid textile finishing technology designed to provide durable water repellency alongside resistance to oil-based contaminants, without relying on conventional fluorinated chemistry. The new Dowsil IE-5619 DWOR Emulsion has been developed to help textile manufacturers and brands respond to increasingly stringent restrictions on fluorinated substances, while maintaining the performance, comfort and appearance of finished fabrics. Achieving effective oil repellency has traditionally been one of the major challenges in developing alternatives to fluorinated textile finishes. Dow says its third-generation silicone-organic hybrid technology is designed to address this limitation, offering resistance to both water-based stains and a range of oil-based contaminants. The product is intended for use on natural, synthetic and blended fabrics, although performance must be validated for individual fabric types and finishing formulations. The new emulsion can help protect against contaminants including cooking oils, motor oil and sebum, as well as common water-based stains such as coffee, wine and milk. “For years, achieving meaningful oil repellency in textiles typically required fluorinated chemistries, which are now facing increasing restrictions,” said Juan Carlos Medina, global strategic marketing director at Dow. “Dowsil IE-5619 helps close that gap with a silicone-based, fluoro-alternative solution that delivers durable water and oil repellency while preserving the softness, breathability and aesthetics consumers expect.” The new formulation is a 30% solids concentrate designed for integration into conventional textile finishing processes. articles.t: 두 개의 섬유 강국을 다루다
articles.o: Addressing two textile powerhouses
articles.s: China and India are among the world’s most important textile manufacturing markets and have been key destinations for Swiss textile machinery for decades. Their industrial structures, raw material bases and market dynamics, however, differ considerably. These differences create distinct requirements
articles.x: China and India are among the world’s most important textile manufacturing markets and have been key destinations for Swiss textile machinery for decades. Their industrial structures, raw material bases and market dynamics, however, differ considerably. These differences create distinct requirements and opportunities for Swiss suppliers of machinery, components and services. With ITMA Asia + CITME in Shanghai and India ITME in Greater Noida, two major Asian textile machinery exhibitions will take place towards the end of 2026. “China and India are both key markets for our industry, but their industrial environments differ notably,” explains Cornelia Buchwalder, secretary general of Swiss Textile Machinery. “The structure of textile production, the availability of raw materials and the importance of domestic demand all influence their investment priorities. Understanding these differences is essential for our member companies to offer technologies that meet the specific requirements of each market.” Extensive value chain China is by far the world’s largest textile manufacturing country, with an extensive and highly integrated value chain covering virtually every stage of textile production. It is also the world’s leading exporter of textiles and apparel, while its substantial domestic market generates significant additional demand. Its position in man-made fibres is particularly strong, with chemical fibre production reaching approximately 87 million tons in 2025. At the same time, China remains a major cotton producer and processor. Exports continue to play a central role in the Chinese textile industry. articles.o: Fulgar advances bio-based fibre debate
articles.s: Italian yarn manufacturer Fulgar has highlighted the potential of bio-based synthetic fibres to reduce the textile industry’s dependence on fossil resources, while emphasising the need for greater transparency, reliable certification and competitive pricing to support their wider adoption. articles.x: Italian yarn manufacturer Fulgar has highlighted the potential of bio-based synthetic fibres to reduce the textile industry’s dependence on fossil resources, while emphasising the need for greater transparency, reliable certification and competitive pricing to support their wider adoption. The company contributed to an international discussion on the future of biosynthetics at the recent Performance Days exhibition in Munich, Germany, where Daniela Antunes, Fulgar’s Marketing Manager, joined industry experts to examine the opportunities and challenges associated with renewable raw materials. The panel discussion, entitled From Fossil to Vegetal: The Promises and Challenges of Biosynthetics , brought together representatives from Fulgar, Indorama Ventures, ISCC PLUS and Noosa. Moderated by Sophie Bramel, Technical Editor at Sportstextiles, the session explored the technical, environmental and commercial considerations influencing the development and adoption of biopolymers in textile applications. Central to Fulgar’s contribution was its ongoing research into next-generation polyamide yarns, particularly EVO and Q-GEO, two developments designed to combine renewable raw materials with the performance characteristics required by contemporary textile markets. EVO is a 100% bio-based yarn developed and manufactured by Fulgar using renewable feedstocks derived equally from castor oil and industrial corn. The castor oil originates from crops cultivated in arid regions that do not compete with food production, while the corn component comes from industrial crops not intended for human consumption. articles.o: Autoneum to acquire Trèves Group in €64 million deal
articles.s: Swiss automotive supplier Autoneum is to acquire the French Trèves Group in a deal that will significantly expand its global manufacturing operations and strengthen its position in automotive acoustic and thermal insulation, interior trim and luggage compartment solutions. The acquisition will bring
articles.x: Swiss automotive supplier Autoneum is to acquire the French Trèves Group in a deal that will significantly expand its global manufacturing operations and strengthen its position in automotive acoustic and thermal insulation, interior trim and luggage compartment solutions. The acquisition will bring together two established suppliers to the international automotive industry, creating a business with combined annual revenues expected to exceed CHF 2.9 billion (€3.1 billion) in 2026. Trèves, which generated revenues of approximately €720 million in 2025, employs around 4,600 people across 26 production facilities in 15 countries in Europe, North and South America, Asia and Africa. The company has longstanding relationships with major automotive manufacturers and specialises in acoustic and thermal management systems and interior components. Under the agreement announced on November 2nd, Autoneum will pay approximately €40 million upfront, with a further performance-related payment of up to €24 million possible depending on improvements in profitability and the achievement of synergies by 2029. More than 80% of the initial consideration will be settled through newly issued Autoneum shares, with approximately €7.5 million paid in cash. The shares will be subject to a three-year lock-up period. The transaction is expected to be completed in early 2027, subject to consultation with the relevant employee representative bodies and customary regulatory approvals. The planned takeover follows Autoneum’s €117 million acquisition of the automotive business of Germany’s Borgers Group in April 2023. articles.s: Heimtextil 2027 will introduce the Functional Futures Lab, a showcase of innovative materials for architecture, interior design and hospitality. The exhibition will feature experimental prototypes and...
articles.x: Heimtextil 2027 will introduce the Functional Futures Lab, a showcase of innovative materials for architecture, interior design and hospitality. The exhibition will feature experimental prototypes and commercially available solutions with applications in temperature regulation, acoustic comfort, flame protection and healthier indoor environments. Figure: Heimtextil 2027 to feature bio-based composites and next-generation textiles The Functional Futures Lab will explore material innovation through three themes: Circular Systems, Living Nature and Natural Performance. These themes will examine material origins, processing methods, durability, and functional properties. Featured innovations will include upholstery materials made from untreated wool fibers, living root systems designed to provide flame protection without toxic chemicals, durable bio-based composites, and dyes derived from food waste for textiles and wood. These materials highlight opportunities to develop alternatives to conventional raw materials and improve the functional performance of interior products. Their commercial potential will depend on production costs, scalability, durability, and compliance with relevant safety requirements. The showcase will present both early-stage research and market-ready solutions. Information on each material's development stage, including Technology Readiness Levels, will help visitors assess its readiness for practical applications. This approach will help textile manufacturers, designers, architects and hospitality professionals evaluate materials for residential and commercial projects. articles.s: German circular knitting machinery manufacturer Terrot Textilmaschinen will highlight its UCC 672-ME double-electronic jacquard machine at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026 in Shanghai, China, from 20-24 November, demonstrating its capabilities for premium mattress ticking, upholstery and technical textiles. articles.x: German circular knitting machinery manufacturer Terrot Textilmaschinen will highlight its UCC 672-ME double-electronic jacquard machine at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026 in Shanghai, China, from 20-24 November, demonstrating its capabilities for premium mattress ticking, upholstery and technical textiles. The Chemnitz-based company, part of the Santoni China Group, will present a 38-inch diameter, E20 gauge machine equipped with 88 feeders at stand H4.1 C39. The exhibition configuration will feature a specialised mattress fabric incorporating cooling yarns, differentiated comfort zones and knitted structures designed to promote ventilation on both surfaces. UCC 672-ME The UCC 672-ME features independently programmable three-way needle selection on both cylinder and dial, allowing manufacturers to control knit, tuck and miss actions at every feeder. This enables intricate jacquard patterns, three-dimensional textures, ventilation zones and reversible structures without the limitations of conventional mechanical patterning systems. Terrot UCC 672-ME knitting head. © Terrot Textilmaschinen GmbH For mattress applications, the technology allows different surface characteristics to be incorporated into a single fabric, combining supportive constructions with comfort-oriented designs. Actual cooling and breathability properties depend on yarn selection, fabric engineering and finishing. The machine also supports upholstery textiles, spacer fabrics, footwear uppers and selected outerwear applications. Available in diameters from 34 to 42 inches, the UCC 672-ME offers configurations with 88 feeders at 38 inches and 100 feeders at 42 inches. articles.o: ITET Bangladesh urges government action to restore stability in textile and RMG industry
articles.s: The Institution of Textile Engineers and Technologists (ITET) Bangladesh has called for urgent government action to restore stability and strengthen industrial security amid rising labour unrest in th...
articles.x: The Institution of Textile Engineers and Technologists (ITET) Bangladesh has called for urgent government action to restore stability and strengthen industrial security amid rising labour unrest in the textile and RMG sector. The organization stressed the need for uninterrupted production to safeguard Bangladesh’s key export industry and maintain investor confidence. In a statement, ITET Bangladesh expressed deep concern over recent incidents of arson, vandalism, labour unrest, protests and road blockades in different industrial areas, saying these incidents have severely disrupted normal factory operations and production. The organization noted that many factories have already shut down, raising concerns over the country's economy, employment and export trade. According to ITET Bangladesh, the industry was attempting to recover from prolonged gas crises and other challenges when the fresh wave of instability created further uncertainty about its future. It also warned that continued unrest could undermine the confidence of international buyers and investors and damage Bangladesh's image in the global market. Emphasizing the importance of protecting workers' legitimate rights and demands, ITET Bangladesh said factory security, a stable production environment and the rule of law must also be ensured. The organization called for resolving the underlying causes of labour unrest through dialogue between workers and factory owners. It also urged the authorities to conduct impartial investigations to identify those involved in arson, vandalism, looting and sabotage and bring them to justice. articles.s: 현대백화점이 현대아울렛 동대문점 개점 10주년을 맞아 식품관을 전면 개편했다. 외국인 관광객 비중이 높은 상권 특성을 반영해 국내외 F&B 브랜드를 구성하고, 연말까지 추가 입점을 통해 식음 콘텐츠를 확대할 계획이다.현대백화점은 4개월간의 리뉴얼을 거쳐 현대아울렛 동대문점 지하 2층 식품관을 ‘쿡스동대문(COOKS DONGDAEMUN)’으로 새롭게 열었다고 지난달 30일 밝혔다.쿡스동대문은 ‘한국의 골목시장’을 콘셉트로 조성했다. 골목길을 연상시키는 좁은 동선과 불규칙하고 입체적인 매장 배치가 특징이다.입점 브랜드는 총 26개다.

articles.x: The Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX) hosted ‘Texverse 2.0’, an inter-university textile innovation and research competition, on October 30. Organized by the BUTEX Science Club, the day-long event brought together students from more than 25 public and private universities and textile colleges across Bangladesh. The event began at 8:00 am and featured eight competition categories: Maths Olympiad, Treasure Hunt, Quizard, Poster Presentation, Case Competition, AI Video Making, Article Writing and Project Exhibition. Students participated to showcase their knowledge, creativity, research capabilities and innovative ideas. A major highlight of the event was the official launch of KINKLE 2.0 , the club's second annual magazine. Professor Dr. Engr. Md. Zulhash Uddin, Vice-Chancellor of BUTEX, inaugurated the publication. The magazine aims to provide a platform for scientific thinking, research-based writing, innovative ideas and students' creative work. At the closing ceremony, Professor Dr. Engr. Md. Zulhash Uddin attended as the chief guest, while Engineer Md. Sayedur Rahman Sayed, Vice Chairman of the Textile Engineering Division of the Institution of Engineers, Bangladesh (IEB), was present as the special guest. Other guests included Professor Dr. Md. Ahashan Habib, Dean of the Faculty of Textile Management and Business Studies, BUTEX; Professor Dr. Kaniz Farhana, Head of the Department of Apparel Engineering, BUTEX; Professor Dr. Md. articles.o: UGC to prioritize industry-oriented research funding, announced at the 7th BUFT-CRISAT Textile Research Conference
articles.s: The University Grants Commission (UGC) of Bangladesh plans to increase dedicated research funding for collaborative projects involving universities and industries, with a focus on practical solutions...
articles.x: The University Grants Commission (UGC) of Bangladesh plans to increase dedicated research funding for collaborative projects involving universities and industries, with a focus on practical solutions to manufacturing challenges, patent development, and commercialisation. Prof. Dr. Mamun Ahmed, Chairman of UGC, announced the initiative while addressing the 7th BUFT–CRISAT Textile Research Conference (TRC) 2026, held on October 31 at the auditorium hall of BGMEA University of Fashion and Technology (BUFT) in Nishatnagar, Turag, Dhaka. The conference brought together local and international academics, researchers, industry leaders and professionals to explore research-driven approaches to sustainability, technological advancement and industrial competitiveness in the textile and apparel sector. Addressing the conference as Chief Guest, Prof. Dr. Mamun Ahmed emphasised the need to connect academic research with real manufacturing challenges, arguing that the country's textile and apparel industry must move beyond its traditional manufacturing strengths through research, technology adoption and higher-value production. He noted that international buyers are increasingly evaluating manufacturers based on environmental performance, supply chain circularity and their ability to adopt automation and digital technologies, alongside production costs. We must rely on research, and that is applied research, engaging industry and academia," he said. articles.o: Danish garment firm Spectre opens $30mn green factory in northern Vietnam
articles.s: Danish garment maker Spectre has inaugurated a new green factory in Hung Yen Province, northern Vietnam, expanding its manufacturing footprint in the country while helping reduce greenhouse gas emissions through energy-efficient production, according to the Danish Embassy in Vietnam. The new facilit
articles.x: Danish garment maker Spectre has inaugurated a new green factory in Hung Yen Province, northern Vietnam, expanding its manufacturing footprint in the country while helping reduce greenhouse gas emissions through energy-efficient production, according to the Danish Embassy in Vietnam. The new facility, Spectre Hung Yen 2, opened at Song Tra Industrial Park in Thai Binh Ward on Friday, marking the company’s fourth factory in Vietnam and second in Hung Yen. With nearly 80 years of experience in the garment industry, Spectre specializes in producing functional apparel for premium sportswear and outdoor brands. Backed by an investment of US$30 million, the new factory is expected to cut carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 1,600 metric tons annually compared with conventional factories of a similar size. It has received LEED Gold certification, the third-highest certification level under the Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) rating system developed by the U.S. Green Building Council. The facility combines solar power with modern design solutions to improve energy efficiency and reduce its environmental footprint. It is also equipped with advanced machinery and technologies, including automation and artificial intelligence (AI) solutions, to improve production efficiency and establish higher standards across Spectre’s manufacturing operations. The factory is expected to create jobs for around 3,000 local workers. Jesper Klausen, Spectre’s co-owner and chief business development officer, said the company, was proud of its latest investment in Hung Yen. articles.o: Chloris advances bio-based dye for commercial denim production
articles.s: Utah-based biotechnology company Chloris Colors is working to scale its bio-based dye, Claessen Blue, across commercial denim production. It is using third-party certifications to support adoption by...
articles.x: Utah-based biotechnology company Chloris Colors is working to scale its bio-based dye, Claessen Blue, across commercial denim production. It is using third-party certifications to support adoption by textile mills and global brands. Figure: Claessen Blue has received ISCC PLUS certification, making it the first bio-based dye globally to achieve it. The dye is designed to run on existing indigo dyeing lines and deliver denim aesthetics similar to conventional indigo. It offers an alternative to synthetic indigo through a milder dyeing process that avoids harsh reducing agents such as sodium hydrosulfite. The company says the process also uses lower alkalinity and can reduce water and energy demand while producing cleaner wastewater. These features could help denim manufacturers reduce the environmental impact of conventional indigo dyeing. Claessen Blue has received ISCC PLUS certification, making it the first bio-based dye globally to achieve it. ISCC PLUS verifies the use of bio-based, bio-circular and recycled feedstocks through independent auditing and a mass balance chain-of-custody system. The dye has also received USDA BioPreferred and TÜV Austria OK biobased certifications, which verify its bio-based carbon content. articles.s: Building on the decade-long success of the Textile Research Conference (TRC), first introduced by CRISAT (Centre of Research & Innovation in Science, Arts & Technology) in 2014, the 7th Textile Research Conference (TRC) 2026 successfully brought together researchers, academics, industry leaders, pol
articles.x: Building on the decade-long success of the Textile Research Conference (TRC), first introduced by CRISAT (Centre of Research & Innovation in Science, Arts & Technology) in 2014, the 7 th Textile Research Conference (TRC) 2026 successfully brought together researchers, academics, industry leaders, policymakers and students from Bangladesh and abroad at BGMEA University of Fashion & Technology (BUFT), Dhaka, creating a vibrant platform for knowledge exchange and collaboration on the future of the textile and apparel sector. Jointly organised by CRISAT and BUFT, the conference showcased pioneering research and innovative solutions addressing some of the industry’s most pressing challenges, including sustainability, circularity, digital transformation, advanced manufacturing, smart textiles and renewable energy. The conference featured more than 20 research presentations across parallel technical sessions. Researchers presented findings on topics ranging from biodegradable dyes, bio-based textile composites and intelligent textile sensors to artificial intelligence applications, textile waste forecasting models, sustainable packaging solutions and renewable energy adoption within textile manufacturing. A major highlight of the conference was the keynote address delivered by Professor Engr. Dr. Hafsa Jamshaid of National Textile University (NTU), Pakistan, entitled “Beyond Recycling: Transforming Textile Waste into High-Value Technical Textiles and Advanced Materials.” The presentation explored innovative pathways for textile waste valorisation and circular material development. articles.t: 에이피알, 매출 두 배 뛰었지만 수익성은 뒷걸음
articles.o: 에이피알, 매출 두 배 뛰었지만 수익성은 뒷걸음
articles.s: 에이피알의 고속성장에 수익성이라는 변수가 부상했다. 3분기 매출이 전년 동기 대비 두 배로 뛰었지만, 영업이익 증가율은 이에 미치지 못했다. 영업이익률은 전년 동기와 직전 분기 대비 모두 하락했다. 미국 대형 유통망을 빠르게 확대하며 외형 성장에는 성공했지만, 매출 증가가 그만큼의 이익으로 연결되지 못하면서 성장의 질에 대한 점검이 필요해졌다.30일 에이피알이 공시한 연결 기준 잠정 실적에 따르면 3분기 매출은 7731억1500만원으로 전년 동기 대비 100.3% 증가했다. 영업이익은 1606억4000만원으로 68.9% 늘었다. 그

articles.o: “수자원관리가 생명줄”…섬유패션 생산국들 ‘물 보전’ 나서
articles.s: 물 부족과 수질오염이 섬유패션업계 생산비용과 공급망 안정성을 위협하고 있다. 기후변화에 따른 가뭄과 홍수, 지하수 고갈에 산업용수 수요 증가까지 겹치면서 주요 섬유 생산국의 물 관련 위험이 확대되고 있기 때문이다. 특히 원면 재배와 염색·가공에 집중됐던 수자원 관리가 개별 공장의 절수 활동을 넘어 산업단지와 하천 유역 전체를 관리하는 방식으로 전환되고 있다.물 사용량 늘고 수자원 불균형 심화유엔환경계획(UNEP)에 따르면 세계 섬유산업의공장별 절수에서 유역 공동관리로 섬유패션공급망의 물 보전 전략이 전환하고 있다. 사진=AI생성이미

articles.o: UN Approves 3-Year Extension for Bangladesh LDC Graduation Until 2029
articles.s: The United Nations General Assembly has formally adopted a resolution deferring Bangladesh’s graduation from the Least Developed Countries (LDC) category by three years with setting the new transition deadline for November 24, 2029. The resolution, introduced by Uruguay on behalf of the Group of 77
articles.x: The United Nations General Assembly has formally adopted a resolution deferring Bangladesh’s graduation from the Least Developed Countries (LDC) category by three years with setting the new transition deadline for November 24, 2029. The resolution, introduced by Uruguay on behalf of the Group of 77 and China was adopted by voice vote at a plenary meeting in New York. Nepal was granted a similar three-year extension. The session was chaired by the President of the 81st UN General Assembly, Bangladesh Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman. The decision follows a formal request submitted by the BNP-led government shortly after taking office in February, followed by a direct appeal from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to the UN Secretary-General in April. The government and domestic business communities sought extra time to address macroeconomic challenges, political transitions and global supply chain disruptions while preparing for the loss of duty-free and quota-free market access. Delegates from France, Canada and Ireland (speaking on behalf of the European Union) supported the deferral while emphasizing the necessity for structural economic reforms. While on the LDC list since 1975, Bangladesh initially met graduation criteria in 2018 and 2021. The transition date was previously delayed to 2026 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. With this latest extension, Bangladesh retains crucial international trade preferences and tariff exemptions through November 2029. Experts Stress Need for Structural Reforms Economists welcomed the extension but cautioned against complacency.
